News.title: Woman accuses Russell Brand of raping her when she was a 16-year-old school girl
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A woman has revealed her identity to publicly claim she was raped by Russell Brand as a 16-year-old girl.

Mia Latter, now 37, alleged she had been mistreated by the jailed comedian when she was a schoolgirl and he was aged 30.

The allegation was reported to the Metropolitan Police, and while Ms Latter has said in an interview she has decided not to continue with the criminal process, the force has said the investigation into the alleged rape remains ongoing.

Ms Latter was referred to under the pseudonym of Alice in previous reporting by the Sunday Times, The Times, and Channel 4 Dispatches documentary.

Speaking to the Sunday Times, Ms Latter waived her right to lifelong anonymity to campaign for a change in law that she hopes will protect teenagers from grooming.

open image in gallery Court artist drawing of Russell Brand in the dock at Southwark Crown Court ( PA Wire )

She is calling for the introduction of a staggered age of consent, which would make relationships between adults and teens aged 16 and 17 illegal.

She was 16 years old when she first met Brand in Leicester Square, central London, while she was on her way home from a shopping trip.

He took her number, later messaged her, and asked if she wanted to go for dinner.

She told the newspaper that Brand – who was working at MTV at the time – still asked her to meet after she had confessed her age to him.

Ms Latter said Brand told her to keep their relationship secret from her school friends, but his entourage knew, with the convicted rapist referring to her as “the child” in front of them.

Ms Latter alleges Brand orally raped her towards the end of their three-month relationship.

According to the newspaper, Ms Latter spoke to the police after the documentary, but the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decided not to include her case Brand’s trial at Southwark Crown Court.

She said: “They [the police] wanted me to be part of a subsequent trial, but they said that the decision was made [not to include her in the first trial] after he had done the Megyn Kelly and the Piers Morgan interviews… I was told that I wasn’t actually going to make it to the October trial because… they didn’t want it to become ‘the Alice show’, which was my pseudonym in the article. I was devastated by it.”

In an interview with conservative podcaster Megyn Kelly earlier this year, Brand had said that the age of consent in the UK is 16, and he did sleep with a 16-year-old when he was 30.

He described himself as being an “immature 30-year-old” and said that consensual sex when there is a power imbalance – such as being famous – “involves exploitation”.

Ms Latter told the newspaper: “He was a very successful man who had a lot of power and sway in the industry. Whereas I was a 16-year-old with no life experience, no sexual experience and no prior relationships. What was my level of maturity meant to be?”

Brand also addressed the comment he had made on Kelly’s show during an interview on Piers Morgan Uncensored.

open image in gallery Russell Brand leaves Southwark Crown Court ( PA Wire )

Ms Latter said she is happy the police were able to get justice for some of the women involved in the case.

She said that a “lot of incredible police work has gone into this”, but said she feels as if the process is “criminalising”.

Ms Latter decided not to continue with the criminal process so she can focus on her campaign.

She told the newspaper: “I just don’t know what capacity I have to give years more of my life to this, for my head to be occupied with these awful crimes.

“And it takes a toll on your personal life, on your marriage. I feel as though I haven’t been the world’s greatest mum at times, because I’ve been so upset, and I haven’t been the greatest daughter [or] sister.”

On her campaign, she told the paper: “It’s shocking to me time and time again that whenever the news comes up again about him, it’s always in the comments about the relationship with a 16-year-old.

“That’s not the most heinous bit. But why is that the thing that everybody collectively gets stuck on? I think we all sort of agree that … adults shouldn’t be allowed to have sexual relationships with children, with somebody under the age of 18. That really doesn’t seem like a gigantic leap to take.”

Brand was convicted of attacks against four of the six women who gave evidence against him, and he is now serving a 10-and-a-half-year prison term for one count of rape and three sexual assaults.

A Met Police spokesperson said: “Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.

“Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.

“This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence.”

The CPS has been approached for comment.

News.title: Panamanian authorities investigate bombing attack on investigative reporter's home
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A bombing attack Saturday on the home of an investigative reporter in Panama was being investigated by authorities, the newspaper “La Prensa” reported.

No one was injured in the attack targeting journalist Rolando Rodríguez, according to “La Prensa,” which publishes his work.

The Attorney General’s Office of Panama said authorities were investigating a possible case of arson but said the probe may be expanded if other crimes are uncovered.

“While this was an attack on my life and the lives of my family, I must say that it changes the rules of the game in Panama,” Rodríguez told reporters Saturday. “Because now, we are all potentially exposed to this kind of thing.”

Rodríguez is a veteran investigative journalist and columnist who has led or contributed to numerous investigations into alleged corruption and irregularities within Panama’s public sector, the judiciary and businesses.

“La Prensa” reported that the attack at Rodríguez's home came at a time when he was preparing to publish a piece implicating former officials from the administration of President José Raúl Mulino and a government contractor.

The newspaper reported that an individual arrived at Rodríguez’s home by taxi around 2:30 a.m., got out of the vehicle and threw an object toward the residence, triggering an explosion. The journalist’s wife managed to escape the house unharmed and Rodríguez was not in Panama City at the time. The newspaper said there was property damage.

Mulino took to social media to condemn the act, stating that the National Police in coordination with the Public Prosecutor’s Office were investigating the incident and gathering evidence. Mulino said Panama does not tolerate such acts under any circumstances and noted that he had reached out to Rodríguez to express his solidarity.

National and international journalists also condemned the attack. The National College of Journalists called for a rigorous and transparent investigation to identify those responsible.

“What happened in the early hours of the morning — which you have learned about throughout the day — is a matter that concerns the entire country,” said Jorge Molina, president of Corporación La Prensa. “This goes beyond the press; it is an act of terrorism. That is a harsh term, especially given Panama’s history.”

News.title: The war in Sudan ought to be on the conscience of the world
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

The people of Sudan need witnesses to their suffering. That is why we believe it to be so important that Bel Trew, our chief international correspondent, is reporting from the heart of the conflict, recounting the testimony of a grandmother whose son and extended family were dragged out, lined up and shot by paramilitaries.

The civil war there is complicated. It is essentially a power-struggle between two military leaders, but it has escalated into ethnic sectarianism between Arab and non-Arab populations.

This is the same kind of violence between ethnic groups that created the humanitarian catastrophe in Darfur 20 years ago, in which 200,000 people were killed and 2 million displaced. The world paid attention then, and vowed that it would not be allowed to happen again.

But it is happening again. The conflict erupted in Khartoum, the capital, three years ago and has now spread to many parts of the country. Both Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, the leader of the Sudanese army and nominal leader of Sudan, and Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, the leader of the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), seem determined to prevail over each other. Both sides have committed war crimes.

The suffering in the country is the greatest crisis of displacement and hunger in the world right now, and too much of the world is looking away.

We will not do that. That is why our reporter has filed her dispatch from among the “100,000 displaced people who have limped into El Obeid in south-central Sudan after long marches along roads lined with corpses”. That is why we have sought to report, analyse and explain the conflict.

It is why we urge world leaders to step up humanitarian relief efforts. As we report from El Obeid, the conditions in the makeshift camps of displaced people are terrible and little aid is getting through.

“Twenty million people are acutely food insecure. Some 14 million people have been displaced, and there are still pockets of famine,” Carl Skau, the then acting head of the World Food Programme, tells The Independent. “And we’re struggling to meet these needs. We’re doing our best. There is access to many parts, but the funding is not there.”

Important as temporary aid is, however, what really matters is bringing pressure to bear on the leaders of the rival armies. Human Rights Watch and other non-governmental organisations say there is mounting evidence that the RSF is bankrolled by the United Arab Emirates, which the UAE denies, while Saudi Arabia supports the Sudanese army, which the RSF claims is also backed by Egypt and Iran.

If there were more international attention paid to the crisis in Sudan, more pressure would be applied to regional powers to intervene constructively. The UAE government, in particular, is sensitive about its reputation and should be urged to come clean about its role.

Donald Trump said a year ago, “We’re going to start working on Sudan.” The American president who boasted about the number of wars he had ended added another to his to-do list. Instead, he started a new war against Iran, destabilising the world economy and his own party’s prospects in this month’s mid-term elections.

It must fall to the leaders of other nations to do their part to bring an end to this terrible conflict.

News.title: Strictly’s Craig Revel Horwood slams Nikita Kuzmin for ‘taking the mick’ with ‘illegal lifts’ of partner Dani Dyer
News.content:
Strictly Come Dancing’s Craig Revel Horwood slammed professional dancer Nikita Kuzmin for “taking the mick” with “illegal lifts” of his celebrity partner Dani Dyer.

The pair took to the ballroom floor on Saturday (14 November) for a Paso Doble to Everybody Wants to Rule the World.

Following the performance, judge Craig Revel Horwood appeared unimpressed by the choreography, saying it was “littered with illegal lifts.”

He added:” You're taking the mick with four massive lifts in that. One foot should remain on the floor at all times.”

Despite this, he went on to say that the couple did a “fantastic, fantastic job”.

News.title: Botham inspires Wales to historic win over All Blacks
News.content:
The second half of Wales’ Nations Championship started with a hard-fought 28-21 bonus point victory over Japan last Saturday. Steve Tandy’s side sit fifth in the Northern Hemisphere table, but just five points separate them from second-place England, and they still have a tonne of pride to play for as they aim to finish as high as possible in the group.

Speaking ahead of the encounter, Tandy said: “We’re excited for the opportunity we have against New Zealand. It was good to get the win last Saturday, but some elements of our execution weren’t where we wanted.

“We have to go up another level this weekend and be more ruthless. We have one of the best teams in the world coming. We want to be better and put in an 80-minute performance.”

Meanwhile, New Zealand arrive in the Welsh capital in imperious form, having won their opening four Nations Championship matches and boasting a +73 points difference. South Africa’s defeat has opened the door for the resurgent All Blacks to pounce, and they’ll be brimming with confidence following their eye-catching 43-21 triumph against Scotland at Murrayfield a week ago.

As for the team news, Tandy has made four alterations to the starting XV that overcame Japan. Taine Basham is poised for his first international appearance since the 2024 Six Nations, while James Botham, Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Adam Beard also begin the contest. The influential Aaron Wainwright is out with a minor calf problem.

All Blacks Head Coach has ordered 10 changes to the 23-man squad that brushed Scotland aside. Forwards including George Bower, Asafo Aumua, Josh Lord, Anton Segner and backs such as Richie Mo’unga, Anton Lienert-Brown and Fehi Fineanganofo all start for the heavily rotated visitors. Full-back Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time, in his 149th Test, while Will Jordan is unavailable because of a hamstring issue.

Kick-off is at 14:10, with team news following now.

News.title: Joseph a star in the making as England revel in role of bullies
News.content:
England have made wholesale changes, with only five members from the starting XV against Australia remaining. Henry Pollock starts at eight, Will Joseph earns just his second cap on the wing and Archie McParland is set for his international debut off the bench.

“Japan are a very well-coached side who will challenge us in different ways, and we know we will need to bring intensity throughout the game,” said Borthwick. “The atmosphere at Allianz Stadium last week was incredible. The players really fed off the energy in the stadium, and we are really looking forward to being back on Saturday [today].”

Japan’s first game of this month’s fixtures ended in defeat as they lost 28-21 against Wales in Cardiff last weekend. That defeat means they have just one win from their first four games of the Nations Championship, which came against Italy in the opening game, and they sit second bottom in the southern hemisphere standings.

“We have had really good training to prepare us for the game we are expecting against England,” Jones said. “We had two days of very settled and pretty training but Wednesday was quite dirty. We had to adapt to certain situations and in the end we did it really well. I was really pleased with the players, really pleased with their effort, really pleased with the way they adapted to the situations. I am looking forward to going to Twickenham with this young Japanese team that is going to play the house down.”

Kick-off from Allianz Stadium is at 4.40pm.

News.title: France pull off one of their greatest wins as Erasmus mind games backfire
News.content:
Given Les Bleus’ injuries, only the 1999 World Cup semi-final victory over New Zealand can come close to this win over the back-to-back world champions, South Africa. The Nations Championship, with the Springboks previously unbeaten, has been blown wide open. Crikey, given these two could meet in a World Cup semi-final next year, rugby’s blue-riband event in Australia has been blown wide open.

And how lucky are we. France did not score a point in the second half and South Africa’s comeback befitted a champion side, but these audacious hosts regaled their Parisian audience with a rugby feast. Rassie Erasmus, the Springboks’ head coach, said that he was nervous before the game and so he should have been. Fabien Galthié, his counterpart, had promised some fun and games, but Erasmus could not help himself: not long before kick-off, he pulled the coup de théâtre, switching his starting and replacement front rows. Time will tell whether such a move was legal.

“We didn’t play well,” said Erasmus. “I can’t find a lot of excuses. They were on top of their game and we were a little bit off. It was one point here and there. They took their opportunities and we didn’t. We weren’t just outplayed, we were outsmarted.”

“I think we’ve killed our dreams for the Nations Championship with this result,” he added, suggesting he thinks New Zealand will beat England next week.

Demons were present for both sides, mainly France. South Africa lost Jasper Wiese to a 20-minute red card for a nasty ruck clear-out – just as Lood de Jager had received in the visitors’ win last year – and, at the end, there was a reverse of that utterly compelling World Cup quarter-final on the same turf. This time, it was South Africa desperately searching for victory, having dominated the scrum and scoring all three of their tries from close range or mauls.

News.title: England’s batting capitulates in defeat to lift Australia’s spirits
News.content:
“We weren’t quick enough to adapt to the conditions, we talked extensively leading into the game about the surface here at Optus,” Brendon McCullum, England’s coach, said. “It’s a bit like batting on a trampoline, there are certain shots that are very difficult to execute. We talked about trying to put those away.”

McCullum called for his team to scrap a bit more, and at least acknowledged this time that driving on the up was unwise.

“KP has got such a nice manner about him,” he said. “He sees his role to get the talent to perform on the world stage. His message will be measured but firm – adapting to conditions, what could we have done, trying to drive the ball on the up is not wise. Next time we hit a surface like this we have to try and work it better.”

After a quiet start, both openers fell tamely. Ben Duckett prodded Johnson to point, then Banton had a booming drive at Bartlett and was caught behind.

Enter Beardman. When he came on to bowl the 10th over of the innings, there was palpable excitement from his home crowd, who had watched another West Australian, Mike Hussey, present his ODI cap before the toss. Later in the day, Hussey was probably glad he rebuffed England’s recent approach to work with their Test batsmen.

Beardman, who is a mentee of Dennis Lillee and has a gorgeously rhythmical action that helped him touch 90mph, started with a maiden to Root, then found just another movement away from Brook to invite the edge. On the occasion of his 200th ODI, Root had been dropped badly on three off Bartlett, and his only boundary came when Beardman found his an inside edge and the ball flew past his stumps.

The pressure told, and Root edged a big drive behind, where Josh Inglis took the third of his five catches. That sparked a collapse of five for 10, with Jordan Cox edging behind prodding in defence, before Curran was caught on the fence hooking for nought. Beardman’s five-fer was completed when Liam Dawson – selected ahead of Adil Rashid again – skewed a flat-footed drive to backward point. Overton followed in the next over, leaving England 65 for eight, with their lowest ever ODI score, 86, inevitably recorded against Australia in 2001, appearing a distant possibility.

A stand of 37 from Will Jacks and Gus Atkinson averted that particular indignity, and the fear of being bowled out for double figures. But the total was never enough and, despite Atkinson bowling Head first ball, the chase was painfully routine thanks to Marsh’s early barrage.

News.title: Kane bends game to his will on record-breaking night
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of England vs Croatia in the Nations League, with the hosts’ captain Harry Kane set to become the country’s most-capped player.

The 33-year-old has enjoyed a memorable few weeks, becoming the first English Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years and following it up with a new Bayern Munich contract, and an appearance at Wembley tonight will take him clear of Peter Shilton’s record of 125 England caps.

Kane scored twice in his record-equalling appearance against Czech Republic at Wembley last month, extending his international tally to 91 goals – a total that is unrivalled for England.

“It’s not about me – it’s about the team,” Kane said before tonight’s landmark moment. “I love coming to every England camp. I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible.”

The 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic left England on nine points after four Nations League group games, with a 2-0 win in the away contest and a 7-0 thumping of Croatia coming after a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

Thomas Tuchel will be hoping that his side can inflict another heavy defeat on Croatia this evening, but a draw will be enough to book their place in the quarter-finals, with the group’s top two teams progressing.

While Kane will collect plaudits for his 126th cap, attention will also be on a potential first, with Jude Bellingham’s younger brother, Jobe, included in a senior England squad for the first time.

The two Bellinghams appearing together in a senior match would be a new experience for them, while it would be the first time that brothers have taken to the field together for England in 19 years.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said on the Football Association’s England app. “It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great.”

News.title: Experts hail a “milestone” as TB deaths fall by more than a third in 10 years
News.content:
The number of people dying from tuberculosis has dropped by more than a third over the last 10 years but progress against the disease is still too slow, according to the World Health Organization.

Figures from WHO’s annual TB report showed that the lung disease took the lives of an estimated 1.13 million people in 2025, down from 1.7m in 2015, a drop of 35 per cent.

While WHO hailed this as a major milestone in achieving global targets - albeit five years too late - it said that progress in wiping out TB was still too slow.

Africa and Europe have made the greatest progress in reducing deaths, with numbers halving on both continents over the 10-year period. India and China - countries that have high burdens of the disease - also cut deaths by 35 per cent.

The report also showed that an estimated 10.6million people contracted the disease in 2025, a reduction of just 75,000 since 2024.

TB - still the world’s leading infectious disease killer - is preventable and curable, and is caused by the bacillus Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is spread when infected people cough or sneeze.

The disease has been around for centuries, and has been described as the quintessential disease of poverty as it spreads in areas of low quality housing, among people with poor nutrition and immunity. It is a particular risk to people who are HIV positive.

Treatment requires a six-month long regimen of medication, and while treatments have become less toxic in recent years, they still take a heavy toll on patients and have a range of side effects, including at the most extreme deafness. Adherence to medication is also a problem.

News.title: Low-cost parenting app halves rates of sexual violence amongst teenagers in Tanzania
News.content:
A low cost parenting intervention has more than halved rates of sexual violence among teenage girls in Tanzania, a study has shown.

The ParentApp digital parenting programme for families is aimed at reducing rates of violence experienced by teenagers of both sexes.

Researchers found the programme helped bolster family relationships and enabled mothers and fathers to better communicate with their children at what is often a tricky stage of their development.

The programme, led by Oxford University and the University of Cape Town in partnership with the Tanzanian government, the World Health Organization and Unicef, combines in-person and mobile parenting support.

Parents have an introductory session with a facilitator and then undertake 12 weekly sessions online. They also join a WhatsApp group with other parents where they can discuss problems and support one another.

The randomized controlled trial, published in The Lancet, included 2,396 children aged 10–17 and 2,396 parents and carers across 80 urban and rural areas.

Families were randomly assigned to receive either ParentApp or a comparison app focused on safe water and hygiene. Researchers analysing the results did not know which app each family received.

At the 14-month follow-up, girls in families participating in the ParentApp initiative reported a 67% reduction in sexual violence; a 54% reduction in sexual exploitation and an improvement in parent-child relationships. The successes were less marked in boys, however.

Violence against children is widespread globally: Unicef data shows that around one in five girls and women and one in seven boys and men globally have experienced sexual violence as children.

Lucie Cluver, professor of child and family social work at Oxford University and one of the authors of the study, said the intervention was aimed at helping parents and children talk to one another and discuss situations before they arise.

In Tanzania, for example, teenage girls might get a motorbike taxi late at night, potentially putting them in a dangerous situation.

“What you’re doing is making plans and problem solving ahead of these risky situations that teenagers end up in. And you’re building trust and the relationship so you can have these difficult conversations,” said Prof Cluver.

She said she was surprised at how big an impact the intervention had on sexual violence: teenage girls reported that because the app helped improve communication with their parents and carers they did not feel the need to go out as much.

The programme cost around $6 per family but researchers calculated that it goes up to around $10 per family if 20% are given smartphones. A traditional in-person parenting intervention generally costs around $120 per family.

Engagement in the sessions was high - around 70 per cent of participants completed the course - and some parents kept in touch with one another after the programme.

However, the authors of the study stressed that while the app focused on families there remains a need to prevent violence against children in other settings, such as schools and religious institutions. There also needs to be a broader societal push to address the scourge.

“The app isn’t the answer to everything - it’s just one part of the puzzle,” said Prof Cluver.

Prof Cluver said she hoped future versions of the programme would include greater focus on digital harms and test whether parents could take the lead themselves.

The programme is being rolled out in other countries, including Mexico, Panama and South Africa, and is easily adaptable for different contexts.

“Tanzania only has 20% smartphone use and we thought if it works in one of the hardest places to do a digital intervention it could work anywhere,” she said.

She said the study showed how parenting was a universal experience, with the majority focused on what is best for their children.

“Parents feel powerless. We live in a world where our kids are facing risks and parents just want to help,” added Prof Cluver.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: AI fuels fastest economic growth in two years
News.content:
The Prime Minister and the Chancellor should not claim credit for the AI-fuelled expansion of Britain’s economy in the third quarter, a think tank said.

Julian Jessop, economics fellow at the Institute of Economic Affairs, said the 0.7pc expansion in the economy was “a tribute to the resilience of the private sector in the face of the energy shock and policy headwinds”.

He said: “This resilience is despite rather than because of anything the Government has done. In particular, the persistent weakens of the construction sector underlines the failure of flagship policies to boost housebuilding and infrastructure spending.

“The Government’s clumsy interventions are also continuing to add to labour and housing costs, including rents. Instead, the key driver of growth and business optimism has been the rollout of AI. This is an area that the Government has not got round to messing up, though that may yet be coming.

“In the meantime, the Government is still borrowing more than expected and the labour market remains weak.

“The full impact of higher inflation and higher interest rates has also yet to be felt. Early surveys for the fourth quarter already show that consumer confidence, retail spending, private sector hiring and housing market activity are all starting to slide again.

“2026 will still be a year when the economy performed much better than expected – at least in terms of GDP. But the new year will start with further increases in energy bills and high levels of job insecurity, which will matter far more to most people.”

Sports.title: Jones warns England: You were good vs Japan, but All Blacks will be 'violent'
Sports.content:
Former England head coach Eddie Jones praised his old side as "very good" as they tore his Japan apart 78-15 on Saturday, but warned the All Blacks will be "violent" against them next week.

Following South Africa's defeat to France in Paris on Friday, victory for New Zealand against Wales in Cardiff would have seen them claim World Rugby's No 1 ranking, and take charge of the Nations Championship southern hemisphere table.

Instead, the All Blacks suffered their first defeat to Wales since 1953 in a shock 35-28 loss up against an immense Welsh defensive effort, and next play England at Twickenham next Saturday.

"England were impressive against Australia, they beat them quite easily," Jones said at his post-match press conference.

England 78-15 Japan - Score summary England - Tries: Joseph (1,10,20,25,56), Steward (15), Genge (18), Murley (29), Earl (40), Martin (45), Curry (64), Smith (68), Fisilau (73). Cons: Ford (15,19,41), Slade (57,69). Pens: Ford (8). Japan - Tries: Dearns (37), Helu (48). Cons: Saito (38). Pens: Saito (14).

"They played powerfully, they played direct, and when they had the ability to shift the ball, they moved the ball accurately and quickly to space. We saw that again today.

"Well, they're [New Zealand] violent after a defeat.

"They're usually violent, very physical. They'll be massively disappointed with that performance [in Cardiff] today.

"New Zealand next week, they'll be back to the old New Zealand. They'll be hard and tough, and physical around the breakdown.

Image: Will Joseph scored five tries on his first England appearance since 2022 as the hosts destroyed Japan at Twickenham

"I thought England were very good. It kills me that Will Joseph - I gave him his first cap - scores five tries against me! That's not being very loyal, is it?

"He's a great kid, mate. He always was going to be a good player.

"I have to take full responsibility for our [Japan] performance. Clearly we weren't good enough today.

"We thought we had a good preparation for the game, but obviously it wasn't good. Without making any excuses, getting the red card early in the game put us on the back foot, and we really never recovered from that, which good teams are able to do.

"We're not good enough in being able to recover from disappointments. That's clearly the case."

Image: England got over for some 13 tries in victory over Japan, leaving 16 points behind in missed conversions

Borthwick: Joseph took his opportunities well - 'There's thinking to do around selection'

Joseph - who England head coach Steve Borthwick failed to select since taking the role in 2023 until Saturday - was the main topic during the home side's press conference.

While Borthwick wasn't effusive in his praise of the wing, he did admit he now had some extra thinking to do around selection ahead of facing the All Blacks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Steve Borthwick and Eddie Jones were full of praise for Will Joseph after he scored a record-equalling five tries in England's thumping win over Japan in the Nations Championship

"He took those opportunities really, really well," Borthwick said.

"Talking about the point of difference he has in his carry - we wanted the ball in his hands as much as possible, and that's exactly what happened.

"It was off the back of all the players, everybody doing their jobs in the middle of the pitch, and that creates those opportunities on the edges.

"His pace, acceleration and footwork is a real asset. And part of today, as I said before the game, was that we want to build a squad, not a team.

Image: Steve Borthwick wasn't hugely effusive in his praise of Joseph, but admitted there is now thinking to do around team selection

"Now there's some people who really put their hand up with quality performances, and it means that competition for players, the depth in the squad, and the level of experience has taken another step forward.

"There's some thinking to do around selection ahead of next week, and I'm still waiting for the medical report, which hopefully all the players come through pretty well tonight.

"I'll get that full medical report, and then I'll make the call for selection when Test week starts tomorrow night."

What's next?

For England, they next face New Zealand in their third Nations Championship Test of the autumn at Allianz Stadium Twickenham on Saturday, November 21 (2.10pm kick-off).

Sports.title: NFL No 1 pick Mendoza set for 'baptism of fire'
Sports.content:
Fernando Mendoza's time has come, so too has a new era for the Las Vegas Raiders.

The NFL's No 1 overall draft pick will make his first regular-season start this Sunday when he takes the reins at quarterback for Klint Kubiak's side.

Mendoza will lead the Raiders out against the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks following the departure of Kirk Cousins in a deadline day trade back to the Minnesota Vikings.

The Heisman Trophy winner has spent the entire summer and the first half of the season learning behind his veteran mentor. Now the stage is his, against the best defense in football.

"They really have a similar kind of DNA to the Vikings, especially for a rookie. You know exactly what you're going to do against this young man.

"You look at Nick Emmanwori and how as a quarterback you stand back there and have to figure out who's coming, who's not, where, what, who is playing what position.

"And then that defensive line, telling him to keep his eyes up the whole time. This is going to be a lot of hand-holding, I would suggest, for this first game, and definitely a baptism by fire."

It beckons as a reunion for Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, who served as offensive coordinator of the Sam Darnold, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Kenneth Walker-led unit that won the Super Bowl in February.

He helped inspire the best of Darnold amid his career resurrection, and is now tasked with orchestrating a smooth start to the career of a young quarterback.

"Our expectation is for him to lead the offense, to lead the operation, and to go play a game here Sunday and be the leader of the team," said Kubiak

"We have to prepare him and give him a lot of reps to get him comfortable."

Mendoza's only action this season came in October when he made a fourth-quarter cameo in the Raiders' 45-17 defeat to the Patriots, going six of eight for 48 yards.

"This is something that he's worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building," said Raiders general manager John Spytek.

"He passed every test. He put us in a position where we had to make a very hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback."

Sports.title: Joseph scores five tries in England annihilation of Japan
Sports.content:
Nations Championship - England 78-15 Japan: Will Joseph scores five tries in first cap since 2022 as hosts score 13

Will Joseph scored five tries on his first England appearance since 2022 as the hosts destroyed Japan at Twickenham

Will Joseph scored five tries on his first England appearance since 2022 as Steve Borthwick's side destroyed Japan 78-15 in Saturday's Nations Championship.

Joseph (five), Freddie Steward, Ellis Genge, Cadan Murley, Ben Earl, George Martin, Ben Curry, Marcus Smith and Greg Fisilau each scored tries on a day when Japan appeared alarmingly inferior to the hosts, copping a 20-minute red card to lock Harry Hockings after just a minute of play.

Indeed, England's points total would even have been 16 greater had eight conversions not been missed off the kicking tee - George Ford missing six, Henry Slade two.

England 78-15 Japan - Score summary England - Tries: Joseph (1,10,20,25,56), Steward (15), Genge (18), Murley (29), Earl (40), Martin (45), Curry (64), Smith (68), Fisilau (73). Cons: Ford (15,19,41), Slade (57,69). Pens: Ford (8). Japan - Tries: Dearns (37), Helu (48). Cons: Saito (38). Pens: Saito (14).

Japan scored tries through lock Warner Dearns and replacement prop Opeti Helu, but it was a rather sombre return for former England head coach Eddie Jones to Twickenham, with his side falling well short of professional standards.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Story of the match

The Test could hardly have started worse for Japan: Joseph sprinting and powering clear down the right in acres of space to score inside a minute, and the TMO bringing Hockings' high tackle on Genge to the referee's attention before Ford even took the conversion.

Joseph got over England's opener inside 60 seconds of the Test

That left Japan down to 14, and by the sixth minute news came from the bunker Hockings' yellow had been upgraded to a 20-minute red.

Two minutes later, England captain Maro Itoje somewhat bizarrely chose to kick for three points off the kicking tee after a scrum penalty, but Joseph soon had his second, collecting a clever Steward grubber-kick angled towards the corner.

Naoto Saito kicked over a 40-metre penalty for Japan to get onto the board, but England had their third try in the 15th minute: Steward finishing after Martin had bulldozed his way forward.

Freddie Steward scored England's third in the 15th minute as they made Japan pay for an early 20-minute red card

Within moments, Genge stormed over for England's fourth as England cut through at will and he handed off a succession of Japanese defenders, with Joseph completing his hat-trick inside 20 minutes seconds later, flying over in the corner again.

Prop Ellis Genge wrestled his way past and over a succession of Japan defenders to score

The Gloucester wing continued to show off his pace and power, bamboozling Japan to score his fourth in the 24th minute, before opposite wing Murley slid over for a try in the corner for England's seventh inside half an hour.

Joseph acrobatically finished to score his fourth try of the first half

With Japan missing out on a try when tighthead Shuhei Takeuchi was held up, the visitors were next to score in any case as Dearns finished strongly from close range.

Cadan Murley got in on the act as England scored seven tries within 30 minutes

England had the final say of the first period, however, as a dominant rolling maul saw Earl get in on the scoring act for a half-time score of 49-7.

Into the second half, Ford produced a stunning 50:22 to earn England a five-metre lineout chance - one which they always looked likely to score from, and duly did through Martin.

The impressive George Martin powered his way over for a second-half England try

Japan lock Michael Stolberg then made a break up the middle of the pitch from deep and was caught by Henry Pollock, but England's Luke Cowan-Dickie was sin-binned for playing the ball while offside after the line-break.

It mattered little as Japan overthrew their five-metre lineout, and Joseph soon remarkably had his fifth try of the Test after plucking an intercept and running clear.

Joseph celebrates running in his fifth try - equalling the record for an England player

When Curry and Smith went over for England's 11th and 12th tries off lineout attacks, England's home support barely cheered, such was the disparity between the two sides.

Replacement back-row Fisilau was then awarded England's 13th try with seven minutes left, despite appearing to be held up, completing the scoring.

'Speechless' Joseph: A very special day for me

England wing and player of the match Will Joseph told ITV:

"Today was, personally, a very special day. I loved every minute of that.

"I loved the way the team moved the ball today. It was a joy to be part of. I'm speechless - it was a pretty perfect day.

"There were a few changes, and it was a short turnaround, but we got together really quickly. The performance we put in today just shows how hard we've been working behind the scenes.

"I'm going to enjoy today, then we'll be in Sunday and get our heads round the All Blacks. That's another challenge I'm looking forward to being part of - if selected!"

'Proud' Itoje: I don't even know how many tries Joseph scored!

England captain Maro Itoje told ITV:

"The performance was very good.

"Japan are a tricky team who gave Wales problems last week but we dealt with those problems.

"I'm super proud of our guys - the guys who came in, Archie [McParland] making his debut, Will making his second cap - I don't even know how many tries he scored!

"I'm just so proud of the team."

What's next?

For England, they next face New Zealand in their third Nations Championship Test of the autumn at Allianz Stadium Twickenham on Saturday, November 21 (2.10pm kick-off).

Sports.title: Tuchel unhappy as anti-racism protocol questions overshadow Spain clash
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel insisted his words had been "twisted" as questions over anti-racism protocols overshadowed the build-up to England's Nations League showdown in Madrid.

Tuchel was asked after England's win over Croatia on Thursday how he and England would react if racist abuse occurred during Sunday's game against Spain.

The head coach responded by saying he would "maybe take five minutes" to remind his players of the anti-racism protocols. Tuchel also said "we will not expect" any abuse to occur in Madrid.

The game is England's first visit to the Spanish capital since 2004, when the match was marred by racist abuse directed at England's black players.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England manager Thomas Tuchel was not happy with questioned about anti-racism protocols ahead of the game in Madrid

Spain were also fined and handed a partial stadium closure last month as punishment for Islamophobic chanting in Barcelona during a game against Egypt in March.

Luis de la Fuente was asked on Saturday by a Spanish-based English journalist: "Does the fact we keep talking about this topic demonstrate that Spanish football still has work to do in the fight against racism?"

In response, the Spain boss said: "What I can tell you, and you can pass this on to Thomas, is that there is no racism in Spain. That's how strongly I feel about it.

"There is no racism. Just as in England, there is no racism in Spain. None of us are racist."

Tuchel was then asked by a Spanish journalist about his counterpart's comments, to which he responded: "I was polite enough to ask [sic - answer] a question from your colleagues.

"And you run and ask the other coach, and tell him that I talk about racism in Spain. It's a perfect example of how it works.

"I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens. I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on earth.

"You create a lot of confusion for absolutely nothing. It's a perfect example of how it should not work."

Tuchel then admitted he was "a little upset" by the situation, feeling he had been tricked to "create a lot of confusion for no reason."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of Sunday's clash with Spain in the Nations League, England manager Thomas Tuchel believes their opponents are the 'biggest test in world football'

When asked if he had a message ahead of the game to send to Spanish fans, he added: "I sent a message but it got twisted. I said I always expect a friendly atmosphere.

"I don't expect racism, nowhere. I am shocked if it happens. It should never happen.

"I am the first person to stand up for these values. I got asked what happens if it happens and I said there are protocols in place.

"Football does what it does best, brings people together - not divides."

Rice not expecting any issues in Spain

England midfielder Declan Rice was also questioned on the topic, where he referenced previous incidents in which the national team had experienced racism.

Montenegro were charged by UEFA in 2019 for racist behaviour after former boss Gareth Southgate confirmed racist chanting was directed at Danny Rose during a 5-1 win.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Declan Rice believes the challenge of Spain will bring out the best in England as they seek to top their Nations League group

The 6-0 win against Bulgaria in Sofia in the same year was also stopped on two occasions in the first half due to racist abuse directed at players.

Speaking ahead of facing Spain, Rice said: "In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro, Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place we followed. We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.

"The manager hasn't brought that up yet. It wouldn't surprise me if he brings that up tomorrow. But we know where we stand.

"I'm not expecting any of that tomorrow night. This is a beautiful city, great stadium, the players we're playing against we have a lot of respect for. It's set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one."

Sports.title: Wales beaten in Norway as threat of Nations League relegation grows
Sports.content:
Wales suffered a 3-1 defeat to Norway in Oslo despite a spirited performance, as the threat of relegation to the second tier of the Nations League now looms over Craig Bellamy's side.

Wales looked the better side in the first half and had chances to take the lead, most notably through Daniel James on three occasions, before they unravelled after half-time.

Antonio Nusa showed why he is often referred to as the Norwegian Neymar as he broke the deadlock with his fine strike into the bottom left corner before substitute Andreas Schjelderup tapped home Erling Haaland's pass to give the hosts a commanding lead.

David Brooks' sublime chipped finish sparked hopes of a comeback but Haaland's penalty, after Connor Roberts pushed Schjelderup down in the box, punctured the late momentum they had gathered.

Wales can no longer finish above Norway due to their inferior head-to-head record, even if they beat leaders Portugal, but can avoid automatic relegation if they are not one of the two worst teams to finish bottom in tier A.

What next for Wales?

Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

"A reminder Wales have Portugal in their final group game on Tuesday.

"Even a win won't be enough to get off bottom spot due to head-to-head records with Denmark and Norway.

"They will avoid automatic relegation to tier B, though, if they don't finish as one of the two worst bottom-placed sides in tier A.

"Wales are on three points, with the other bottom sides in tier A currently on 0 points.

"A relegation play-off against a side from tier B would be the alternative."

Sports.title: Meetmebythesea gives McManus a first Paddy Power Gold Cup
Sports.content:
Ben Pauling’s Meetmebythesea showed his liking for Cheltenham once more and delivered owner JP McManus with his first victory in the prestigious Paddy Power Gold Cup.

Sent off the heavily backed 2-1 favourite on his first run since winning as a novice at the Festival in March, he put in some tremendous leaps on the way round for Harry Cobden.

Blueking d'Oroux, having his first run for Dan Skelton, looked the biggest danger after long-time leader Quebecois faded but Meetmebythesea powered away up the hill to win by two and a half lengths to give Cobden a second big victory in two days in the McManus colours.

Pauling said: "Harry wanted to ride him forward because not many are coming from behind today and he jumped brilliantly and travelled so well.

"I was a little worried turning for home that Dan's horse was going so well but he showed a lot of guts and then won well. Jumping the last he had plenty left and he has so much pace for a big horse.

"He needed to do that today and he showed a lot more than we have seen from him so far because he found plenty for pressure. He's just really good and you don't know what you have got until you run in races like that - that was cool, very cool.

"I didn't get nervous until 20 minutes before as you just want it so much when you believe in them so much and it's great that it has all come off.

"This is the race that really made me tick growing up and I've been coming to this meeting since I was 14. This has always been a big race for me and to have the favourite was a dream so to win it is even better.

"I had so much faith in this horse and I talked him up plenty in the lead-up. It's all well sitting on the fence but I knew he was good, just not how good. You just have to believe he is going to keep on improving and hopefully that puts him bang there for some of the better races."

BetVictor make Meetmebythesea 12-1 from 25s to now step up to the highest level at Kempton on Boxing Day where he could be given the opportunity to replicate The Jukebox Man's King George VI Chase heroics for Pauling last Christmas.

"I suppose we have to think about Kempton at Christmas and I think he's going to stay every yard of three miles," added the local handler.

"To keep a horse like this improving is cool and we need these types of horses to keep us going the right way. It's not easy when you're in the top 10 and you need to find horses of this calibre. He looks to be one of them.

"It's one of the big ones of my career and he has a bright future. I hope he could be as good as any I've trained but we've a long way to go. He might have to improve another 10 to 15lb to be winning a big one.

"I think this might be his trip or a nice flat three (miles) for now. Kempton felt nice last year, so who knows."

Having provided McManus with one of the major races absent from his trophy cabinet, a trip to Kempton at Christmas could represent the chance to tick off another missing from the mantlepiece.

However, festive dreams may be on hold for the Irishman, who was content to relish yet another fantastic result at Prestbury Park.

"I left it to Ben and this was his plan, you have to give him all the credit," said McManus.

"It's always nice to win a race at Cheltenham and I've tried to win this race many times but just come up short. Today thankfully it happened.

"You don't get tired of days like this and I've never won the King George, Champion Chase and Arkle, so we've got to try get those next.

"He could be a King George horse, but this was the plan for this lad today and he's only six. I know six-year-old's have won it before but we'll just have to see."

Atomic City lays down credentials in Triumph Trial

Atomic City laid down an early marker for his division in the JCB Triumph Trial Juvenile Hurdle at Cheltenham when displaying a smart turn of foot.

Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old was ridden with great confidence by J J Slevin at the back of the field and the 88-rated performer from the Flat jumped with aplomb bar one sticky leap at the second last.

Charles Darnay hit the front off the home bend under Harry Cobden but Slevin had him in his sights and brought his mount up against the rail before quickening clear to win by four lengths and justify 11-10 favouritism.

Coral cut him to 14-1 from 25s for the Triumph Hurdle in March with his rider suitably impressed.

Slevin said: "He's a high-class Flat horse who was quite good in Cork the first day and the aim today was to get him to spit it (the bridle) out today.

"He would be high up in Joseph's pecking order I would say, at least this stage, and I'd say he's going to be a Triumph Hurdle horse, he's a fair horse.

"I'd say he will be better with softer ground. He's jumped and travelled well and he couldn't have been better there.

"He's won easy and it's still early days. A lot of the lads won't have gone to the well yet with their juveniles and as the year goes on we'll find out more. But he was very impressive today."

Sports.title: Declan Rice accepts he had an ‘average World Cup’ as England gear up for Spain showdown
Sports.content:
Declan Rice has admitted he had an “average” World Cup at the end of a gruelling season and needed time out during the international window in September and October in order to return stronger.

The Arsenal midfielder believes the break has served its purpose, having produced starring performances against Bayern Munich and Liverpool in recent weeks. He is now ready to hit his best level for England in Sunday’s Nations League showdown against Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium.

Rice managed nerve pain in a hamstring that affected his lower back throughout the second half of last season and his fitness was a talking point during the World Cup. The 27-year-old had good games, most notably against the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the last 32 when he filled in towards the end as an emergency right-back.

Rice played well and scored in the third-place playoff against France. But he was typically honest when asked to reflect on his tournament as he prepared for the Spain game. England will leapfrog the world champions and finish top of their Nations League group if – and only if – they win in Madrid. It would theoretically bring an easier draw for the two-leg quarter-finals in March.

“By my standards it was an average World Cup,” Rice said. “France was probably my best game, Congo I played really well; some of the other games I didn’t play too well but you look back … I played 69 games [in the season].

“A title win with Arsenal, a Champions League final loss and into a World Cup. It’s annoying because at the World Cup you want to be at your best, you want to be totally fresh, you want to be ready. It’s annoying that I couldn’t perform how I did at Arsenal towards the back end of the season.

View image in fullscreen Declan Rice was frustrated with his performance levels during the World Cup. Photograph: VCG/Getty Images

“But knowing if I’m not going to be at my best, just constantly give 100% for this team, for the badge and you could see that. I loved [the last-16 win in] Mexico. We had the disappointment of Argentina in the semi-final, the second group game against Ghana. It’s games you look back on and think: ‘Could I have done better?’”

The playoff against France was on 18 July. After a short break, Rice reported back to Arsenal and played 45 minutes of the Community Shield against Manchester City on 16 August. When he played the 90 minutes of the defeat at Brighton on 19 September, he “did not feel right at all”, leading to a conversation with Tuchel who stood him down from England’s first four Nations League ties, the first of which was the 3-2 loss against Spain at Wembley. Rice sent a voice note to the England captain, Harry Kane, to explain his absence.

“I had an honest conversation with the boss here [Tuchel], who was really understanding,” Rice said. “He said: ‘Take some time, get yourself ready.’ It was about using that time to come back fitter and stronger. I feel really good now. It’s still like I’m building up to being 100 per cent but it’s closer to that than what I was a few weeks ago, for sure. And over the last few weeks, my performances have picked up.”

Rice, who won his 81st cap in the win over Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, had only previously withdrawn from three England camps. “I know the importance of playing for England, I know the importance of showing up, being available,” he said. “It’s one of the biggest things to me. Last camp, if I didn’t speak to the manager about it, I wouldn’t have done it. But he gave me his word. So I was in a better place mentally knowing that he authorised it.”

Rice has played at least 50 club matches in each of the past five seasons. “It’s something my body has got used to,” he said. “Probably last year, I felt it more than anything in terms of the amount of games, the toll it does take and realising as you get older, you have to take the recovery side of it a lot more seriously. When you were 21, 22, 23 … you could get up and have a round of golf the next day [after a match]. Now, even though I’m young at 27, you get up after a game and you can hardly feel your legs.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Meanwhile, Tuchel has decided to start James Trafford in goal against Spain – an eye-catching decision that will only harden the impression that Jordan Pickford is no longer his first-choice goalkeeper. Tuchel gave them two matches apiece in the September/ October window and said that he was minded to split the minutes once again this time.

View image in fullscreen James Trafford will start in goal for England against Spain. Photograph: Richard Calver/Getty Images

When he started Pickford against Croatia, it felt as though he had shelved the plan, given his insistence that the Everton player remained his No1 and Spain is plainly the bigger game. But Tuchel announced at his pre-match conference that Trafford would be given the opportunity.

“Traff will play,” Tuchel said. “We want to see how far Traff is. So he gets a highly competitive match. We had some changes in the back four in the last match [against Croatia], so we went for more stability and more experience with Pickers. And Traff gets the match tomorrow.

“Hopefully he’s not too over-excited or overly nervous because there’s no need to be. We trust him. But it is different to play for England than to play for your club. And to have the opportunity to play matches where it really matters is the best way to show up and to show that you’re ready. We know what Jordan can do for us. Jordan is, at the moment, our No1. I have a very clear picture in high-pressure moments.”

Tuchel also revealed that Ezri Konsa was back in contention after missing the Croatia game with a minor knee problem. He made it sound as though the Arsenal defender would start. “He showed up yesterday for individual work and he showed up today for training,” Tuchel said. “Ezri is back and ready to play.”
