Sports.content:
Magnusson: And your time starts ... now! What is paleontology? Smithers: Yes, absolutely correct. Magnusson: What’s the name of the directory that lists members of the peerage? Smithers: A study of old fossils. Magnusson: Correct. Who are Len Murray and Sir Geoffrey Howe? Smithers: Burke’s. Magnusson: Correct. What is the difference between a donkey and an ass? Smithers: One’s a trade union leader, the other’s a member of the Cabinet …

One of the Two Ronnies’ most celebrated sketches involves a Mastermind contestant whose specialist subject is answering the previous question. History repeats itself: the first time as comedy, the second time as Manchester United, who seem continually to be answering not the question of who would be the best available manager now, but who might have been the best available manager a few years ago.

The problem with football is that it never sits still. What was true once isn’t necessarily true now. What is true now won’t necessarily be true in a season or two’s time. Almost nothing is absolute. What works once might not work in a different context. The key to good recruitment is identifying to what extent somebody’s past success was contingent on their environment, and how they may behave in a different circumstances. And that is very difficult, which is why only four managers have won the English league title with more than one club.

The possibility of José Mourinho becoming manager of United was first raised as Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. Mourinho has recently claimed he turned the job down; other versions of events have him raging in a Madrid hotel as he learned that David Moyes had been hired, seemingly because Sir Bobby Charlton, then a senior board member, was worried about his impact on the image of the club.

It’s impossible, of course, to say whether Mourinho would have been a success had he taken the job then. But he had the ego to ensure he would not have lived in Ferguson’s shadow and, although he had been bruised by the Real Madrid experience, English football still recognised his aura. He was still adept enough to win a third league title at Chelsea.

By the time Mourinho finally took the United job in 2016, though, events in his final few months at Stamford Bridge had undermined him. He seemed weary and fractious, the tactical doubts raised in his final year at Madrid had proliferated and there was a growing sense his methods did not quite work with elite modern players.

There was a lot of talk about him as a guaranteed winner, but there’s no such thing in football. Very few managers last more than a decade at the very top. Only the most driven personalities, the most fecund minds, can endure the process of constant evolution necessary to stay ahead of the pack for more than a few years.

It’s easy to see why a board would have looked at his list of honours and been impressed, but United were appointing a manager on the way down. Was that obvious at the time? Perhaps not, but there were warning signs, and it’s the job of those doing the job of recruitment to identify them.

View image in fullscreen Erik ten Hag, skilfully as he managed Cristiano Ronaldo’s exit, seemed overawed by the United job. Photograph: Vince Mignott/EPA

With every appointment there are mitigations. Given the immense power Ferguson had, it would have been hard not to appoint Moyes when he had backed him. Yet if there was ever a time when he might have been the right man for United, it was surely six or seven years earlier; modern managers tend to peak in their mid-late 40s.

Louis van Gaal was 62 when he took the reins at United, enjoying a second coming after winning the Dutch title with AZ Alkmaar and an impressive 2014 World Cup campaign with the Netherlands. Perhaps the comparison isn’t fair in that he arrived as an elder statesman; nobody, other than perhaps Van Gaal, thought he would be a long-term appointment. But the idea he would bring calm after a period of turbulence was to ignore everything he had previously done. Van Gaal is many things but he is not a calming presence.

But again, the timing felt wrong. It could never have worked given he was preparing a side for the World Cup, but had he come in to replace Ferguson in 2013, as a hugely respected figure with a robust self-belief that was never going to care about breaking Fergusonian taboos, he might have been the man to see United through the awkward transition.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim were supposed to be the coming men, managers identified on the way up. Both seemed to make sense. Ten Hag’s Ajax had played astonishing football, had beaten Juventus and Real Madrid thrillingly in the Champions League, had come within Lucas Moura’s implausible hat-trick of a Champions League final. Amorim had ended Sporting’s 19-year title drought.

But it turned out they weren’t right. Ten Hag, skilfully as he managed Cristiano Ronaldo’s exit, seemed overawed by the job; Amorim’s insistence on playing 3-4-2-1 with a squad ill-equipped to play that way was one of the reasons Dan Ashworth expressed reservations, leading to his departure as sporting director.

It is possible, of course, maybe by this point even likely, that there is no right answer, that the mess United are in is insoluble, Old Trafford a meat grinder that will keep chewing up managerial reputations in perpetuity. But United’s board’s attempts to identify the rising star have been no more successful than their habit of appointing fading legends.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho seemed weary and fractious when the former Chelsea and Real Madrid manager arrived at Old Trafford in 2016. Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty Images

Which brings us to Mauricio Pochettino. He has done remarkable things: he may not yet have won trophies in England but he effected such an extraordinary transformation at Tottenham that it seemed not unreasonable they should be part of the Super League project. He found things difficult at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea, but most people do. A last-16 exit at a home World Cup with the USA was about par. The question, now he is 54, is whether the sense of drift about his career is an unfortunate and temporary state, or evidence that he is not quite what he was.

Perhaps the United job will revitalise him and he will revitalise them. But this feels like another appointment that would have been better made a few years ago; that United, once again, are answering the previous question.

Sports.title: Clinical Norway dent Wales’ Nations League top-tier hopes with victory in Oslo
Sports.content:
Wales suffered a 3-1 defeat to Norway in Oslo to dent their hopes of staying in the top tier of the Nations League.

Antonio Nusa and Andreas Schjelderup struck in the space of nine second-half minutes as Norway turned the screw.

Substitute David Brooks halved the deficit 11 minutes from time as Wales finished strongly.

However, Connor Roberts brought down Schjelderup and Erling Haaland converted from the penalty spot, extending his Nations League goals record to 23, as Norway avenged their October defeat in Cardiff.

It means Wales will definitely finish bottom of Group A4, irrespective of Tuesday’s result at home to Portugal.

Although they could finish on six points with Denmark and Norway, they have a worse head-to-head record against both nations – and could now face a playoff in March to avoid relegation to Group B.

Sports.title: De la Fuente adamant there is no racism in Spain despite England reminder to players
Sports.content:
Luis de la Fuente has told Thomas Tuchel there is no racism in Spain after the England coach’s admission that he would remind his players of the anti-racism protocol prior to their meeting at the Metropolitano on Sunday night.

This will be the first time the countries play each other in Madrid since some of England’s black players were subjected to racist abuse in a match at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2004. And although England have returned to Spain three times without incident since then, twice in Seville and once in Alicante, Tuchel was asked on Friday about going back in the buildup to Sunday’s game. The England coach replied that England “will not expect anything [untoward]” but also said: “maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid].”

Asked to respond to those words, and whether Spain still had work to do combating racism after being fined for discriminatory chants about Muslims during a game against Egypt in Barcelona in March, the Spain coach asked for confirmation as to whom they had come from, then said: “I can say the opposite. Tell Thomas there is no racism. As clear as that. Exactly the same as in England. We’re not racists, none of us.”

Tuchel, speaking later on Saturday night, expressed his irritation with the media, accusing journalists of manufacturing a row. “I got asked ‘what will happen if and if and if’, and I said if it happens, we have a protocol in place. That’s it … I never talked about racism in Spain, I answered politely a question about what happens. You create a lot of confusion for absolutely nothing.”

De la Fuente also described Spain versus England as “one of the best games you can see anywhere in the world right now, maybe the best”, and admitted that his team needs to exercise more control than they had been able to do during their 3-2 win at Wembley in September.

Asked to explain how the Premier League could be the richest league in the world and English players command bigger transfer fees than Spaniards despite the national team not winning anything since 1966 while the selección have won two World Cups and three Euros in this century alone, he insisted that it is a mistake to mix price and value.

View image in fullscreen Spain defeated England at Wembley in their Nations League game in September. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

“There is a song about value and price and it is exactly that,” the Spain coach said. “Someone has to pay it and that’s very welcome but it doesn’t mean it is the real value. I am surprised often when you see the prices paid for our players compared to [the fees] paid in England. I think ‘they’re so cheap’. They [Spanish players] are the best in the world. You can buy a player for half the price of what you pay in England for someone. In that world, in that market, that’s what’s spent. But I’m clear on this: we must not confuse price and value.”

“Between the English model and the Spanish model, I would choose the Spanish model,” De la Fuente added. “It is recognisable and the players have the ability to express it. The English model has developed a lot and I think it is very good. But you have to have the players. We can’t play like them and they can’t play like us.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“One of the strengths England have is the ability to run into space. When the game is open, they have people who are comfortable with that space and playing that style. Last time against them we lacked control, were unable to have longer periods of possession and impose ourselves more on our opponents.

“In the last two tournaments, England have been third and finalists. I think they are a great team and they have great players. That shows you it is not easy to win. Maybe that should make us appreciate what we’re doing this century: it is marvellous and very difficult. England are always candidates to win everything [nowadays]. This is one of the best games you can see in the world.”

Sports.title: Chelsea go top of WSL as Sandy Baltimore bullet sees off Manchester City
Sports.content:
Pragmatic, resolute and gutsy. Sonia Bompastor showed her ruthless side and delivered a tactical masterclass as Chelsea earned a 1-0 win over Manchester City and leapfrogged them at the top of the Women’s Super League.

Lucy Bronze credited fellow full-back Katie McCabe with firing Chelsea up pre-match, having told them they “had to be dogs” in the game, and a dogged performance followed. Sandy Baltimore’s stunning strike in added time at the end of the first half was the difference as the west London side nullified the threat of a team that had scored in each of their preceding 21 games in all competitions, inflicting their first loss of the campaign.

The task for City got even tougher when goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita received a straight red for clattering into Alyssa Thompson, but despite their numerical disadvantage it was end to end right up until the final whistle.

“It always affects you when you go one player down,” said manager Andrée Jeglertz. “But we handled that and that’s not why we lose the game. I think it’s small details. It’s a tight game, it’s two great football teams, there’s a lot of situations, there’s a lot of battles and they managed to score on their big chance from a great finish. We also have a couple of great opportunities where we don’t manage to score.”

Momentum was with City going into the match after their 5-0 defeat of West Ham the preceding weekend and a 4-1 win against Inter in the Champions League on Tuesday night and they were able to welcome the injured duo Vivianne Miedema and Beth Mead back to the bench to bolster their matchday squad.

At Stamford Bridge the England women’s manager, Sarina Wiegman, the US women’s manager, Emma Hayes, and passionate women’s football advocate and pundit Ian Wright were in the stands. It was a fixture that promised much, and it delivered: the league’s most potent attacks, with Chelsea having scored 28 league goals before this fixture to City’s 27, while Bompastor’s side had the most solid defence, having conceded only five times before kick-off.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: United see off Palace Show Manchester United captain Maya le Tissier marked her 150th appearance for the club with a superb strike in a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace at the Progress with Unity Stadium. Presented with a framed shirt before kick-off, Le Tissier whipped a low shot from distance into the net in the 18th minute before Elisabeth Terland confirmed United’s win after the hour mark. United moved up to fourth with the win and they kept hold of the position after Tottenham drew a blank in a goalless draw at home to Everton, whose winless run in the league stretched to five matches. In the day’s late game, Liverpool ended a five-match winless run in the WSL by easing past Brighton 3-0. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

It was a chess match. After a thrillingly frenetic start there was a change for Chelsea just 12 minutes in, with the centre-back Kadeisha Buchanan replaced by Veerle Buurman. There was speculation over whether the withdrawal of the Canadian defender was due to injury and Bompastor unconvincingly claimed it was.

“Yesterday in training, she got a knock to her head during contact with a teammate. She was fine after the training session. She was fine in the evening. We assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,” she said. “I just felt watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. Then I took the responsibility to make the substitution. But for me, I was almost forced to do that because I know my player and I know she was not in the game.”

However, if, as many believe, the defensive switch was a tactical decision, it was a stroke of genius, as Buurman was excellent at nullifying the threat of Khadija Shaw.

“She had a really good performance against a top player,” said Bompastor. “Today was positive. But again, as I’ve told you previously, when it doesn’t work it’s not so positive.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Ayaka Yamashita fouls Chelsea’s Alyssa Thompson, leading to the goalkeeper’s red card. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

There were chances at both ends but they were limited and it took until the fourth of five added minutes for Chelsea to draw first blood. The goal was sensational. Baltimore collected the ball just inside the box on the right, from Ellie Carpenter, lined up her shot and sent a piledriver of a strike into the roof of the net.

It was the only shot on target in the first half.

City sought an instant reply after the break but they could not find a way through and momentum ebbed and flowed. Jeglertz withdrew Sam Coffey and Mary Fowler in favour of Miedema and Laura Blindkilde Brown to help his side assert some authority in the middle and, through Miedema, to add some creative instinct.

However, as City pushed they left themselves vulnerable on the break and when Maika Hamano’s crossfield ball was met by Alyssa Thompson with just over 15 minutes remaining it was disaster for City. Yamashita raced out of her box and clattered into the Chelsea forward, conceding a free-kick and receiving a straight red card.

Despite City’s efforts, Chelsea were in control and they held strong to blow the title race wide open.

Sports.title: Portugal immortalise Cristiano Ronaldo’s No 7 shirt in tribute to national legend
Sports.content:
Portugal have made a permanent change to the No 7 shirt to honour the legacy of Cristiano Ronaldo and ensure the number remains forever associated with their greatest footballing icon.

The former forward, whose career spanned 23 years and 246 caps in which he scored 146 goals, announced his retirement on 5 November after a falling out with coach Jorge Jesus. His last appearance for Portugal was on 24 September, in a 1-0 home win over Wales in the Nations League.

Before their Nations League clash against Denmark, Portugal tweeted a unique design change to the iconic No 7 shirt to ensure Ronaldo’s version remains immortalised.

The small change to the number 7 is an acknowledgement of the star’s playing career in which he broke the men’s all-time scoring record. He captained his country to their first major trophy at Euro 2016, before adding two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025.

Portugal will also pay tribute to Ronaldo before and during their Nations League fixture against Denmark in Braga on Saturday.

View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo wore the iconic No 7 shirt for 20 years in a career that lasted 23 years for Portugal. Photograph: Armando França/AP

“Time to debut a new 7. Because there’s one that will be eternal,” the Portuguese national team wrote on social media on Saturday. The post included a goat emoji to signify “Greatest Of All Time”.

It also included a video that showed a horizontal crossed line through the No 7 as it is commonly written in Europe, suggesting that Ronaldo’s successors will all have that cross to bear when they wear the number.

Sports.title: Raphinha sees red as Brazil stunned by Japan while Argentina’s post-Messi era starts with defeat
Sports.content:
Raphinha was sent off as Brazil crashed to a 3-2 defeat to Japan in their international friendly in Singapore. The Barcelona captain had been substituted after 71 minutes, but was shown a red card after protesting against Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s stoppage-time winner on the touchline. The Brazil head coach, Carlo Ancelotti, was also sent off in a fractious ending to the match.

Japan went 2-0 up inside 20 minutes through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. Vinicius Junior reduced the deficit in the 33rd minute and scored again to drag them level on 75 minutes, before Sakamoto’s controversial late winner.

Argentina’s post-Messi era began with a 2-1 defeat at home against Uruguay in Buenos Aires. The loss marked the World Cup finalists’ first match since Lionel Messi’s international retirement in early October.

View image in fullscreen Argentina’s Nico Paz is crestfallen in Buenos Aires after a 2-1 defeat against Uruguay, the hosts’ first match since Lionel Messi’s international retirement. Photograph: Rodrigo Valle/Reuters

Leonardo Balerdi opened the scoring with an own goal in the 48th minute, before Maximiliano Araújo doubled Uruguay’s lead in the 53rd minute under their new coach, Diego Forlán. Julián Álvarez pulled one back for the hosts in the 73rd minute.

This clásico rioplatense on Friday also kicked off a new chapter for Argentina under Lionel Scaloni, who extended his contract through 2030 this week.

Messi’s retirement remains a fresh wound for local fans; notably, the La Bombonera stadium fell short of a sellout, a rare departure from the norm. While most supporters in the stands wore the albiceleste jersey with Messi’s No 10, Scaloni chose not to assign the number for the match. The coach explained he has yet to select a successor and as it is not mandatory he prefers to leave the jersey vacant for now.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

On the pitch, Argentina lacked the explosive, incisive spark Messi typically produced in the final third. Neither Nicolás Paz nor Thiago Almada was able to fill that void. Argentina will hope to bounce back against Costa Rica in Córdoba on Tuesday, while Uruguay host the Dominican Republic on the same day.

Sports.title: John McGinn double saves Scotland’s blushes against North Macedonia
Sports.content:
A special occasion for Andy Robertson saw Scotland flirt with embarrassment. Collection of his 102nd cap moves him level with Kenny Dalglish in the all-time Scottish list. Robertson will soon be a record holder. This was, however, John McGinn’s night. A double from McGinn, the second a penalty, spared Scottish blushes against a North Macedonia team who threatened to administer red faces to those in navy blue.

This proved an almighty struggle for Scotland. Questions – and plenty of them – surround whether or not Sébastien Pocognoli can build on the excellent work of his predecessor Steve Clarke. For now, Scotland are a tough watch. Pocognoli looks tactically inflexible and this is not the new dawn many predicted.

“At times it wasn’t pretty,” admitted McGinn. The 32-year-old compared this Scotland process to a club team starting a new season. The rationale is fair enough, were this a remotely forgiving environment.

It was Robertson who led the dressing room inquest in the immediate aftermath of last month’s defeat to Slovenia. It is not in the Tottenham full-back’s make-up to personalise scenarios but shortcomings in the last international window, Pocognoli’s first as the Scotland manager, added to the sense that the bigger picture was important here. North Macedonia looked favourable visitors, having not scored a goal in eight outings.

Pocognoli could call upon Kieran Tierney, Scott McTominay and Ché Adams for the first time and deployed all three from the outset. It already appears the Belgian coach will not deviate from a back three. Ben Gannon-Doak took his place at right wingback, as is feasible against such weak opposition. Scotland’s approach will inevitably change for Monday’s meeting with Switzerland.

View image in fullscreen Andy Robertson, the Scotland captain, equalled Kenny Dalglish’s record of 102 caps. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Scotland had been ponderous until McTominay came within an excellent Stole Dimitrievski save of properly announcing his international return. The midfielder swivelled and struck, with Dimitrievski equal to the Napoli man’s effort.

Robertson was denied the opportunity to mark his special night with a goal by an errant whistle. The referee hauled play back for a Scotland free kick – McTominay had been upended – when the playing of advantage would have seen Robertson collect a Billy Gilmour pass in a scoring position. The Hampden crowd mumped and moaned, which rather summed up recent attitudes around this Scotland team. It feels as if the public are not yet fully engaged with Pocognoli’s project. Adams sought to lift the mood, the striker stooping for a header that took a deflection before Dimitrievski batted away.

In backing up their statistical position, North Macedonia were providing nothing by way of attacking threat. Their enjoyment came from frustrating the Scots. McTominay, who has previous for acrobatic excellence in this arena, tried a 34th minute bicycle kick that flew over the crossbar and Scotland’s most lively player tried again with a low shot which Dimitrievski blocked with his midriff. This lack of cutting edge was a Scottish concern long before Pocognoli entered the dugout. The boos that met the half-time whistle, seconds after North Macedonia had created their first chance of the evening, depicted a supporter base who remained unconvinced.

Less than a minute of the second half had been played when Gilmour produced one of the worst misses ever witnessed at this famous old venue. Calamity in the North Macedonia defence allowed Adams to steal in. The Torino striker laid the ball back to Gilmour six yards out and, with an open goal, he blazed his shot wildly over the bar. It was a genuine, utter howler.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Scotland’s Billy Gilmour reacts after shooting over from six yards against North Macedonia. Photograph: Russell Cheyne/Reuters

Route one broke the deadlock for Scotland. Ryan Porteous’s looping header from the halfway line caused panic in the North Macedonia defence. Adams capitalised, his pass to the advancing McGinn setting up the Aston Villa midfielder’s 23rd goal for his country. Relief was as obvious as celebration.

Although a North Macedonia response was not in the script, the equaliser epitomised Scottish slackness. A near post run from Elmin Rastoder saw him meet a menacing Enis Bardhi corner from the left. Angus Gunn in the home goal was helpless as Rastoder flicked home.

North Macedonia clearly now sensed Scottish vulnerability. While Pocognoli’s men continued to dominate the ball, North Macedonia’s counterattacking threat had increased. Officialdom, and sharp footwork from Gannon-Doak, were soon to come to Scotland’s rescue.

Gannon-Doak was instantly convinced of the foul by Dimitrievski after the Bournemouth man tried to skip past the goalkeeper. It took the VAR to inform the referee that the incident was worthy of further inspection. Intriguingly, it was not Oli McBurnie – still awaiting his maiden Scotland goal and on in place of Adams – who took the spot-kick. Up stepped McGinn, who made no mistake. While Gannon-Doak is due credit for winning the penalty, this appearance once more raised serious questions about his decision making.

That of the Scottish FA in hiring Pocognoli would be open to question had North Macedonia delivered a shock. That they did not do so spared Scotland ignominy. “It was not always perfect,” said Pocognoli. You aren’t kidding, Sébastien.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s ex-boss reveals he was twice interviewed for Manchester United job
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s ex-boss reveals he was twice interviewed for Manchester United job

Rudi Garcia has revealed he came close to becoming Manchester United manager in 2021.

The Frenchman was amongst the candidates to replace Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in the Old Trafford dugout five years ago.



3 Garcia has revealed he was twice interviewed for the United job Credit: Getty

Solskjaer was dismissed by the Red Devils following a crushing 4-1 defeat at Watford, ending his three-year stint in charge.

With his exit coming midway through the season, United opted to appoint an interim boss until the end of the campaign.

United manager hunt

And former Belgium boss Garcia has now revealed he was in the running for the role and was interviewed twice by the club.



At the time, he had been out of work following his departure from Lyon at the end of the previous season.

The 62-year-old had spent just under two years with the club as well as previously winning a league and cup double with Lille in 2011.



However, Garcia missed out on the job as Ralf Rangnick was ultimately appointed in December 2021 on a deal until the summer.

Recalling how close he came to securing the United job, Garcia told The Athletic: "Yes, I interviewed twice to work in this fantastic club, one of the best clubs in the world.



"I’d like to work in England and I met Darren Fletcher and John Murtough.

"It was an interim role and they asked me what I would do once it was over.

"I told them I would do so well that I would be staying in Manchester, but they gave the job to Ralf."

3 United ultimately appointed Rangnick as interim boss in December 2021 Credit: Getty



Rangnick went on to guide United to a sixth place finish in the Premier League in his brief tenure.

The German was succeeded by Erik ten Hag in the summer of 2022 as the club's new boss.

Ten Hag would be the first of four permanent managers to be appointed by United in just over four years.

He was replaced by Ruben Amorim in November 2024 before Michael Carrick succeeded the Portuguese earlier this year.



Following the former United midfielder's sacking on Thursday, Mauricio Pochettino has now been announced as the club's latest manager.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss will officially take over on Thursday after signing a deal until the summer of 2029.

3 Garcia most recently guided Belgium to the quarter-finals of this summer's World Cup Credit: Getty

Rudi Garcia's managerial career 1996-98: AS Corbeil-Essonnes 2001: Saint-Etienne 2002-07: Dijon 2007-08: Le Mans 2008-13: Lille 2013-16: Roma 2016-19: Marseille 2019-21: Lyon 2022-23: Al Nassr 2023: Napoli 2025-26: Belgium Honours: Ligue 1, Coupe de France

Who is Rudi Garcia?

As for Garcia, he would return to the dugout with Al Nassr, where he would sign Cristiano Ronaldo following his United exit.



However, his tenure would last less than a season before he was ousted in April 2023.

Garcia took over at Napoli three months later, but was dismissed just 12 matches into the 2023/24 Serie A season.

His most recent role saw him guide Belgium to the quarter-finals of this summer's World Cup before departing after their defeat to eventual winners Spain.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel to drop key England star for crunch Nations League clash against Spain
Sports.content:
James Trafford will start in goal ahead of Jordan Pickford for England against Spain, Thomas Tuchel has confirmed to talkSPORT.

The Leeds United shot-stopper is set to be given the nod for Sunday's Nations League clash, live on talkSPORT.

3 Trafford will play in goal for England ahead of Pickford against Spain Credit: Getty

Trafford started in the reverse fixture at the end of September when England lost 3-2.

He then played in the 2-0 victory over Czech Republic, and his outing against Spain this weekend will be his fifth for the Three Lions.

All of these appearances have come in 2026, and he made his debut in March during the 1-1 friendly draw with Uruguay.

When speaking to talkSPORT, England head coach Tuchel said: "James is starting, we're doing it like the last camp.

"It's a good opportunity for him, first of all, to show how far he is, and for us to observe how close he is

"A beautiful game for him, big opportunity, big stages. We trust our players, and they share the matches like the last camp."

On whether or not this changes who is the no. 1 for England, Tuchel insisted: "I will always tell you the same, Jordan is no. 1, Jordan knows.

"We use the Nations League to see our goalkeepers in high-pressure moments, because it is different if you play a Nations League game in Group A or in qualifiers, everything is difficult in itself.

"It's the highest level, and this is where we need to see. I know what Pickers can do for us, I know what he did for us. I know him in high-pressure moments, he played the World Cup for us, the Euros.

"We don't know about Trafford. He deserves to be in these matches, and that's the decision."

3 Tuchel has chosen to name England's rising goalkeeping star over their long-term no. 1 for the final match of 2026 Credit: Getty

Pickford has featured in England's past three fixtures and conceded just one goal during that run.

That was in the 2-1 victory over Croatia on Thursday night, which has teed up a winner-takes-all clash against Spain.

Should England win, they will finish top of Nations League Group A3 on goal difference.

However, regardless of the result in Madrid, they have already booked a place in the quarter-finals.

England eye massive win over Spain

Tuchel also explained the magnitude of playing the world champions, who have won their last 12 matches and not lost since June 2025, in his press conference.

"It is the biggest test in world football for national teams at the moment, because Spain seems unbeatable."

3 England will hope to end 2026 on a high by beating world champions Spain on their own turf Credit: Getty

Tuchel added: "It is, in itself, a powerful nation since many, many years in international football. Very, very strong identity, and a very strong, competitive mentality.

"They won the last big titles. They won the European Championship, they won the World Cup, of course.

"We're trying to take it away from them, we're trying to beat them, and we're up for it.

"I think it's two powerful nations, I think we're in a very good moment to push our limits. We're in a very good moment to try what so many teams tried.

"I think we were very close at Wembley in the first match. We're up for a spectacular match and we're up for the fight, we want to win, that's the target for tomorrow."

Tuchel also gave a positive update on his squad's fitness as he said: "It's good news, because we have everyone back.

"Ezri Konsa is back and available, Djed Spence is back and available. We have full choice in our back four."

The match against Spain will be England's last of 2026, with the next international break coming in March.

Sports.title: Niclas Fullkrug lined up for permanent West Ham exit after outscoring Harry Kane
Sports.content:
Werder Bremen boss Daniel Thioune has signalled his intention to keep Niclas Fullkrug beyond next summer.

The German forward is currently in his third spell at the Bundesliga side having joined on loan from Championship club West Ham United.



3 Fullkrug has rediscovered his form in his third spell with Bremen Credit: Getty

Fullkrug has run riot so far this season, already netting nine goals in nine appearances to help Bremen sit sixth in the table.

He currently leads the Golden Boot race ahead of Bayer Leverkusen forward Patrick Schick who has eight goals, whilst Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is in joint-12th with just four league goals thus far in the 2026/27 campaign.

And Thioune has now publicly stated that the club would like to re-sign Fullkrug on a permanent basis.



"I believe the desire is shared by all sides," Thioune. "We as a club, I as coach, and Niclas himself are all very interested in continuing to work together beyond the summer."

Fullkrug's return to goalscoring form is a welcome one after netting just three times in 29 appearances in all competitions for the Hammers since signing from Borussia Dortmund for £27million in 2024.



His time in East London was tough as a result of injuries and inconsistent playing time, with him even launching an explosive rant in the direction of his own teammates when the Irons drew with an already-relegated Southampton back in April 2025.

A mid-season loan to Serie A giants AC Milan in January of this year was not the fresh slate he had hoped it would be, with him scoring just once in 20 appearances as his parent club were relegated from the Premier League in his absence.



Fullkrug recalled to Germany national team

Fullkrug's recent goal-scoring prowess earned him a recall to the Germany national team for the first time since September 2025, and his first selection by new manager Jurgen Klopp.

“Good form and scoring goals are never a bad thing,” Klopp answered when asked why he had brought Fullkrug back. “Fulle has been performing and scoring all kinds of goals, almost all of them spectacular."

Klopp added: "He has an incredible influence on the game, not just through his goals, but also the way he carries himself, I don't think he was able to have that influence on a team at every stage of his career, at Bremen, he can.

3 Bremen are keen to make Fullkrug's loan move permanent next summer Credit: Getty



"When you feel at home, you can see what happens. That's generally the feeling we want to give the players, even if we don't have them together very often.”

Fullkrug's most successful spell of his career came playing for the River Islanders, in which he scored 45 goals in 90 appearances between 2019-2023.

Of Bundesliga players with at least 20 shots this season, only Eintracht Frankfurt forward Younes Ebnoutalib has a higher xG per shot than Fullkrug (0.26 to 0.21).

“I was delighted because he thoroughly deserves it," Thioune said of his feelings when he found out Fullkrug was called up for international duty this November.



"If you look at his individual performances, he’s been one of the standout attacking players. He’s earned this call-up through his own hard work. I’m proud to have a Germany international in our squad."

For Fullkrug, there is perhaps just one simple explanation as to why he has rediscovered his knack for goal - feeling at home.

3 Fullkrug has just three goals in 29 appearances for West Ham since signing in August 2024 Credit: Getty

"Werder is simply my home," he told reporters during the DFB press conference on Tuesday. "It's my footballing home. As you all know, one sleeps the best in one's own bed.



"I immediately felt comfortable there. I joined the academy at the age of 14 and, in my estimation, I believe about 70-90 percent of the same people are on staff there."

He also ensured that he gave the Bremen medical staff their flowers for keeping him fit and healthy since his arrival.

"I'm healthy and there's a medical department there that takes good care of me," Fullkrug continued. "They've managed to get me back on track and ensure that I haven't missed any training sessions.

"And we have a great team from which I benefit. The transfers that we brought in this summer have all done great. I just happen to be one of them."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel questioned for overlooking uncapped English star thriving in Premier League
Sports.content:
Jayden Bogle has been top-notch for Leeds United so far this season and deserved to be selected in the England squad.

That's the view of former Leeds defender Matthew Kilgallon, who had extensive praise for one of the most in-form Premier League players.



3 Bogle has enjoyed a strong start to the season for Leeds and been one of the league's best defenders Credit: Getty

Bogle has started in all ten of Leeds' league fixtures and has shone on the right side of their attack and defence as a wing-back.

He has drawn 16 fouls during the campaign, which is the most in their squad, and been a constant threat across all areas of the pitch.

A former England Under-20 player, Bogle has never earned a call-up to the senior side and therefore missed out on Thomas Tuchel's latest side.



Trent Alexander-Arnold and Ben White were the chosen right-backs, with Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence also able to play in the role.

But for Kilgallon, Bogle deserved a spot in the squad and possibly his England debut against either Croatia or Spain, with the latter being their opponents live on talkSPORT on Sunday.



Bogle England omission a 'shock'

"Is there a chance, at some point, with question marks against Trent and Reece James injured, that perhaps he could get a call-up for his country?" Scott Minto asked on Saturday Session.

Kilgallon replied: "Scott, it's a right shout from you. To be honest, I couldn't believe he wasn't in the squad this time, he has been outstanding.



"Don't get me wrong, he's got a lovely relationship with James Justin, they work really well together, or they've got a bit of freedom - sometimes, James Justin will come forward with the ball and Jayden Bogle will sit back in that right-side centre-half, or right-back.

"But honestly, it's quite hard to actually say what position he plays for Leeds United... I've seen him in goal at one point!

"Sometimes, he's actually the highest player on the pitch for Leeds United, he's got freedom but, do you know what?

3 Kilgallon was surprised to see Bogle not be called up to the England squad amid his run of form at club level Credit: Getty



"He works so hard, he will go forward and make something happen, but he'll be back defending, his recovery runs are unbelievable.

"I was shocked he wasn't in the squad, he's getting spoken about quite a lot and what I've seen of him this season, and it's a lot by the way, he's been top drawer."

Although Bogle has received plaudits for his performances at Leeds, he was at the centre of controversy last weekend.

The 26-year-old avoided a red card in their 1-0 win over Spurs after a tackle on Mathys Tel, who was eventually substituted with an injury.



Bogle caught Tel on the back of his ankle in a challenge that sparked fury from talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara.

Former Chelsea left-back Minto asked about the incident, and Kilgallon explained why he was not dismissed at Elland Road.

3 Kilgallon understood why people called for Bogle to be sent off, but explained why he avoided a red Credit: TNT Sports

"If it was with the actual tackling foot, his right foot, and it hits him high on the Achilles, then you're going, 'That's going to be a red.'



"But it was his standing foot, he looks to try and plant that left down to then try and tackle with his right foot.

"He's actually caught him with his standing foot on the Achilles and it does look bad slowed down.

"But if you actually watch it at real pace, he's in control as he's going towards the winger, he's not running in there recklessly where you go, 'Oh my god, it's a car crash'.

"He's actually gone in, slowed himself down to sort of jockey him, I think that's where he got away with it, I think I heard something about the ref saying it was something to do with the pace when he came into the challenge."



Leeds later issued a statement to condemn vile racial abuse that was sent to Bogle after the match.

Sports.title: Manchester United quietly complete first signing of Mauricio Pochettino era
Sports.content:
Manchester United have reportedly prised highly-rated striker Tyler Adjei away from Reading.

The 16-year-old becomes the first signing of the Mauricio Pochettino era following the Argentine's appointment at Old Trafford.



2 Adjei has been capped six times for England's Under-15s Credit: Instagram @adjei.tyler7

According to The Athletic, the teenager was registered as a new Red Devils player this week.

What has been said about Tyler Adjei?

A source told the news outlet: "He's got an athletic profile; he's got more to come physically.

"He moves well, he has a good temperament, mentality and demeanour.

"He has a good energy to train.

"He’s got a way to go technically, as is the norm for a player of his age."



Able to operate anywhere across the front line, it has been claimed that United view him as a No.9 going forward.

With five goals from 18 games in the U18 Premier League, Adjei is believed to have had no shortage of suitors.



But its the Theatre of Dreams that the youngster has chosen.

Adjei will link up at United with international experience to his name, having been capped on six occasions for England's Under-15s.

And it will be with Darren Fletcher's U18s that the centre-forward will be operating in.



2 Adjei is just the latest teenage starlet that the Red Devils have signed Credit: Instagram @adjei.tyler7

What other youngsters have Man United signed?

United's acquisition of Adjei is just the latest teenage star that they have snapped as part of their aggressive pursuit of talent for their academy.

Twice the club raided rivals Manchester City in the summer after bringing in midfielders Karim Cassim and David Eze.

And they also managed to lure winger Isaac Konde away from Liverpool.

That is in addition to bringing in forward Tynan Thompson from Tottenham in a package deal worth £8million.



Meanwhile, Cristian Orozco joined from Colombian outfit Fortaleza CEIF, with goalkeeper Kit Margetson snapped up following his Swansea departure.

And with Pochettino known for bringing through youth players, those in the academy know there is a pathway to the first team.

Sports.title: Stan Collymore: My only friend in football Danny Kelly saved my life after I retired
Sports.content:
Stan Collymore: My only friend in football Danny Kelly saved my life after I retired

Stan Collymore has paid an emotional tribute to the late Danny Kelly, thanking him for being his 'only friend' in football.

On Wednesday morning, it was announced that beloved broadcaster and talkSPORT presenter Danny had sadly passed away, aged 69.

5 Thousands have joined talkSPORT in paying tribute to Danny Kelly, who has sadly died aged 69

A much-loved member of the talkSPORT family, Danny became one of the most recognisable voices on radio after joining the team in 2007.

Danny had been undergoing treatment after being diagnosed with throat cancer, which led to him stepping away from his talkSPORT role in March.

In his last appearance, he urged men to go out and get themselves checked in what was an emotional message.

Tributes have flooded in since Danny's passing, with colleagues past and present, readers and listeners rushing to remember him fondly.

Danny was known to be a mentor for many younger journalists and pundits, one of whom was former England, Liverpool and Nottingham Forest star Collymore.

The pair co-hosted talkSPORT's weekday evening slots following Collymore's arrival on the network in 2008.

And the ex-Premier League striker paid a touching tribute to Danny, thanking him for offering him his chance in the media industry during a dark period following his retirement from football in 2001.

Collymore pays tribute to Kelly

Joining talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs on Friday, Collymore recalled the role Danny played in a difficult time in his life.

Collymore began: “Between retiring from football in 2001 to 2008, when I joined talkSPORT, my life was a mess. It's on record, it was a mess.

“At times I didn't genuinely know whether I was going to see the next day."

5 Collymore scored over 100 career goals, including for Liverpool, but struggled with life after football Credit: Getty

5 Danny was a cherished member of the talkSPORT family, and brought great joy to listeners whilst being a cherished colleague too Credit: talkSPORT

In an incredibly tough time, Danny would ultimately hand Collymore a lifeline when he offered him the chance to join him on talkSPORT.

He continued: “I was driving back from London, I'd been to see a psychiatrist and I switched on BBC London - Danny was presenting.

"He was talking about sports books, and he said, ‘The best sports book I've ever read was Stan Collymore's.'

“I stopped the car on the motorway near High Wycombe and I called in and he said, ‘Oh my God, Stan Collymore's on the line. Let's have a chat’.

“I didn't hear anything then for the next couple of years, and then when Danny did his show - the Evening Kick Off on talkSPORT - he was asked who he would like to present the show with.

"This is a guy who's worked with everybody in radio, and he said me. And we did a couple of years."

On social media, Collymore said without that offer from Danny, 'I know I wouldn't be writing this today'.

Sharing his fond memories of Danny, Collymore recalled how the pair bonded over a shared love of music, while the much-loved broadcaster was always on hand offer a listening ear.

He went on: "Monday nights in particular were very special because we'd talk about all the topics from the weekend.

“And after the show, I would drive back to Cannock, back in bed for 16, 18, 20 hours at a time - I was really struggling mentally.

“And we would have the most amazing conversations about Scritti Politti, Prefab Sprout, 80s obscure bands.

“The greatest thing I can say about him - other than all the tributes that have been laid bare about his fun, his big brain, his big personality - was the fact that he would never judge somebody.

5 Collymore has been a regular on talkSPORT since 2008, and thanked Danny for making this possible Credit: Getty

“He would ask you, ‘What are you like? Why are you like this? He was incredibly inquisitive’. So he became, probably over football and media, my only friend.”

'A loving man, a kind man'

Danny remained a constant support for Collymore as he faced personal tragedy.

He shared: “Last year, I lost my mum, who was beloved to me. Then I lost my dad, and I had a real issue around that.

“Then in early March, I lost a really close friend, one of my closest friends, somebody I love very, very much.

“And Danny, when he made the announcement on talkSPORT [about his cancer diagnosis], sent me a 10, 12 minute voice message. And it was all about, ‘How are you? How's life? How's family?’

“And he'd just come off air to basically tell everybody that he had cancer, and he didn't know whether he was going to make it.

“That was the man he was. It didn't matter what the time of day was. He was a notorious night owl - at two, three in the morning, we'd have a chat about any number of things.

5 Danny will forever be remembered as one of radio's biggest and best presenters, and leave a lasting legacy for all of us Credit: talkSPORT

“But you see the length and breadth of the globe of people and the tributes to him - I watched the funeral today and I just want to send all of my love to [his wife] Alex and his very close friends and family.

“But he was a good man, an honest man, a loving man, a kind man. And I'm really, really glad to be able to say that he was my friend.”

Rounding off his touching tribute, he added: “I knew I wasn't a great man, but Danny would introduce me, ‘And the great man, Stan Collymore’.

“I'd go away feeling 10 foot tall because I thought, ‘Well, if Danny Kelly thinks I'm all right, then I'm alright’.”

Sports.title: Rickie Lambert’s brutal memory proves Mauricio Pochettino will fix glaring Man United problem
Sports.content:
Rickie Lambert and Toby Alderweireld have told talkSPORT what Manchester United can expect from Mauricio Pochettino - and it's what they need the most.

Pochettino has taken the reins at Old Trafford from Michael Carrick, who was sacked following a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

6 Pochettino has been named Man United boss Credit: Getty

The ex-Tottenham and Chelsea boss will leave his role in charge of the United States' national team on November 18, with talkSPORT revealing that the total compensation is around $12million (£9m).

What Pochettino will bring to Man United

Alderweireld, who made over 170 appearances under the Argentine at Spurs, revealed that being in top shape is a minimum requirement.

He told talkSPORT Breakfast with Alan Brazil and Ally McCoist: "He will make players fit. That's for sure. Second of all, he brings intensity.

"It's not like everyone is playing on their own game. No, he wants a team.

"He wants a team that's going to be on the front foot, wants to play pressure and have the ball as well.

"So, a clear idea, intensity and players being fit - I think that's the way he likes to work."

During his time at Southampton, Pochettino famously went to extreme lengths to stop Luke Shaw eating pizza - with his dietary habits continuing in his spell at Spurs.

Alderweireld added: "Everyone, food-wise, gym-wise, everything needs to be like he wants it, and that's a big part of his philosophy.

6 Pochettino oversaw three successive top-three finishes and a run to the Champions League final with Spurs Credit: Getty

"And then you're gonna want to buy the players, maybe not always the biggest names, the biggest talents, but guys who desire to win, desire to become better, desire to run.

"If you see the players he bought from Spurs, that's thing number one: the desire to become better, the desire to win games, to win duels, to run.

"I think that's why I think Pochettino is the man for Man United to change things around.

"In the past couple of transfer windows, they bought good players, good quality, but they miss some chemistry; they miss the intensity, and I think Pochettino will bring that one hundred per cent."

Man United running stats under Carrick

Pochettino has his work cut out for him to introduce his intensity to the players, who have been called out for their work rate this season.

6 Man United players have spent much of the season walking under Carrick Credit: Getty

Team Distance (km) Opp. Distance (km) Difference (km) Arsenal 1193.8 1149.3 44.5 Brighton 1159.5 1119.9 39.6 Bournemouth 1169.9 1145.7 24.2 Fulham 1194.6 1175.2 19.4 Brentford 1164.3 1146.4 17.9 Leeds United 1172.8 1155.7 17.1 Newcastle 1157.9 1148.2 9.7 Tottenham 1141.1 1132.2 8.9 Ipswich Town 1173.7 1165 8.7 Forest 1143.4 1137.3 6.1 Chelsea 1136.3 1138.3 -2 Hull City 1148.4 1154.3 -5.9 Everton 1139.4 1149.7 -10.3 Sunderland 1142.7 1157.9 -15.2 Crystal Palace 1132.4 1149.8 -17.4 Coventry City 1133.6 1151.2 -17.6 Man City 1126.3 1150.9 -24.6 Man United 1125.1 1151.9 -26.8 Aston Villa 1137.6 1172.1 -34.5 Liverpool 1112.3 1154.1 -41.8

Man United rank 19th for distance in the Premier League, having covered just 1125.1km this season, according to Opta.

Ironically, 120.8km of that came in their most recent outing in the Villa draw - their most in a top-flight game under Carrick in 2026.

Liverpool are the only team below them for distance, and yet Andoni Iraola's side top the rankings for sprints - to show that the Reds are more selective with their intensity off the ball.

Alarmingly, Man United, meanwhile, sit 14th for the same metric.

Pochettino's new side also boasts a -26.8 differential when comparing their distance covered to their average opponents’ distance (with only Liverpool and Villa ranking worse).

Man United running stats this season Premier League 2026/27 Distance (km) - 1125.1 (19th) Sprints - 1065 (14th) Distance High-Speed Running - 62.7 (14th) Difference to Opp Distance (KM) - Minus 26.8 (18th)

6 Man United boast some of the worst cumulative running stats in the Premier League this season and consistently get outrun by their opponents game-to-game Credit: AFP

Inside Pochettino's extra training

As noted by talkSPORT's chief football correspondent, Alex Crook, improving the running stats will be first up on the priority list.

And Rickie Lambert, who worked under Pochettino at Southampton, has warned United's players about what happens if they complain.

The 11-cap England international famously appealed to the Argentine to scrap the team's Monday 'horseshoe' running drills days after playing — only for Pochettino to double the workload in response.

Lambert explained on talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Baker: "One of the things that he does is on a Monday, he does running. Now, as British lads, we're not used to that.

"It was 12 horseshoes in 45 seconds. Now, most of the lads can do that easily. I couldn't. I really struggled doing that, especially after playing a full game.

"So I said to the lads, 'I'll go and speak to him. Who wants to come in with me?' Jos Hooiveld put his hands up. So we go in, we speak to him, we express how myself and the group are feeling.

"'You just need to calm it down a little bit.' And he was so reassuring; he made me feel like he was really listening to me.

"And then he went, 'OK, I understand.' The next Monday, we've done 24 runs!"

6 Pochettino fixed Southampton's leaky defence to ensure their Premier League survival Credit: Getty

Lambert continued: "It will come down to the dressing room because it came down to us. After that, after he'd done 24 runs, we all looked at each other, and we were like, 'What are we going to do?'

"And it was either we're going to go away from him, or we're going to get behind him.

"And we all chose to get behind him at that moment. And from then on, we progressed massively individually and as a collective.

"And that dressing room will go for the same thing. They will all dictate how that manager goes, even as good as I think he is.

"The dressing room will have the ultimate say. And if they go with him, they'll turn that club around. I honestly believe that."

6 Pochettino has built his managerial career around a high-pressing, high-energy approach Credit: getty

A trip to Anfield is first up for Pochettino and Man United, which could bring the 54-year-old a sense of deja vu.

Back in 2015, Jurgen Klopp's first game in charge of Liverpool saw him look to implement his renowned pressing style almost overnight against Pochettino's Spurs side.

And in a goalless draw at White Hart Lane, the Merseysiders became the first team to run further than Tottenham that season, with their 116km covered the most the players had achieved so far.

Over a decade later, fans can guarantee one thing from Pochettino's reunion with Liverpool - his Man United players will run...

Sports.title: Arsenal told £79million rival Premier League striker would be their perfect No.9
Sports.content:
When it comes to a striker that fits the bill perfectly for Arsenal, they need look no further than Hugo Ekitike.

That's according to talkSPORT's Ade Oladipo, who has insisted the currently injured Liverpool star could be the missing piece in the Gunners' strong side.



4 Injury has prevented Hugo Ekitike from building on his strong debut season at Liverpool Credit: Getty

Despite a near-perfect start to the season, the Premier League champions have found themselves lacking firepower up front at times and heavily reliant on Kai Havertz as their focal point.

Six of Arsenal's nine Premier League wins this term have been by a single-goal margin, highlighting goals as a potential area for improvement.

While Viktor Gyokeres is also available, Mikel Arteta has been reluctant to use him - starting the Swede just once in the league.



With the £63.7million man facing an uncertain future, this has again led to suggestions Arsenal are in need of an attacking focal point.

The north Londoners have recently been linked with Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane and Club Brugge's Nicolo Tresoldi.



But talkSPORT's Oladipo believes the perfect fit lies closer to home, who named Liverpool star Ekitike as a tailor-made Arsenal player.

The man for the job?

With Arsenal five points clear at the top of the Premier League after nine wins from their opening 10 games, Oladipo and Manchester United pundit Flex discussed where they could possibly strengthen.



“You look at that forward line and that's the weak point," said Oladipo on talkSPORT's Thank Football it's Friday.

“Saka and his injuries is obviously taking him down a bit. Gyokeres - I don't think the manager fancies him.

“Havertz - we still don't know what position he is. Is he a no.8, no.9, or a no.10? It's all over the place with Havertz.

4 Mikel Arteta is yet to find a prolific goalscorer for his Arsenal side Credit: Getty



“I like him, but he's almost numberless. It's kind of strange - he’s like a nine-and-a-half."

This led Oladipo to outline Ekitike as the perfect striker for Arsenal, who insisted he possesses all of the attributes to star for them.

Ekitike remains sidelined after rupturing his Achilles in April, which robbed him of a place in France's World Cup squad after an impressive debut season with Liverpool.

After his £79million arrival from Eintracht Frankfurt, the forward fired in 17 goals altogether last term to finish as the Reds' top scorer.



And with Arsenal boss Arteta building a physically strong team capable of grinding out results, Oladipo insisted Ekitike's presence - standing at 6ft3in - and ability make him perfect for the Emirates.

He said: “You know who's the perfect number nine for Arsenal? They won't get him, but the perfect number nine for Arsenal - Ekitike.

4 Ekitike hit double figures in Premier League goals in his first season in England Credit: Getty

“Honestly, Ekitike I think is fantastic. You just look at them as Arsenal players. Even that's why I said Bradley Barcola - he kind of reminded me of an Arsenal player."



A huge Reds fan, Oladipo quickly added: “Obviously they're at Liverpool and hopefully they stay at Liverpool for years to come!"

Arsenal's Achilles heel?

As mentioned, a lack of goals has been Arsenal's only real shortcoming so far this season.

Their latest victory - a 1-0 home win over Hull - saw them equal their best ever start to a Premier League campaign, and leaves them with a commanding five-point lead at the top of the table.

However, the Gunners have done so without a main source of goals, with Havertz, Martin Odegaard and Bukayo Saka their joint-top scorers in the league with three goals apiece.



A lack of clinical finishing appeared to worry Arteta following the Hull win, who admitted his side must improve here.

4 Martin Odegaard has shared Arsenal's goalscoring responsibilities from midfield in the opening months of the season Credit: Getty

Speaking afterwards, he said: "We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

"Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks.



"We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And open, I think, the scoreline much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game."

Sports.title: England boss Thomas Tuchel angry at being dragged into race row after being told by Luis de la Fuente: 'There is no racism in Spain!' on eve of Nations League showdown
Sports.content:
England boss Thomas Tuchel angry at being dragged into race row after being told by Luis de la Fuente: 'There is no racism in Spain!' on eve of Nations League showdown

Thomas Tuchel was dragged into a bitter race row on the eve of England's Nations League showdown with Spain.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols in case their players suffered racist abuse at the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday evening.

England players were notoriously subject to racial abuse at the Bernabeu in 2004 and England have not played in Madrid since.

But Spain manager Luis de la Fuente reacted angrily when he was told that Tuchel had addressed the subject.

'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente said. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'

The row then deepened when a Spanish journalist told Tuchel about De La Fuente's reaction and the England coach grew exasperated with the line of questioning.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols

'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente said. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'

'I was polite enough to answer a question from your colleagues,' Tuchel said, 'and you run and ask Spain's coach and tell them that I talked about racism in Spain.

'I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered a question politely. I never expect racism. The dressing room is the most anti-racist place in the world. This is a perfect example of how you create confusion out of nothing.'

Tuchel had earlier said: 'It's important that the players know about the protocol. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch.

'We had a same discussion before the Serbia game [in Belgrade in September 2025]. There is a protocol in place.'

England midfielder Declan Rice said that Tuchel had not yet addressed the group about racism protocols but that they were clear about what they would do if any England players were abused.

England's game against Bulgaria in Sofia in 2019 was halted after allegations of racism against England players but the game was completed.

Sports.title: England's Euro 2028 mission starts NOW! Thomas Tuchel's men must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - or risk their 'DNA' cursing them yet again, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
It is four months, almost to the day, since England shrank from the call of history and lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina in Atlanta but Thomas Tuchel may not believe that the Nations League tie against Spain in the Metropolitano on Sunday evening represents his best shot at redemption for the way things played out that afternoon in America’s South.

That is largely because Tuchel does not appear to believe he has anything to redeem himself for. The manner of his side’s capitulation - and the substitutions he made - in the Mercedes-Benz Stadium last July enraged the nation, but Tuchel said the fault was in the damned DNA of the English, that we were underlings, and that our players found it constitutionally impossible to keep hold of the ball.

Whatever Tuchel thinks, the fact remains that the tie against Lamine Yamal, Fabian Ruiz, Pedri and Mikel Oyarzabal and the rest of the world champions at the home of Atletico Madrid offers Tuchel and his players the opportunity to encourage themselves and their fans that they are not destined to be also-rans wired to fall at the final hurdle for evermore.

Spain are formidable opposition. They are on a record-breaking run of 43 matches unbeaten and have won their last 12 in succession. They haven't drawn a game since their June 15 game against Cape Verde in the World Cup. Their last defeat was on March 22, 2024, when they lost 1-0 to Colombia in a friendly. Some ask whether they are the best international side the world has ever seen.

‘Spain seem unbeatable,’ Tuchel said, when he walked into the press room at the Metropolitano on Saturday night and heard hymns of praise being lavished upon the opponents he is about to face.

‘They have a very strong identity and a very strong mentality. We are trying to take it away from them. We are up for it. We are up for the fight. We are up for a spectacular match. We can see how far we can push the limits with the world champions in Madrid. The group is full of self-belief and rightly so.’

England must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - even if they have flaws

Thomas Tuchel must show he can find a way around the limitations presented by the 'DNA' he has complained about

This may be the toughest game that Tuchel’s England side play until the European Championships in 2028, where the final will be contested at Wembley, and they will play all their games at home. They need to go into that tournament with the belief that they can beat the best when the pressure is at its highest.

Beating Spain away in the final game of the group phase of the Nations League is not quite the same as a critical match at a major tournament but it is as stiff a challenge as Tuchel is going to face until then. Beating Croatia 7-0 in front of gangs of schoolkids in Rijeka last month was hailed as the best England performance of the Tuchel era. Which says it all, really.

It was a great performance in a relatively meaningless match. Now it is time for him to show that he can marshal an England side to succeed against the very best, not fall apart when the prize is in sight. His protestations of powerlessness in the aftermath of the Argentina defeat were not a good look for a coach who was hired with the idea that his coaching prowess and his game management could get England over the line.

Has he learned anything from the manner of the Argentina defeat? ‘This game against Spain will be proof of concept at the highest level,’ he said, ‘but we are up for it. I think we have taken the next step after the World Cup. The best thing is to trust our process and trust ourselves. We need to be clear about how we want to impose ourselves and I think that is all visible.’

Now it is time for him to show that he can find a way past the limitations of England’s footballing DNA, find a way to compete with Spain and France when it really matters, and find a way to end the culture of near misses that has come to be England’s lot in the last decade of appearances in semi-finals and finals.

England have played six matches since that day of crushing disappointment in Atlanta and scored 22 goals. But in the only one of those matches that really mattered, they lost 3-2 to Spain at Wembley in the opening tie of their Nations League campaign at the end of September, a game in which they were largely outclassed by Luis de la Fuente’s team.

Spain are what England have to aim for. Tuchel mentioned their example and their ability and their mindset straight after the semi-final loss to Argentina. ‘Ball possession plays a crucial role,’ he said at his post-match press conference in Atlanta. ‘It’s maybe not in our DNA like it is in our Spanish DNA or in our Argentinian-Brazilian DNA, to take the ball and control the game with the ball.’

This may well be their toughest game until the final of the 2028 European Championships, if they get that far

The England coach said more recently that England need to go back to trusting a traditional style that emphasises direct, high-intensity physicality rather than trying to copy Spanish patience in ball-retention. England, though, were taught a lesson in sophistication by the Spanish in September.

And for all the attention lavished on Yamal, Spain’s defence is the best in the world. Rodri, the shield for that defence and also the world’s best in the role, is not fit for this game but even without him, Spain’s back-line inspires an awful lot more confidence than England’s.

‘They were the best in the World Cup at the back,’ Declan Rice, England’s central midfielder, said on Saturday. ‘Defence wins you titles. Everyone talks about their attacking talent but you look at their central defenders, their full backs and the way their midfielders contribute to the defence, too.’

That defence will have to stop England’s resurgent front line, led by Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane, who could be flanked by Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers and backed up by the supreme talent of Jude Bellingham just behind them.

Bellingham’s improving relationship with Tuchel, which cannot have been harmed by the inclusion of Bellingham’s brother, Jobe, in this squad, is another reason to hope that England still retain the capacity to improve after the World Cup. The elder Bellingham has become England’s most influential player.

England at their best would be one of the few teams capable of extending them. Rice said on Saturday that the game between the two sides was ‘massive’. England need to prove they can find a way to get closer to the world champions. To beat them, Rice said, would be a ‘massive statement’.

‘Playing against them is a great incentive to win. It will show where we are as a group. We are trying to attack teams full throttle and with players like Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers in our attack, it feels as if it is going to take off one night and maybe tomorrow night will be the night. We can beat Spain. For sure, we can.’

Tuchel needs to prove England can win, not just be noble contenders. They need to prove that their DNA need not be a curse.

Sports.title: Declan Rice bites back at Graeme Souness: Arsenal star claims pundit doesn't understand how the game has evolved over 'old man's football' criticism - and jokes: 'My numbers aren't bad "for a centre-back!"'
Sports.content:
Declan Rice bites back at Graeme Souness: Arsenal star claims pundit doesn't understand how the game has evolved over 'old man's football' criticism - and jokes: 'My numbers aren't bad "for a centre-back!"'

Declan Rice has laughed off criticism from Graeme Souness by claiming his numbers 'aren't bad for a centre back', after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' and 'cheating' by dropping into defence.

Souness has long believed the Arsenal and England star does not do enough for a midfielder and said recently he might as well play centre back, adding that he would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Rice is aware of what Souness has said but believes his return of 22 goals and 33 assists since joining the Gunners in 2023 disproves the former Liverpool midfielder's opinion.

‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves,’ said Rice. ‘For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’

Rice, who will start as an advanced midfielder when England take on Spain here in Madrid on Sunday night, added: ‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’

Rice also believes Souness, 73, may not understand how the game has evolved.

England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has laughed off Graeme Souness' criticism after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' 'cheating' by dropping into defence

Pundit Souness believes Rice would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man's football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ began Rice. 'We played him the other week and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball. The game is different now. It's what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It's changed a lot, and you're always trying to look for tactical advantages.

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I'm constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He's constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we're now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There's no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he's done.

‘I didn't get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I've never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’

Sports.title: England pulverise Japan 78-15: Five-try Will Joseph twists knife into old boss Eddie Jones to pass early World Cup audition with flying colours
Sports.content:
England pulverise Japan 78-15: Five-try Will Joseph twists knife into old boss Eddie Jones to pass early World Cup audition with flying colours

What a cruel twist of fate that one of Eddie Jones’ teenage apprentices came back to twist the knife.

Will Joseph was still living in the Harlequins academy house when Jones invited him to train with the senior England team in 2022.

Joseph felt like he had won the lottery, fast-tracked into a squad with the likes of Owen Farrell and Danny Care.

Jones rewarded his efforts in training with a two-minute cameo against Australia but he had to wait more than four years for his second cap.

It finally came this weekend, against Jones’s Japan, as the centre-cum-winger scored five tries on a ruthless night at Twickenham.

Only Douglas Lambert (1907), Rory Underwood (1989), Josh Lewsey (2003) and Henry Arundell (2023) have achieved such a feat.

‘Today was a very special day,’ said Joseph. ‘I loved every minute of it. I’m pretty speechless. It was almost a perfect day'

Cadan Murley goes over for England in a swashbuckling first half at Allianz Twickenham

The power of Ellis Genge (pictured after his try), Maro Itoje and George Martin set up this win

On the bench, England’s replacements were even plotting to put Joseph on the back of their dominant driving maul in a bid to score a record-breaking sixth.

This game was billed as an early World Cup audition.

Steve Borthwick has already pencilled down circa 26 players for his 33-man World Cup squad and this was a shot for his fringe players to stake their claim.

Without question, Joseph was the standout, although it is worth remembering that his opposite man, Riku Tokito, had not played a single game of professional rugby.

Joseph was allowed freedom to roam but not once was he blinded by the spotlight of a full house in South West London.

He showed similar composure to his older brother, Jonathan, who won 54 caps for England between 2012 and 2020.

These days, Joseph Sr is one of the stadium comperes at Twickenham. At half-time, he spoke of his pride for his younger brother and reflected on the long and challenging journey towards his second cap.

‘Today was a very special day,’ said Joseph, when interviewed by his sibling. ‘I loved every minute of it. I’m pretty speechless. It was almost a perfect day. I was very grateful to get five tries in front of my family and friends.’

In the midfield, marginalised centre Max Ojomoh did everything that was asked of him

Joseph was left without a club after London Irish went bust, unused at Harlequins before finally finding his feet in the midfield at Gloucester.

Anyone who has watched the Cherry and Whites this season knows all about Joseph’s box-office skills.

He has established a silky centre partnership with Seb Atkinson, who missed out on this Japanese demolition because of a hip injury.

Joseph has the ability to cover both wing and centre and, in the era of versatility, this was a performance that should see him moved into Borthwick’s list of World Cup probables. When George Furbank is fit and firing – and ready to provide No10 cover from full-back – then Joseph could challenge Marcus Smith for England’s No23 jersey.

There would be no complaints if Joseph is now fast-tracked into the squad to take on the All Blacks next week.

He showcased his speed, footwork and vision – with his fifth try coming from an interception inside his own half.

While it was Joseph’s name in lights, the platform for this victory was laid by the power of Ellis Genge, Maro Itoje and George Martin. They muscled up from the start, with Japan lock Harry Hockings shown a 20-minute red card in the first minute.

Japan were hoping to take inspiration from Wales’ famous victory over the All Blacks but lightning never looked like striking twice. England pulverised Japan with their size and power, subjecting their old master Jones to a night that he would rather forget.

‘It kills me, that Will Joseph,’ laughed Jones. ‘I gave him his first cap and he scores five tries against me. That’s not very loyal, is it? He’s a great kid, he was always going to be a great player. Sometime you’ve got to do something for someone else. Hopefully Steve will give me some of his muesli and yoghurt.’
