Sports.title: Russell partners with BRDC to launch karting academy
Sports.content:
Formula 1 star George Russell has launched a karting academy in partnership with Silverstone to make motorsport more accessible and discover the next young superstar.

The eight-time grand prix winner launched his GR63 Karting Academy on Thursday with it open to boys and girls aged eight to nine, based at the kart track in Silverstone.

It features a “four stage path to the top” and will start in December with an open-access format inviting every eligible driver to Silverstone, where 80 will be selected for stage two.

That will see the 80 drivers compete in the “GR63 Shootout” on 31 January to determine the 25 slots for an eight-round championship at Silverstone from March to November in 2027.

The championship is fully-funded for each driver and the top five will go head-to-head in stage four next December, where the winner will receive a fully-funded karting campaign in 2028.

“Karting is where it all started for me,” said Russell, who won titles on a national and international level before progressing into single-seater competition.

“It taught me everything I’ve relied on throughout my career. I know how hard it is for talented young drivers to get that first opportunity, especially when budgets are tight.

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT images via Getty Images

“With the GR63 Karting Academy, I want to give something back by finding those hidden talents and giving them the support and platform they need to reach their potential.

“I'm really grateful to Silverstone and the British Racing Drivers’ Club for helping make this happen."

The academy is designed for those who “may not have the budget required to progress through the sport” with the costs in motorsport, both at grassroots level and at the top, increasing.

So costs to enter the academy’s opening stage are £25 with that rising to £75 for the “GR63 Shootout”, before everything is fully-funded from stage three onwards.

BRDC president David Coulthard said: “As owners of Silverstone and guardians of British motorsport, the BRDC has always been committed to reinvesting in the sport and nurturing home-grown talent.

“That commitment has played a big part in Britain’s long record of success in motorsport, and it is a great source of pride for the Club and its Members.

“The GR63 Academy captures that ethos perfectly, and we are delighted to work with George to support the next generation of drivers here at Silverstone."

All drivers must be a citizen of a commonwealth country and to book oneself for stage one, an arrive and drive session, click the link for the Silverstone website here.

Sports.title: Lawson to stay in F1 as Racing Bulls announces 2027 driver pairing
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed Liam Lawson will stay with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 campaign, partnering Arvid Lindblad for a second, straight season.

They have formed a formidable duo this year having propelled Racing Bulls to fifth in the championship, which is set to be the Anglo-Italian team's best-ever result.

Despite sitting on 89 points, however, compared to 38 for rookie Lindblad, Lawson's future was in doubt thanks to junior driver Nikola Tsolov starring in F2 this year.

The 19-year-old Bulgarian is second in the standings and has been handed private testing opportunities and a rookie FP1 session in Mexico as part of his junior driver duties.

So Racing Bulls was weighing up its need for short-term performance against its explicit goal of training young drivers for parent team Red Bull.

But with Lawson rising to the occasion in recent weeks, performing some of his strongest races under constant pressure, the 24-year-old has effectively been too good for the team to ignore.

Nikola Tsolov Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Sources indicated to Autosport in Brazil last weekend that amid a big push for the company's top leadership to back Tsolov, the pendulum swung back towards Lawson's favour with his performances over the Americas triple-header.

Read Also: Formula 1 How the Racing Bulls pendulum is swinging back towards Lawson

So the Kiwi has now signed a fresh deal for 2027 with team boss Alan Permane saying he had "no doubt" that the squad will field the strongest possible line-up next season.

"We’re delighted to be continuing with Liam and Arvid for 2027," he said. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we’ve seen the progress they’ve made, both individually and as a pairing.

“I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027."

Next year is set to be Lawson’s third, full season in F1 having made his debut at Zandvoort towards the back end of the 2023 campaign - having another partial season in 2024.

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

"I’m very happy to be continuing with Visa Cash App Racing Bulls next year,” he said. “We’ve had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I’ve loved driving.

“It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for P5 in the constructors' championship. It's a testament to the hard work of everyone both at track, and back at the factory.

"I’m looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027. We’re building something super positive and I’m excited by what we can achieve together.”

Lawson is currently eighth in the drivers’ standings with Lindblad in 11th ahead of the final three rounds: Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

"Looking back on my first season in Formula 1, it's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test," said 19-year-old Lindblad.

"I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season. It's set to be an exciting year, and I look forward to continuing to drive alongside Liam."

Sports.title: What the Brazilian GP revealed about F1's ability to cope with rain
Sports.content:
The question of what might happen in a wet race has vexed Formula 1's stakeholders since before the beginning of the season. It's also prompted some unnecessarily hysterical commentary throughout the year, peaking in the run-up to last weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos, where rain for qualifying and the race was a virtual certainty for the first time this season.

Although the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was interrupted by rain and the discovery of a software glitch, by the time the race got going the track was drying quickly. This was not the case in Brazil.

Qualifying at Interlagos was red-flagged for 80 minutes after a downpour coincided with the start of the session, and many media outlets alighted on a spicy George Russell quote in the aftermath.

"I love driving in the rain here but, at some point, if that was a race, there was no way we should be driving in that because the chances of seeing a really, really horrific incident are very, very high," he said.

Perfect headline material for a noisy story, but context was lacking. The general consensus within the paddock after that session was that the FIA made the right calls at the right time, immediately suspending Q1 during the initial downpour, then applying great rigour to identify a safe ‘window' to restart it.

"In general, I want to race, but yesterday [Saturday] I think it was the perfect call," said Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur after the race. "When we did the first [Q1] lap before the red flag, we came back with two centimetres of water in the car…"

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Carlos Sainz, Williams, Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Those conditions were too wet to stage any kind of track activity beyond a boat race in the pitlane. The real questions surrounded how the cars and the latest generation of tyres would perform in the kind of wet and/or rapidly changing circumstances in which qualifying and the race could actually be staged.

Historically, Pirelli's heavily treaded ‘extreme' wet tyres are rarely seen, since too much of their operating window sits outside the margin of what is considered to be acceptable racing conditions. They displace massive quantities of water but the tread blocks overheat too quickly as the track dries. By the time the track is wet enough to justify the ‘extreme' tyre, a red flag is usually imminent.

The intermediate tyres have therefore been the wet-weather boots of choice, but this year's are understood to be too ‘hard' and slow to come up to operating temperature. Pirelli just hasn't been able to accomplish like-for-like running with the narrower wheels mandated for this season, given the testing restrictions.

It's long been feared that lack of grip from the new intermediates, combined with the more brutal torque delivery of the latest generation of engines, would make the 2026 F1 cars dangerously undriveable in the wet. Hence the outbreak of hysteria ahead of the Brazil weekend.

What actually transpired was less dramatic, and more nuanced. The nature of the track surface at Interlagos meant driveability was occasionally an issue, but not always. In the background, the FIA has been doing a lot of work since the beginning of the year to manage power delivery in these conditions.

Alexander Albon, Williams, Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

While qualifying – once it got started – offered some hope that the ‘extreme' wets are now more useable, the intermediates were a little more problematic. Kimi Antonelli went off at Turn 12 on his lap to the grid, and several other drivers reported their cars became a handful again when rain in the last 10 laps dictated a return to the intermediates.

"I think what is good is that we can use the 'big wet' much more than in the past," said Vasseur. "And this is good because it's not pushing you to use inter when it's a more 'big wet' situation, or mix between the two, and then you are taking risks.

"I think the quali was pretty good… but also the grip was completely different. You saw in the lap to the grid today that everybody was completely like hell. I think it's a difficult track with these conditions."

Pirelli's target for next year is to bring the performance of the wet-weather compounds closer together, so the intermediate warms up faster and the ‘extreme' is more resistant to wear. But this is a challenge to engineer because the tracks differ so much in terms of the energy going through the tyres.

"It was difficult to fire them up but they also wore quite quickly," said Alex Albon, who finished 15th in Brazil.

"So even when they're cold, they're wearing and it just feels like they never overheat, or they never level up to temperature. And then by the time you're circulating, the tread's already come off the tyre and then you're already struggling, you're sliding around. So, you never feel good at any point in the race; it never feels like it comes alive."

This would explain some of the peculiarities of the opening laps, where those at the front of the grid found themselves having to be super-cautious because they couldn't feel the grip – while some of those towards the rear, who spent less time waiting for lights-out, got strong getaways.

Even among those there was a variance: Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton quickly broke through to the top 10 from 20th and 21st on the grid, only for Hamilton to then go backwards as his car developed massive oversteer snaps. Verstappen, like Antonelli, then found his car less performant on the slicks.

Wet conditions added to the drama of qualifying Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

This mixed spread of performance over the wet and dry tyre compounds will be tricky to unpick, but the consensus remained that the wet-weather rubber needs more development. There were minor gripes but not the disasters that were feared and noisily predicted.

"I think the level of the wet and the inter is not good enough and we need to work with Pirelli on finding a better tyre," said Carlos Sainz, "because in the mixed conditions the inter is still a very weak tyre at the rear. By the time it warms up, the front is gone.

"And the extreme, honestly, yesterday we had so much sliding and a big lack of rear grip, so still missing a bit of development on these two tyres."

While the data gathered through running in many different conditions this weekend will be useful, it's still an isolated example. What worked or didn't work at Interlagos may not translate elsewhere, given variances in surfaces and ambient temperatures.

"Quite tricky I would say," was Liam Lawson's take on racing in the wet in a 2026 F1 car.

"The biggest problem today is the [ambient] temperature was much cooler than yesterday. And so even though there was less water, on the laps of the grid the cars were nearly undriveable, and the temps were just going down.

"So, we survived the start of the race but at points when it rains a lot, the inter becomes... it's not that the standing water's too much, it's that you can't actually keep the temperature in it. So, if we're on a track like Vegas and it rains, honestly, I think we're in trouble.

"But overall, obviously we got through a weekend for the first time with these tyres."

Additional reporting by Roberto Chinchero and Guilherme Longo

Sports.title: F1 2026 calendar update: Imola off the table, no plan B if Iran war escalates
Sports.content:
The Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix which will conclude Formula 1’s 2026 season are set to proceed as planned, provided there is no dramatic escalation of the Iran war.

The Middle Eastern conflict, which started in late February as the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, has destabilised the region. The calendars of many motorsport championships have been impacted – not least F1’s, whose Saudi Arabian race was cancelled while Bahrain’s round was postponed and hosted in Malaysia.

F1 has been monitoring the situation closely, with a chilly Imola as an alternative season finale on the first weekend of December if Qatar and Abu Dhabi were unable to host their respective events.

Lusail did run its MotoGP round without major issues last weekend, though both Yamaha teams withdrew from the competition due to the geopolitical situation.

10 November was F1’s deadline to provide Imola with a final answer as to whether the Italian track would have to prepare for a grand prix in the next three weeks; it will not.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls Photo by: Zak Mauger / Motorsport Images

So the 2026 season will end with the planned Las Vegas-Qatar-Abu Dhabi triple-header, with travel insurance and governments’ travel advice currently allowing it.

However, there’s a caveat: F1 is aware it cannot guarantee the situation won’t change by early December and insists it will prioritise safety if the conflict escalates.

Team bosses have been maintaining a straightforward stance on the matter – they trust F1 and the FIA to make the right calls.

“I trust them to take the best decision for all of us,” Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur commented in Mexico. “Me, personally, I want to race. It doesn't matter where, but I want to race. Now, I will go where they will tell us to go.”

“Stefano and Mohammed have been pretty clear about the situation that Formula 1 follows what the international guidelines are, whether there are travel restrictions, airlines not flying, any warnings in the region, the kind of feedback that local governments are making,” his Mercedes counterpart Toto Wolff added in Friday’s press conference at Interlagos. “So not only the promoters, but what the local governments are making. And this is what you need to rely on, in my opinion, and I'm fully with that.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“I think that if riders stand up, who know nothing geopolitically about what's going on, but have an audience that listens, I think that is something that creates media value. But I would have done the same as MotoGP management has done. You want to ride or drive, go. If you don't want to, don't go. It's as simple as that, and everybody can take their personal decisions on that, and I respect that.

“Of course, you've got to be wary of what's happening in the next few days, a few weeks, and Stefano has his finger on the pulse to monitor that. If things were to get more dangerous and we would get that feedback, then he's going to be the first one, together with Mohammed, to protect the people that were meant to travel. So that's why I'm following their guidance.

“From what I'm hearing internally, it hasn't been raised. It hasn't been a topic. But also there, if someone feels they don't feel comfortable, he or she doesn't feel comfortable travelling, then it's something that I would always respect. And maybe that's an opportunity to give somebody else a chance. It wouldn't change anything for the relationship. I've always respected that some people didn't want to go to certain grands prix, and that's how I see it at the moment.”

Additional reporting by Ronald Vording

Sports.title: Ignore social media echo chamber and trust F1 over Middle East races – Wolff | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says Formula 1 is right to go ahead with its plans to race in the Middle East.

Many sports including other motor racing series cancelled events in the region due to the US-Iran war. However F1 commercial rights holder Liberty Media held its Moto GP event in Qatar last weekend, despite one manufacturer staying away due to concerns over the safety of travelling to the region.

F1 confirmed this week it has abandoned its back-up plan to relocate the final round of 2026 to Imola in Italy if its planned events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi cannot go ahead.

Wolff said those questioning the wisdom of racing in the Middle East should pay less attention to media coverage and listen to those in charge of the series.

“For me, with our social media feed, we are always at risk of seeing what we want to see,” he told the BBC. “I believe you need to trust what the authorities say. You need to rely on the commercial rights holder, that’s F1, and the FIA as our governing body.”

However Wolff said no staff will be forced to attend the final two rounds and anyone choosing not to could hand an opportunity to a replacement.

“I strongly support that if someone doesn’t want to go to Qatar or Abu Dhabi, personally doesn’t want to, then I’m very fine with that,” he said. “We don’t want to oblige anyone. There’s not going to be any sanctions, or so on, on teams.

“If you don’t feel right about going there, then I have respect for that, and don’t go. It gives an opportunity maybe to someone else to be tested and to see how another person would perform in the future. That’s how I would approach it.”

Sports.content:
The Daily Mail says the FIA has barred its Formula 1 reporter from attending the final three rounds of the world championship as a media representative.

It quotes a letter sent yestreday by FIA general manager Alberto Villareal regarding an article the newspaper published about Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc , whom its F1 correspondent Jonathan McEvoy called a “sneaky little b*****d”.

“The FIA considers that your article falls short of the standards of professionalism expected of media representatives accredited to cover the FIA Formula One World Championship,” said Villareal, quoted by the newspaper.

“Accordingly, the FIA has decided to exercise its discretion under the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship Accreditation Guidelines to withdraw your media accreditation for the remainder of the 2026 season, with immediate effect.”

Three rounds of the season remain in the USA, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Earlier this year Max Verstappen ordered the removal of another journalist, Giles Richards of The Guardian, from a Red Bull press conference. Verstappen was unhappy Richards asked him three months earlier whether he regretted colliding with George Russell during last year’s Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Grosjean admits his single-seater career is likely over after ending IndyCar season 19th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 driver Romain Grosjean, who survived a fireball crash six years ago in Bahrain, is preparing to call time on his single-seater racing career.

Grosjean raced in F1 between 2009 and 2020, then switched to IndyCar. He completed his fifth season in the series this year but the 40-year-old admits he is unlikely to return.

“The reality is, this is probably the end for me with single-seaters,” Grosjean told Racer.

Grosjean finished on the podium three times in his first season in IndyCar with Coyne, earning the attention of top team Andretti, who hired him for the 2022 season. The team replaced him after he finished 13th in the championship for two years running,

After spending one year at Juncos Hollinger, Grosjean lost his drive for 2025, but returned with Coyne this year. The season began promisingly when he reached the final round of qualifying in St Petersburg, but a string of finishes outside the top 10 followed.

The Coyne driver finished on the podium just once all year. He ended the season 19th in the standings ahead of just six other full-time drivers, including RLL’s Mick Schumacher, who replaced him at Haas in 2021.

Grosjean said it had been a “tough” season overall. “I had [a] few amazing moments. I got the chance to lead the Indy 500. I finished in the top 10. I ran [in] the top five most of the last 60 laps. Amazing! I got a podium in Markham, which was incredible with my ‘tractor.’

“But then we go to Milwaukee and Laguna Seca, and [at] Laguna Seca, I qualified dead last, almost. I know it’s one of my fastest tracks, so I’m like, ‘I don’t want that anymore.’ I’ve had enough of those moments where you just don’t have the tools to play.”

Grosjean was supposed to contest his final grand prix at Abu Dhabi in 2020. However the burns he suffered in his Bahrain crash forced him out early. His former team Haas gave him the opportunity to test one of its cars at Mugello last year.

Sports.title: Court of Appeal to hear Audi’s case over Tsunoda decision on November 25th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The International Court of Appeal has set a date to hear Audi’s appeal over the Italian Grand Prix stewards’ decision regarding Yuki Tsunoda.

Audi is challenging the decision not to penalise Tsunoda, who finished the race in 10th position, for triggering an extra formation lap before the start of the race.

The ICA will hear the case on November 25th at the FIA’s headquarters in Paris.

Tsunoda, who substituted for Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson at Monza, finished seven seconds ahead of Gabriel Bortoleto. Therefore the Audi driver could gain a point if Tsunoda is penalised.

Bortoleto previously said Audi’s case was “straightforward”.

F1’s sporting regulations state any driver who causes an extra formation lap must start the race from the pit lane and will receive a Stop-and-Go penalty if they fail to. As Tsunoda did not start from the pit lane, Audi believes he should receive a penalty.

The stewards ruled Tsunoda “was not the ’cause’ of the extra formation lap” and therefore did not have to start from the pit lane.

This is the second time this year the ICA has been asked to rule on a decision taken by the stewards at a grand prix. In September they reinstated two penalties which were originally issued to Pierre Gasly during the Monaco Grand Prix and later rescinded.

ICA hearing announcement

On 6th September 2026, at the end of the formation lap during the race restart following a red flag, the race director ordered an additional formation lap Following the race, the stewards investigated a potential breach of Article B5.9.4 of the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations by Mr Yuki Tsunoda (driver of car number 22), which requires any driver who caused an extra formation lap to start from the end of the pit lane. Failure to do so, a Stop-and-Go penalty should be imposed on the driver. In decision number 69, the stewards decided to take no further action against Mr Yuki Tsunoda. On 9th September 2026, Audi Revolut F1 Team lodged an appeal against that decision, arguing that Mr Yuki Tsunoda had caused the extra formation lap and should therefore have received the prescribed Stop-and-Go penalty.

Sports.title: Racing Bulls keep Lawson and Lindblad as Tsolov gets Red Bull reserve role | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed an unchanged driver line-up for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad will continue to drive for the team next year.

The news ends speculation Red Bull’s second Formula 1 team would replace either of its drivers with Nikola Tsolov. The Red Bull junior driver lies second in the Formula 2 standings with four races remaining.

Shortly after Racing Bulls confirmed its driver line-up, Red Bull announced Tsolov as its reserve driver for 2027. Red Bull also announced Tsolov will be Racing Bulls’ reserve driver.

Racing Bulls is on course to score its best championship result under any of its identities, including its time competing as Minardi, before it was purchased by Red Bull at the end of 2005.

However Lawson’s future at the team came into doubt as Racing Bulls delayed its decision on its driver line-up for next year. Lawson made his F1 debut in 2023 and gained promotion to Red Bull in 2025 but the team dropped him after just two rounds. Lawson made a temporary return to Red Bull this year as a substitute for the injured Isack Hadjar.

During his time at Racing Bulls, Lawson has scored enough points to single-handedly put Racing Bulls fifth in the constructors’ championship. However he clashed with Red Bull driver Max Verstappen during a practice session in Mexico earlier this month, which his rival said was “not very smart behaviour” for a driver who was “fighting for [his] seat”. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies denied his team would have any say in its junior squad’s driver line-up.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane said Lawson and his rookie team mate Lindblad form “the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition”.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027.”

Tsolov said he hopes to make the step up to F1 after next year. “My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver,” he said. “Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting.

“I’m confident that with the team’s support and experience, I’ll have the best possible preparation to make sure I’m fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes.”

Mekies said Red Bull has been highly impressed by Tsolov. “Nikola is an exceptionally talented young driver, and we have been hugely impressed by his development and performances over the past few years,” he said.

“To fight for the championship in F3 and now challenge for the F2 title in his first full season says a great deal about his ability and determination. What has impressed us just as much is his maturity, his approach to racing and his willingness to keep learning and improving.

“We have enormous belief in Nikola’s potential and see him as a driver with a very exciting future in F1. This appointment reflects our confidence in him and our commitment to his continued development. Our focus in 2027 will be on giving him the experience, tools and support he needs to be ready to race in F1 next.”

Sports.title: Pacheco and Fulghum Fight for a WBA Title Spot Stuck Behind Munguía
Sports.content:
The WBA lists tonight’s Diego Pacheco vs. Darius Fulghum fight in Carson, California, as a final eliminator at super middleweight. Winning it sounds like an immediate ticket to a championship bout, yet Jaime Munguía still owes Bektemir Melikuziev a mandatory defense, leaving the DAZN main event winner staring at a wait that could stretch into 2028.

In its November 12 preview, the WBA initially called the bout a title eliminator. Its official fight schedule now lists the contest as a final eliminator without attaching any timeline for when the winner actually gets his shot at the belt.

Melikuziev Gets the First Shot

Melikuziev earned his spot by beating Fulghum in an eliminator back in May 2025 and has been sitting on the shelf waiting for his turn ever since. After ordering Munguía to face him in September, the WBA turned around and allowed the champion to take a detour against Nikita Zon on October 31 in Riyadh after both sides struck an exception deal. Melikuziev kept his mandatory position, meaning tonight’s winner is only fighting to stand behind someone who has already waited a year and a half.

“He wins this fight, no matter how he wins. He wins this fight, keeps that unblemished record, he’s going to fight for a title next,” said Sergio Mora on DAZN, referring to Pacheco. Chris Mannix offered a far more realistic view, calling a 2027 title shot a possibility for either fighter.

Mora’s prediction ignores the traffic jam the WBA created at 168 pounds. A 2027 shot only works if Munguía and Melikuziev get in the ring early next year and the sanctioning body refuses to grant any more favors. If their fight drags into the second half of 2027, the Carson winner gets pushed straight into 2028. Even if Munguía beats Melikuziev, there is no guarantee the WBA enforces its own deadline promptly. Having already let Munguía squeeze in the Zon defense while Melikuziev waited, the WBA has shown it will bend its schedule whenever a champion wants an extra bout.

Eddie Hearn wants Pacheco to climb onto the turnbuckle after a win and call out Canelo Álvarez and Munguía. Pursuing another belt is likely the only way Mora’s prediction actually comes true for Pacheco, because waiting on the WBA queue could waste a full year of his prime. For Fulghum, the WBA route is even more backward. He could win a final eliminator tonight only to wait nearly two years for a rematch against the same fighter who already beat him in the last one.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames Outpoints Gerome Warburton in Riyadh
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames (26-1-1) beat Gerome Warburton (18-3-2) by unanimous decision Saturday in the 10-round main event of Zuffa Boxing 13 at The Venue in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Adames did his best work to the body, landing the heavier punches whenever he caught up with the retreating Welsh southpaw.

The judges scored it 100-90, 99-91 and 98-92 for Adames. Boxing News 24 scored it 100-90. The fight was contested at a 165-pound catchweight, as a non-title fight.

Adames finds his best work to the body

The opening round produced little clean work from either fighter. Adames set a slow pace and Warburton threw tentatively from the back foot, giving the champion room to follow him without taking many risks. In the second, Adames found the clearest scoring punches of the round with several right hands to the body.

Adames switched to southpaw in the third and sat down on hooks to both sides of Warburton’s body. It was his most sustained burst of offense in the early rounds, and his output dropped again when he went back to orthodox. The fourth and fifth passed at much the same pace as the opener, with Adames willing to take the rounds on a handful of clean punches and Warburton rarely committing to his own shots.

By the sixth, Warburton was making Adames chase him around the ring. The movement kept him out of range for stretches, but Adames landed hard to the body when he closed the distance. Warburton kept moving in the seventh, and Adames looked frustrated at times as the Welshman slipped away before the two could trade.

Warburton threw more in the eighth, using his punches mainly to keep Adames from getting close. There was little sustained offense behind them, and Adames went back to walking him down in the ninth. The final round followed the same pattern. Adames pressed at a steady pace and landed when he got close enough, while Warburton kept moving and rarely let his hands go.

Warburton came in off back-to-back decision wins over Nathan Heaney and faced a substantial step up against a reigning world champion. His movement made Adames work to get into range, but he seldom made Adames pay for coming forward. That left Adames free to choose when to press and when to settle for the work he had already done.

The win came in Adames’ Zuffa Boxing debut, five pounds above the middleweight limit. He is expected to return to 160 pounds for a mandatory defense against Meiirim Nursultanov, where his WBC belt would be on the line.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames vs Gerome Warburton Zuffa Live Results: Round-by-Round Updates
Sports.content:
Former WBO bantamweight champion Jason “Mayhem” Moloney (30-4, 20 KOs) defeated Andres Teran (19-3, 14 KOs) by unanimous decision in the 10-round bantamweight co-main event. The judges scored it 99-91, 98-92 and 97-93 for Moloney. Teran looked to counter in the early rounds and landed some solid shots in a cagey start.

The action picked up in the middle rounds as Teran pressed forward and both fighters had their moments. Moloney dictated the pace and landed the cleaner punches as the fight wore on. Teran came into the bout after stopping previously unbeaten Floyd Diaz in six rounds. The win came in the 35-year-old Australian’s Zuffa Boxing debut.

Bruno “Brunello” Surace (27-1-2) handed Kamil Bednarek (17-1, 10 KOs) his first professional loss by unanimous decision in a 10-round super middleweight bout. The judges scored it 98-92, 97-93 and 96-94 for Surace.

It was the Frenchman’s first fight in about 18 months, following his decision loss to Jaime Munguía in their May 2025 rematch.

Bednarek pressed forward and stayed busy, but he rarely troubled Surace with his power shots. Surace landed the cleaner punches from the early rounds, countering Bednarek as he came forward. He mixed shots to the head and body and kept Bednarek from getting much out of his pressure. Surace finished strongly to close out his Zuffa Boxing debut.

Heavyweight Jakhongir “Jak Kong” Zokirov (3-0) knocked out Brandon Colantonio (8-3) at 3:00 of the first round in a scheduled six-round fight. The 6-foot-7 Uzbek prospect hurt Colantonio to the body early. Colantonio got back to his feet, but Zokirov went back to the body and forced him to take a knee. The referee deducted a point from Zokirov for landing a punch while Colantonio was down.

Zokirov kept landing heavy shots after the action resumed. Colantonio’s corner stopped the fight before the start of the second round. It was the second straight stoppage win for the 23-year-old Zokirov, who stopped Zachary Spiller in two rounds in his previous fight.

Dariial “Wolf” Kuchmenov (11-0) handed Ivan Ortiz (13-1-2) his first professional loss by split decision in an eight-round lightweight bout. Two judges scored it 77-74 and 76-75 for Kuchmenov, while the third had it 76-75 for Ortiz.

Kuchmenov used his jab to control the distance early and dropped Ortiz with a counter hook as the Mexican came forward about two minutes into the first round. It was the first knockdown of Ortiz’s career.

Ortiz began landing more regularly midway through the third and caught Kuchmenov with a hard right hand late in the fourth. Kuchmenov regained the initiative by going to the body as Ortiz began to take control. The final two rounds went back and forth, with Kuchmenov holding on to win by a point on the closest card in his favor.

Light heavyweight Rakhmatullo “Tullo” Boymatov (2-0, 2 KOs) knocked out Moro Inusah Kanla (10-2, 9 KOs) at 1:29 of the first round in a scheduled eight-round bout. Both fighters traded heavy combinations from the opening bell.

Boymatov was first to touch the canvas, but the referee ruled it a slip. Moments later, Boymatov dropped Kanla with an overhand right. Kanla got up, but Boymatov caught him with a flush left hook that ended the fight.

Kanla had entered on a six-fight knockout streak. It was the second straight first-round stoppage for the 22-year-old Uzbek prospect, who stopped Caleb Hall in his pro debut in May.

Alexander Castro (16-2, 12 KOs) upset former WBA welterweight champion Radzhab Butaev (16-3, 12 KOs) by majority decision in a 10-round middleweight bout. Two judges scored it 97-93 and 96-94 for Castro. The third had it even at 95-95.

Butaev entered as the heavy favorite in the opening bout of the Zuffa Boxing 13 prelims. The Colombian underdog was coming off a loss. Castro’s win over the former champion was his first since that defeat.

Abdulaziz Alotaibi (1-0) won his professional debut by unanimous decision over Ezra Ssali in a four-round featherweight bout on the Zuffa Boxing 13 prelims. All three judges scored it 40-35 for Alotaibi. The 24-year-old controlled the bout against the Ugandan Ssali and won every round on all three cards.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Cornered by WBA Order for Melikuziev Fight
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía has 30 days to sign a deal with mandatory challenger Bektemir Melikuziev, and nobody watching the WBA’s circus at 168 pounds should hold their breath. For the last year, the sanctioning body has treated its own rules like optional suggestions, handing out soft exceptions while Melikuziev rots on the shelf for nearly 18 months waiting for the title shot he already earned.

ESPN’s Salvador Rodríguez reported Saturday that the two camps have a 30 day window to reach terms before the WBA orders a purse bid with a 60 percent split for Munguía and 40 percent for Melikuziev. That threat is completely toothless, because Munguía already blew past an October deadline once and got rewarded with a lucrative voluntary stroll against Nikita Zon instead of getting stripped.

Munguía won the WBA belt back on May 2 in Las Vegas with a unanimous decision over José Armando Reséndiz. His initial mandatory period expired on August 30, and the WBA Championship Committee waited until September 21 to officially order the Melikuziev fight with an October 21 deadline. Nine days after that deadline passed without a deal, the WBA caved and let Munguía take the Zon fight in Riyadh two weeks ago.

Melikuziev got pushed aside so Munguía could collect an easy payday in Saudi Arabia, all under the promise that the Uzbek southpaw would be next. Now the 30 day clock is ticking again, and there is zero guarantee Munguía will not look for another exit ramp or drag out negotiations until a purse bid forces his hand.

Meanwhile, the rest of the super middleweight division is stuck in traffic. Diego Pacheco and Darius Fulghum meet Saturday night in Carson, California, in a WBA eliminator that feels almost pointless right now. Whoever wins that fight is walking straight into a brick wall of sanctioning body delays. Even if Munguía and Melikuziev sign contracts tomorrow, a fight date still has to be locked in for early 2027, meaning the Carson winner will be lucky to get his shot before next summer.

Nobody knows that frustration better than Fulghum. Melikuziev edged him out 114 to 112 on all three scorecards in a Las Vegas eliminator back in May 2025, and Melikuziev still has not gotten his crack at the title. If Fulghum pulls off the upset in Carson and Melikuziev somehow topples Munguía, we could see a rematch for the belt. For Pacheco, winning Saturday just puts him at the back of a very slow line.

Munguía knows what is waiting for him if he actually steps into the ring with Melikuziev. Melikuziev is a heavy handed, relentless pressure fighter who punishes the body and suffocates opponents on the inside. After going twelve rounds with Zon, Munguía cannot afford to sleepwalk through camp if this bout finally gets across the finish line.

The WBA claims its order governs the title picture after Saturday night, but until Munguía and Melikuziev are both standing in the ring, fans should keep their expectations low.

Sports.title: Out of Sight: Crawford Lurks at Ennis Launch for Attention
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford gave fans another reason to talk about a fight with Jaron “Boots” Ennis just by showing up in Carson on Friday. The retired champion (42-0, 31 KOs) watched Ennis (35-0, 31 KOs) and Josh Kelly (17-1-1, 9 KOs) face off at their kickoff press conference at Dignity Health Sports Park, two months after telling Boots he still had more to prove at 154 pounds.

Ennis puts his WBA and WBO junior middleweight titles up against IBF champion Kelly on February 27 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. Crawford, 39, walked away from the sport after beating Canelo Alvarez last year. Speaking with reporters after Friday’s launch, Crawford said Boots could become undisputed at 154 pounds, admitted he was unimpressed by WBC champion Sebastian Fundora’s last performance, and picked Ennis to stop Kelly within seven rounds. When asked directly about coming out of retirement, Crawford shut the door by saying, “I’m done,” twice.

That doesn’t matter much in boxing. If Turki Alalshikh waves a bunch of cash in front of Crawford’s face, he is not likely to say no to it. Promoters know how quickly “I’m done” turns into a training camp once serious money hits the table.

At the same time, you can’t blame Crawford if he still refuses the offer. He fancies himself as being among the Mount Rushmore of boxing as one of the best ever, and fighting a prime, explosive 29-year-old like Ennis could ruin all that with a bad loss. Heck, Crawford nearly got beat by a stationary Canelo last year, and many fans believe he was gifted a decision over Israil Madrimov in 2024. He looked terrible in that fight, getting lit up with right hands all night while struggling to deal with Madrimov’s movement.

At this point, it has to be eating Crawford up hearing all the gushing from fans about Ennis while people stop talking about him due to his inactivity. Boxing fans move on fast the second a fighter stops competing.

It wouldn’t have to be this way if Crawford had stuck around and faced younger lions like Ennis at 154, or tested himself against dangerous talents at 168; he would still be the center of attention instead of lurking in the crowd at press conferences to stay in the mix.

Showing up in Carson works well for Crawford right now. He gets to stay in the middle of the biggest 154-pound conversations, keep his name tied to a potential undisputed champion, and see what Turki Alalshikh is willing to pay without putting his unbeaten record on the line. If Boots collects a third belt in Atlanta, Eddie Hearn will have another reason to bring up Crawford’s name, and the price tag will only go up.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Chases Ryan Garcia Loophole to Escape Jack Catterall Nightmare
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez wants nothing to do with Jack Catterall right now, and who can blame him when a massive payday against Ryan Garcia is sitting right there on the table for February 6. According to Mike Coppinger, the WBA has notified the camps that Lopez can apply for a special permit to unify with WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia, which would move mandatory challenger Jack Catterall to the back of the line once again.

It’s understandable why Teofimo (22-1, 13 KOs) is looking for a way around Catterall. Stylistically, Catterall (30-2, 13 KOs) is pure poison for Lopez. We have seen this movie plenty of times whenever Teofimo steps in the ring with a slick, negative southpaw or a defensive counterpuncher who refuses to stand in front of him.

Look at how lost and miserable Lopez looked against Sandor Martin and Jamaine Ortiz, where he spent half the night swinging at air and looking totally frustrated because nobody would trade with him. Catterall fights that exact same spoiling, hit-and-not-get-hit style, and he has the timing to make Lopez look awful or even steal a decision on the scorecards.

Ryan Garcia (25-2, 20 KOs) is the complete opposite. Garcia stands right in front of you, keeps his chin up, and leaves wide-open lanes for counter right hands and left hooks. For Lopez, fighting Garcia is a golden ticket to a massive purse and a highlight-reel shootout, whereas taking the Catterall mandatory first risks blowing the whole February 6 promotion before it even gets off the ground.

Eddie Hearn Threatens Legal Action Over the Belt

Of course, Catterall’s promoter, Eddie Hearn, is furious and threatening legal action if the sanctioning body lets Lopez bypass his fighter while keeping the strap.

“I would sue them immediately,” Hearn said on Inside the Ring.

Hearn had already predicted that Lopez would vacate the WBA belt if forced to defend against Catterall. Keeping the title gives Lopez serious leverage at the negotiating table with Garcia’s team, allowing him to pitch a two-belt unification and demand a much bigger slice of the revenue. Even as a three-division champion with plenty of name value, walking into negotiations without a belt weakens his bargaining power. Fans buying tickets or ordering the event barely care whether one belt or two is on the line, since they are tuning in to see Lopez and Garcia trade bombs, but for Lopez’s bank account, that strap matters plenty.

The WBA Timeline Mess Leaves Catterall Waiting

For Catterall, this endless waiting game is getting ridiculous. He earned his shot back on May 23 by beating Shakhram Giyasov for the WBA Regular title, under terms that were supposed to guarantee him a shot at the full champion within 180 days. That deadline points right to November 19. Instead, Rolly Romero held the belt for over 15 months without fighting Giyasov, lost a majority decision to Lopez on August 22, and now Lopez is trying to kick the can down the road into 2027.

Even though the WBA reaffirmed its September 22 order on November 11 and gave the sides a 10-day window to reach a deal or head to a purse bid, everybody knows how sanctioning bodies operate when huge money is involved. The WBA collects its 3% sanctioning fee from both fighters, and a Garcia vs. Lopez clash brings in vastly more cash than a mandatory defense against Catterall. Chris Mannix also reported that Lopez’s team already filed a unification permit request on November 5, meaning the wheels are already turning behind closed doors.

Spring Megafights Could Freeze Catterall Out Until 2027

If the WBA caves and grants this exception, Catterall is left holding a worthless paper title shot. Worse yet, if Garcia beats Lopez on February 6, you can bet Garcia will immediately chase mega-fights against names like Devin Haney, Conor Benn, or Mario Barrios in the spring rather than bothering with a low-reward mandatory against Catterall. Unless the WBA actually enforces its own rules for once, Catterall is going to spend another year sitting on the sidelines watching everybody else cash in.

Sports.title: Bradley Urges Shakur Stevenson to Take Hearn Fights Without Signing
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley recommends that Shakur Stevenson find out ahead of time what fights he can get, but not sign with his Matchroom company. Stay a free agent and fight twice for Hearn, and then move on.

The pickings are kind of slim for Shakur with Matchroom, though. Even if he doesn’t sign with them, there aren’t superstar fighters that will provide him the kind of money that he was reportedly asking for when he was signed with Zuffa.

He wanted $15 million per fight and reportedly turned down a $7 million offer to fight Raymond Muratalla. If Shakur cares about money, the biggest payday he potentially gets is fighting Jaron ‘Boots’ Ennis, but he might have to go up to junior middleweight to make that fight.

Given the big production Stevenson made about wanting a 144-lb catchweight for a fight with Devin Haney, he probably won’t be excited to move up to 154 to face a puncher like Ennis.

Bradley wants Shakur to try and get a deal with DAZN that would allow him to work with other promoters on their platform. From there, he could fight the opponent he wants that competes on that network. The big question is whether DAZN would support the paydays Shakur wants.

Hearn brought up the idea of Shakur focusing on the undisputed championship at 140, which would put him in fights against Raymond Muratalla, Dalton Smith, Gary Antuanne Russell, and whoever wins the vacant IBF title.

The immediate question is whether Shakur fights Muratalla or gives up his WBO light welterweight belt. That would be the second straight fighter he chose not to face after he failed to make a deal with Devin Haney.

“I don’t want to be, you know, solely tied to you, but let me get these two fights. Once I get done here, I can move on to do work with another promoter,” said Bradley to Fighthub TV, describing how he would have Stevenson approach those talks. “That way it’ll be easier for him to make fights, right? “Okay, Eddie, what do you got for me? Who do you got?”

Matchroom has some good fighters, but not the ones that would lead to the type of purses Shakur was hoping for. He was paid well for his last two fights on Turki Alalshikh’s cards, getting $10 million for Teofimo Lopez and $7 million for William Zepeda, according to Sportster.com and SalarySports.com.

Perhaps the best piece of advice Bradley gave Shakur was for him to fight more often, because the ideal way to increase his popularity to get the kind of paydays that he was hoping for at Zuffa. Fighting once a year isn’t going to get it. In 2026, Shakur has only fought once, beating Teofimo.

Ghana News.title: Daniel Niibi Afotey Odai elected NDC Greater Accra Deputy Youth Organiser
Ghana News.content:
Daniel Niibi Afotey Odai has been elected Deputy Regional Youth Organiser of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Greater Accra Region after narrowly defeating three other contenders in the party’s regional executive elections.

Niibi secured 45 votes in the election held on Saturday, November 14, 2026, edging his closest challenger, Atsu Eric Afeme, who polled 44 votes.

Jones Klutse obtained 32 votes, while Rashid Isah secured eight.

The result gives Niibi a new role in the party’s regional youth leadership as the NDC continues its internal reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general elections.

Niibi’s political career began at the branch level. He served for eight years as Deputy Youth Organiser for the Krowor Constituency, where he was involved in youth mobilisation and organising party structures.

He holds a degree in Political Science from the University of Ghana and is a Chartered Manager.

He is also the District Director of the Youth Employment Agency (YEA) in Krowor, where his work involves connecting young people to employment, skills development and other opportunities.

Outside politics and public service, Niibi manages Nungua Royals FC and works as a media consultant with the Multimedia Group.

Niibi campaigned under the message, “Youth in Politics: From Spectators to Decision Makers”.

His proposed agenda included establishing a functional Greater Accra Youth Secretariat, creating a database of young party members across the region’s 34 constituencies and setting up a 24-hour youth hotline.

He also proposed appointing a youth desk officer in every constituency and introducing a welfare scheme for young party members.

The NDC’s regional executive elections form part of the party’s internal reorganisation, with the outcome expected to shape its leadership structures and mobilisation efforts across the country.

As Deputy Regional Youth Organiser, Niibi will work with the regional leadership on youth mobilisation and strengthening the party’s structures in Greater Accra.

Ghana News.title: Sam Jonah credits Acheampong with advancing Ghanaian ownership of mineral wealth
Ghana News.content:
Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has credited former Head of State General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong with advancing Ghanaian participation and ownership in the country’s mining and timber industries.

Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Mr Jonah said Acheampong’s government introduced policies in 1972 that gave the state controlling interests in major companies, including Ashanti Goldfields and the Consolidated African Selection Trust.

He said the measures were intended to increase Ghanaian control over the country’s natural resources while retaining foreign partners, their capital and technical expertise.

“For the first time since the Portuguese landed at Elmina, the majority of the wealth beneath Ghanaian soil belonged to Ghanaians,” he said.

Sir Jonah said Acheampong’s government did not rely on force to take control of the mining operations but retained foreign partners under management agreements.

He said the government required the companies to locate their head offices in Accra, give the state a controlling role and train Ghanaians for senior management positions.

“But he insisted on three things: that the head office be in Accra, so that the decisions that mattered were taken by people who had to look Ghanaians in the eye; that the state hold the controlling voice; and that a Ghanaian be trained and placed in the deputy managing director's chair, with the clear expectation that the top chair would follow,” he said.

Sir Sam Jonah said the policy helped create opportunities for Ghanaian professionals in the mining industry.

The University of Cape Coast Chancellor said he was among those who benefited from the policy.

“In due course, I was that Ghanaian. So were many others, in many companies. A whole generation of Ghanaian engineers, geologists and accountants came up through the door that decree opened,” he said.

Sir Jonah had earlier disclosed that he joined Ashanti Goldfields in 1969 as an underground miner at Obuasi, before the government took control of the company in 1972. He later rose to become its chief executive.

His remarks formed part of a broader assessment of Acheampong’s leadership and the former military government's approach to Ghanaian participation in strategic industries.

Ghana News.title: ArchXenus marks 15 years with more than 140 projects, launches GeneXus
Ghana News.content:
Architecture firm ArchXenus has marked 15 years in practice with more than 140 projects, using its anniversary celebration to launch GeneXus, a book documenting 12 of its selected works, and to introduce initiatives aimed at strengthening its contribution to Ghana’s built environment.

The two-day celebration, held on 10 and 11 November 2026 at Christ Temple East in Accra, a building ArchXenus designed and whose construction it managed, featured the launch of the GeneXus book, the Xenus Impact Foundation and the African Urban Futures Conclave. It also brought architects and other stakeholders together to examine the future of cities, climate-responsive buildings, housing and investment in the built environment.

The firm is led by Nana Akua Oppong-Birmeh and Agnes Ofosu-Appiah, both Partners and Principal Architects at ArchXenus E and Co-Directors of the Xenus Impact Foundation. Both said the firm’s most significant achievement over the past 15 years was not simply the number of projects it had completed, but the people it had helped develop, and the model of partnership it offered, particularly to women building careers while managing family responsibilities.

“Just by virtue of our existence, so many people have found their feet, especially women. They have found the confidence to pursue their passion, to proceed into family life, and not worry about so many things, because we are modelling this and creating an opportunity for us to grow,” Nana Akua said.

“Being partners and running the firm together has taught us that there’s strength in numbers. We are both married women with children, so we have life happening as well as work that is ongoing. When one person is down or out, the other steps in. We complement each other, which allows us to work, see where the gaps are in the built industry, and provide solutions for them,” Agnes said.

The GeneXus book brings together 12 selected ArchXenus projects. Nana Akua said the publication was intended to strengthen the documentation of Ghanaian architecture and give students and practitioners local examples from which to draw inspiration, noting that many still relied on foreign publications despite the availability of projects designed and led by Ghanaians.

“This is an opportunity for people to gather inspiration right here, in our cities, in Ghana, designed and led by Ghanaians, with familiar names. In places where you can actually pick a cab, go and experience them, and get inspired,” she said.

Agnes said the African Urban Futures Conclave was conceived to address the fragmented nature of conversations in the built environment, where architects, engineers and other professionals often discussed issues within their own disciplines although the challenges facing cities required collaboration across sectors.

The full Conclave will take place in April 2027 and is intended to be held biennially, bringing stakeholders from Ghana and across West Africa together to exchange ideas, plan, make business connections and agree on practical actions. Ahead of it, ArchXenus has agreed a challenge with the Ghana Institute of Architects inviting architects to showcase solutions to the problems facing cities.

The Conclave is one strand of the newly launched Xenus Impact Foundation, which the partners established to give ideas room to grow beyond the firm’s commercial work and to serve communities through impact projects and corporate social responsibility. The Foundation works in four ways: publishing, through AX Press, which includes GeneXus; building, through impact projects; convening, through gatherings such as the Conclave; and showing, through exhibitions, including Time Space and Essence in Venice in 2027.

Nana Akua called for stronger coordination in the planning of Ghanaian cities, arguing that architects are commonly commissioned to work within defined plots even when the impact of a building extends beyond its boundaries.

“For an architect, you are usually given a defined plot of land to work with. You can think beyond it, but you can only work on that plot. Most cities that have developed have a vision for what they want to be, and that makes it easier for everyone to plug into that vision and let us have the kind of city that we all dream of,” she said.

Agnes raised concerns about the gap in housing provision for middle-income earners, saying Ghana’s housing deficit, commonly put at about 1.8 million units, persisted despite a visible construction boom that did not translate into options for people in that bracket.

“When you see a construction boom, it’s not for middle income. There’s a lot of luxury, and there are a lot of affordable housing schemes. But somewhere in the middle, there’s a gap. And the kayayei: when they arrive in Accra or whichever big city they go to, what buildings and what systems have we put in place for them?” she said.

The Foundation’s pilot impact project, CoSpace, responds to that gap, exploring how middle-income earners can afford dignified homes in established neighbourhoods closer to work and school rather than living far from both.

These concerns were among the issues explored on the second day of the celebration, 11 November, under the theme “Conversations & Connections”, a foretaste of the full Conclave.

The discussions connected the role of architecture to wider questions about the kind of cities people want to live in, including lessons from architectural practice in Ethiopia and the need to move beyond plans towards implementation.

Climate-responsive construction also featured prominently, with discussions on why green buildings matter and how they could be delivered at scale. A virtual address and moderated discussion on “Designing for Dignity” considered the human needs that should inform design, while conversations on moving from vision to delivery examined what is required to turn urban plans into practical outcomes.

The gathering also considered what makes urban projects investable, bringing questions of capital, business connections and collaboration into discussions about the future of cities.

Ghana News.title: Sam Jonah calls for renewed agricultural investment, recalls Operation Feed Yourself achievements
Ghana News.content:
Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has criticised successive governments for abandoning the agricultural gains of General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong’s Operation Feed Yourself campaign, arguing that Ghana allowed a successful food production initiative to collapse.

Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Sir Jonah said the programme, launched in 1972, was a nationwide mobilisation effort that brought traditional authorities and communities into the drive for food self-sufficiency.

He said the campaign used radio broadcasts and information vans to encourage people across the country to participate in agricultural production.

“Cutlasses, hoes, fertiliser and seed were sold at heavily subsidised prices. Feeder roads carried produce to market. Above all, the government invested in water, from Dawenya and Asutsuare to the great Tono dam in the north,” he said.

Sir Jonah said the campaign produced significant results, particularly in rice production.

“Rice imports fell to zero in 1975, and again in 1976. Zero. Farmers in the North exported rice and tomatoes to Upper Volta, and Tamale earned a nickname, The Rice City,” he said.

He argued that the programme demonstrated Ghana’s capacity to achieve substantial improvements in domestic food production when agricultural policies were supported by sustained investment and nationwide participation.

Sir Sam Jonah said the programme’s decline represented a missed opportunity for the country.

“The tragedy of Operation Feed Yourself is not that it failed. It is that it worked, and we let it go,” he said.

He contrasted the campaign’s reported achievements with Ghana’s current food import bill, which he put at about US$2 billion annually, with rice and chicken accounting for a significant share.

Operation Feed Yourself was introduced under Acheampong’s military government in 1972 to promote domestic food production and reduce dependence on imports. Colonel Frank Bernasko played a leading role in the campaign, helping mobilise traditional authorities and communities.

Sir Jonah’s remarks formed part of a broader argument for renewed investment in agriculture and a stronger national commitment to food security.

Ghana News.title: Benjamin Danso defeats NDC Greater Accra chair Ashie Moore by a margin of over 500 votes
Ghana News.content:
Ashie Moore (L) & Benjamin Danso (R).

Benjamin Danso has emerged as the new Greater Accra Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), defeating incumbent Emmanuel Nii Ashie Moore in the party’s regional executive election by a margin of over 500 votes.

Mr Danso’s victory brings an end to Mr Ashie Moore’s tenure, which began in November 2022 when he defeated then-incumbent Joseph Ade Coker to take over the regional chairmanship.

Mr Ashie Moore had served in the position for almost four years and was seeking another term. Ahead of Saturday’s, November 14, 2026, polls, he expressed confidence that delegates would retain him, citing his work and leadership of the party in the region.

In an interview ahead of the election, he said he was confident delegates would reward his efforts.

“I’m very confident the delegates today will reward hard work,” he said.

However, the delegates voted for Mr Danso, giving him the responsibility of leading the party in the Greater Accra Region for the next four years.

Mr Danso had, during his campaign, pledged to lead with service, integrity and commitment to the party’s grassroots.

He also outlined plans to strengthen party structures across all 34 constituencies in the region and build a united front capable of securing victory for the NDC in the 2028 general elections.

Benjamin Danso served as the NDC Constituency Chairman for Krowor in Greater Accra. In June 2023, he was elected chairman of the Greater Accra NDC Constituency Chairmen’s Association, a caucus that brings together constituency chairpersons across the region.

That role gave him experience coordinating and engaging party leaders beyond his own constituency.

Ghana News.title: Owusu Nkrumah Ababio elected Ahafo NDC Regional Chairman
Ghana News.content:
Owusu Nkrumah Ababio has been elected Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Ahafo Region following the party’s 2026 Regional Executives Elections.

The keenly contested polls, held at Nana Bosomprah Park in Goaso, saw Mr Ababio secure 106 votes to defeat his closest contender, Joseph Baradoe, who polled 94 votes. The third candidate, Ahmed Ali Awinbila, obtained three votes.

The results were certified and signed by the Ahafo Regional Director of the Electoral Commission (EC), Emmanuel Kyei, bringing the electoral process to a close.

In the contest for Regional Vice Chairman, Abdul Mumin Sadick emerged victorious with 85 votes, defeating Prince Ahmed Mohammed, who secured 59 votes. Salamatu Braima polled 43 votes, while Joseph Asako Azumyarn obtained 12 votes.

Awudu Razak won the Regional Secretary position with 114 votes, beating George Mawuli, who polled 89 votes.

For Deputy Regional Secretary, Gbene Mohammed Sidiki secured 85 votes to emerge as winner ahead of Patricia Oteng Agyemang (65 votes), Richard Adampoah Kowoji (41 votes) and Haruna Alhassan (11 votes).

Masawudu Sulemana was elected Regional Organiser after polling 109 votes against Iddrisu Loaman Dauda’s 94 votes.

Shilla Yahaya won the Deputy Regional Organiser position with 77 votes, defeating Ibrahim Anyas Muniru, who obtained 66 votes, and Peter Bonsu, who polled 59 votes.

In the financial portfolios, Smartwilliam Kwasi Aziblame won the Regional Treasurer position with 112 votes, beating Ibrahim Musah, who secured 88 votes.

Abdulai Hamidu was elected Deputy Regional Treasurer with 129 votes, defeating Abdul-Kadri Yahaya, who polled 73 votes.

Apraku Lartey emerged as Regional Communication Officer after securing 117 votes against Issaka Azumah’s 86 votes. Alfred Aboagye won the Deputy Regional Communication Officer position with 127 votes, beating Misiagbetor Etse JohnChris, who obtained 75 votes.

Abdallah Ibn Chambas recorded the highest individual vote tally in the elections, securing 136 votes to win the Regional Zongo Caucus Coordinator position. His opponent, Abdulai Mamoudou Sana, polled 67 votes.

In the youth wing elections, Abdul Razak Ahmed won the Regional Youth Organiser position with 18 votes against Ibrahim Issifu’s 11 votes.

Dufie Jennifer was elected Deputy Regional Youth Organiser after polling 10 votes, narrowly beating Paul Mensah Quainoo, who obtained seven votes. Dauda Karim secured six votes, Kwame Qyabaah four, while Yussif Issah polled two votes.

For the women’s wing, Gawusu Pooley Mamuna won the Regional Women Organiser position with 13 votes, defeating Hajia Safia Iddrisu, who polled 11 votes.

Mary Louisa Owusu was elected Deputy Regional Women Organiser with nine votes, narrowly beating Lucy Amoah, who obtained eight votes. Bernice Agyei secured seven votes, while Augustina Akua Abrafi polled one vote.

The newly elected regional executives are expected to focus on strengthening the party’s grassroots structures, consolidating internal cohesion and mobilising supporters ahead of the 2028 general elections and other political activities in the region.

Ghana News.title: ‘Yentua’ was negotiation, not recklessness – Sam Jonah on Acheampong’s debt decision
Ghana News.content:
Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has praised former Head of State General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong’s 1972 decision to repudiate some of Ghana’s external debt, describing it as an act of courage and a demonstration of negotiation skill.

Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Mr Jonah said Acheampong’s government announced on February 5, 1972, that Ghana would not honour about US$90 million in suppliers’ credits it considered tainted by corruption, fraud or inflated contracts.

He said the decision became known through the Akan expression “Yentua”, meaning “we will not pay”.

“The Daily Graphic put it in one Akan word, in a headline this country has never forgotten: Yentua. We will not pay,” he said.

Sir Jonah argued that Acheampong’s decision reflected a willingness to withstand immediate economic pressure in pursuit of what he described as long-term national dignity.

“He was prepared to absorb short-term pain for long-term dignity. That is not recklessness. That is negotiation,” he said.

According to Mr Jonah, the debt repudiation compelled creditors to return to negotiations, eventually leading to a rescheduling agreement in Rome in 1974.

Under the arrangement, he said, the debt was rescheduled at an interest rate of 2.5 per cent, with an extended grace period.

Sir Jonah contrasted the 1972 decision with Ghana’s suspension of payments on much of its external debt in December 2022, which preceded the country’s debt restructuring programme.

He said the two episodes reflected different circumstances, arguing that Acheampong’s decision was presented as a deliberate negotiating position, while the 2022 default was driven by the country’s inability to meet its debt obligations.

“In December 2022, fifty years after Yentua, our government again announced that it would stop paying most of its external debt. But this was no choice made from strength, to the applause of the nation. It was a default forced upon us, and it reached into the savings of pensioners and ordinary depositors,” he said.

“In 1972 the slogan was Yentua: we will not pay. In 2022 the honest slogan would have been Yentumi: we cannot,” he added.

The lecture formed part of a broader call for renewed discussion about Ghana’s debt management, economic sovereignty and the lessons that can be drawn from the country’s past dealings with creditors.

Ghana News.title: Sam Jonah calls for honest reassessment of General I.K. Acheampong’s leadership
Ghana News.content:
Business leader and University of Cape Coast Chancellor Sir Sam Jonah has called for a fresh and balanced examination of the leadership of former Head of State General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong, urging Ghanaians to confront the complexities of his time in office.

Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture at the Marriott Hotel in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Sir Jonah said the country needed to move beyond the silence and polarised narratives surrounding the former military leader.

He said the lecture offered an opportunity to examine Acheampong’s record, including his policies, achievements and shortcomings.

“Our forebears left us a saying for an evening such as this: Se wo were fi na wosankofa a yenkyi. It is not wrong to go back for what you have forgotten. That is what we shall do tonight. We shall break the silence,” he said.

Sir Jonah disclosed that he had personally benefited from policies introduced under Acheampong’s government, particularly those that expanded opportunities for Ghanaians in the management of the Ashanti Goldfields Corporation.

He said he joined the mining company in 1969 as an underground miner at Obuasi, three years before the government took control of the company in 1972.

“I am a beneficiary of this man. In 1972 his government took control of the Ashanti Goldfields Corporation and opened its senior management to Ghanaians. I had joined Ashanti three years earlier as an underground miner at Obuasi. The chairs I would one day occupy were built on policies General Acheampong signed into law,” he said.

He, however, clarified that he had never met the former Head of State personally.

“I never knew him. I never sat across a table from him. But my life bears his fingerprints, and I would be a fraud to pretend otherwise,” he added.

Sir Sam Jonah said his intention was neither to glorify Acheampong nor to condemn him without examining the full record of his leadership.

“Ghana has already done both to this man, and neither has served us well. Tonight, I intend to examine the leadership of General Acheampong, the vision and the blindness, the triumph and the disappointment, the man and the system he led, and to let you judge it whole,” he said.

General Acheampong came to power in January 1972 after leading a military coup that overthrew the government of Dr Kofi Abrefa Busia.

His government introduced policies and initiatives including Operation Feed Yourself, which sought to boost domestic food production, and the Yentua policy, under which Ghana repudiated certain external debt obligations.

It also advanced the Union Government proposal, which sought a political arrangement involving civilian and military participation.

Acheampong was removed from power in July 1978 and later executed by the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council in June 1979.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
