Mr Guterres’ successor has not been announced. The new secretary-general will take office on 1 January 2027 and will lead the UN into the next climate summit (COP32) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, later that year.

World.title: Tanzania vs Nigeria: Injury knocks Lookman out of next crucial test
World.content:
Ademola Lookman will miss Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Tanzania in Zanzibar on Tuesday. He sustained a knee ligament sprain, which also casts doubt on his availability for Atlético Madrid’s upcoming fixtures.

A scan confirmed the injury on Saturday, following the Super Eagles’ 3-1 victory over Tanzania at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo on Friday.

The team’s media officer, Promise Efoghe, announced that the forward would be unavailable for the return fixture.

“Scan has revealed Ademola Lookman suffered a sprain in his knee ligament during yesterday’s match. This rules him out of Nigeria’s next AFCON qualifier versus Tanzania in Zanzibar on Tuesday,” Mr Efoghe said.

Lookman was forced off late in the first half in Uyo and was replaced by Moses Simon.

Before his withdrawal, the Atlético Madrid forward had provided the assist for Alhassan Yusuf’s second-minute opener, giving Nigeria an early advantage.

However, Tanzania drew level in the 32nd minute through Alphonce Msanga, who scored with the visitors’ first shot on target.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The teams went into the break at 1-1. Still, Super Eagles coach Éric Chelle introduced Tolu Arokodare in the second half, and the striker responded with two goals to secure Nigeria’s victory.

The result revived Nigeria’s qualifying campaign following their disappointing 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau in September. The Super Eagles now have six points from three matches in Group L, one behind leaders Guinea-Bissau.

Atlético fixtures in doubt

Lookman’s injury comes at a difficult time for the forward, who was not used in Atlético Madrid’s 2-1 defeat to Barcelona in their LaLiga encounter on 8 November.

The Nigerian remained on the bench throughout the match despite his club seeking a late equaliser.

He now faces a race against time to recover for Atlético’s next two matches after the international break.

Diego Simeone’s side are scheduled to visit Getafe in a LaLiga fixture on 22 November before hosting Norwegian club Viking FK in the Champions League three days later.

The Getafe encounter will take place at the Coliseum, while the European fixture is scheduled for the Riyadh Air Metropolitano in Madrid.

Lookman’s availability for either match will depend on his recovery from the knee injury. Atlético will be keen to assess his condition before deciding when he can return to action.

For Nigeria, his absence is a setback as Chelle’s men prepare for Tuesday’s return fixture at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar, where they will seek another victory to strengthen their position in Group L.

World.title: Nigeria, South Africa trade words over exclusion from diplomatic ceremony livestream
World.content:
In the last 24 hours, the Nigerian and South African governments have been trading words over the exclusion of Nigerian High Commissioner to South Africa Femi Fani-Kayode’s speech from the live stream of a diplomatic ceremony in Pretoria.

In its latest response to South African presidential spokesperson Vincent Magwenya, the Nigerian High Commission in Pretoria said Mr Fani-Kayode was treated with contempt and disdain, and that this, by extension, is mistreatment of Nigeria.

The commission, through its official X handle, called Mr Magwenya a “liar” and a “disgrace.”

“Outside of that, your insolence and ignorance know no bounds. You are bringing your nation into disrepute and willfully and purposely burning the bridge of peace and reconciliation. That is a matter of concern to us. The only thing that is inappropriate is the shameful way that you and your team behaved,” the commission said.

The comment was a response to Mr Magwenya’s X post, which was directed toward Mr Fani-Kayode.

The Nigerian High Commissioner, on Friday, accused the South African presidency of cutting off the live stream during his speech at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria, where he presented his credentials to President Cyril Ramaphosa.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Fani-Kayode, also accredited to Lesotho and Eswatini, said he was the only one of the 15 ambassadors given the stage to speak whose live stream was cut off.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“To be clear, we were the ONLY ones that were left out. Clearly, some elements in South Africa do not want to hear what we have to say or see our faces, but we are here to stay as long as we are welcome and have the confidence of President Ramaphosa, which I am sure we do,” he said.

The South African presidential spokesperson responded to Mr Fani-Kayode, stating that the event was livestreamed by the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC), whose operations are not controlled by the presidency.

Mr Magwenya said the SABC is a public broadcaster, and that the “President does not interfere with its operations or intervene in its editorial processes.”

He accused Mr Fani-Kayode of misrepresenting the facts.

He also said, “I would encourage you, as you start your tenure in South Africa, to meet with SABC to forge a mutually beneficial, respectful and professional relationship.”

However, hours after Fani-Kayode’s allegations, the SABC uploaded a separate video featuring his speech on its website.

Joining the diplomatic spat, the Nigerian High Commission accused Mr Magwenya of trying to heighten diplomatic tension between the states by “adding fuel to the fire.”

“A few months ago you, as spokesman to the President of the Republic of South Africa, described our President and the President of Ghana as peddlers of fake news after they expressed their deep and legitimate concerns about Afrophobia and Xenophobia in your country.

“We let that one go and ignored you. Today, you are calling our newly accredited Ambassador to your country a liar, barely a few hours after he presented his letters of credence.

“You also claim that he has disgraced our country simply because he complained to your President about a slight which your media team subjected him and our nation to.

“We also have the full video clip of the proceedings after the pictures were taken which, if and when we are given the go-ahead to do so, we shall release,” the High Commission said.

Relations between Nigeria and South Africa grew tense after a new wave of xenophobic violence broke out in April and has since been linked to the death of at least 12 Nigerians.

Mr Fani-Kayode, first deployed to Germany as ambassador, said he asked to be redeployed to South Africa because it was more “proximate to my political thinking when it comes to foreign affairs and a pan-African vision.”

World.title: ADC accuses NBA of double standards over petition against lawyer
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) of double standards over its decision to petition a disciplinary panel against lawyer Kalu Kalu for making disparaging remarks about Federal High Court judge Peter Lifu.

The opposition party questioned why the association had moved against Mr Kalu when the Court of Appeal had previously rebuked the judge over his handling of a separate case involving the deregistration of political parties.

In a statement on Saturday, the ADC’s National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, warned the NBA against allowing itself to be drawn into what the party described as a political campaign against the opposition.

“The NBA is not a political party. It must, therefore, not be seen to be behaving like a member of a political coalition against the opposition,” Mr Abdullahi said.

The statement followed the NBA’s announcement on Friday that its president, Oyinkansola Badejo-Okusanya, had forwarded a petition against Mr Kalu to the Legal Practitioners Disciplinary Committee (LPDC).

What triggered the petition

Mr Kalu, a lawyer associated with the ADC and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, appeared on Channels Television’s Politics Today on 11 November to discuss Justice Lifu’s judgement in the party’s leadership dispute.

The judgement, delivered on 5 November, invalidated the David Mark-led leadership and decisions taken under it, including the process through which Mr Abubakar emerged as the party’s presidential candidate.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The ADC has rejected the ruling and moved to challenge it, while Mr Kalu has argued that the court’s orders did not expressly invalidate Mr Abubakar’s nomination.

During the television programme, Mr Kalu made personal remarks about Justice Lifu, reportedly describing him as a “coconut judge”.

The presenter, Seun Okinbaloye, interrupted him and objected to the language, insisting that the programme should not be used to disparage a sitting judge.

Mr Kalu subsequently withdrew the remark.

In a statement issued on Friday, Mrs Badejo-Okusanya condemned the comments, saying lawyers were entitled to challenge judicial decisions but must avoid personal attacks on judges.

She said the Rules of Professional Conduct for Legal Practitioners, 2023, required lawyers to maintain professional standards and treat courts with respect.

The NBA president disclosed that she had submitted a formal petition, accompanied by the relevant broadcast recording, to the LPDC.

She clarified that Mr Kalu would have an opportunity to respond and that the committee would determine whether his conduct amounted to professional misconduct and whether any sanction was warranted.

ADC cites earlier appellate ruling

Responding to the development, Mr Abdullahi questioned why the NBA had focused on Mr Kalu’s remarks when an appellate court had previously criticised Justice Lifu’s conduct.

“What has Kalu Kalu said about Justice Peter Lifu that the Court of Appeal has not already said?” he asked.

The ADC referred to a 16 June ruling in which the Court of Appeal rebuked Justice Lifu for delivering a judgement ordering the deregistration of the ADC and four other political parties despite an earlier appellate order staying proceedings.

The court described the judge’s conduct as judicial impertinence and judicial rascality, and suspended the enforcement of his deregistration order.

On 28 July, the appellate court overturned the judgement, holding that the Federal High Court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the suit.

The earlier proceedings concerned the proposed deregistration of the ADC, Accord, Action Alliance, Action Peoples Party and Zenith Labour Party.

They were separate from the ADC leadership dispute, which Justice Lifu decided on 5 November.

The earlier appellate findings did not determine the validity of the November judgment or establish that it resulted from political interference.

ADC warns against political interference

Mr Abdullahi maintained that the NBA should be more concerned about judicial accountability than what the party described as an attempt to victimise a lawyer for expressing his political views.

He accused the association of risking its credibility by appearing indifferent to alleged misconduct within the judiciary while pursuing disciplinary action against Mr Kalu.

The party also alleged that some lawyers and judges were collaborating with politically connected individuals to undermine the administration of justice.

However, Saturday’s statement did not provide evidence establishing such collusion or linking the NBA’s petition to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

Mr Abdullahi argued that respect for judicial institutions should not prevent lawyers from speaking against perceived wrongdoing.

“We agree that lawyers must exercise restraint. But there is no respectful way to address evil, and the NBA cannot teach us one,” he said.

In its earlier statement, the NBA said judicial accountability and professional discipline were not mutually exclusive.

The association said it was entitled to demand accountability from judges while insisting that lawyers observe professional standards.

However, that statement preceded the ADC’s latest allegations.

PREMIUM TIMES made two telephone calls and sent a WhatsApp message seeking the NBA’s response to the party’s accusations, including whether the association took any action following the Court of Appeal’s earlier criticism of Justice Lifu.

No response had been received as of the time this report was prepared.

World.title: MOVIE REVIEW: At 59, Emeka Ike remains Nollywood’s ‘OG lover boy’ in ‘Mother’s Bargain 2’
World.content:
For decades, Nollywood actor Emeka Ike has been one of the faces associated with the industry’s romantic leading men. From his piercing gaze and charming screen presence to the effortless affection he brings to romantic roles, Ike built a reputation as one of Nollywood’s quintessential lover boys, particularly during the home-video era of the 1990s and early 2000s.

Now 59, the veteran actor appears unwilling to relinquish that familiar screen identity. Rather than allow age to distance him from the romantic roles that endeared him to audiences, Ike seems to have embraced a more mature version of the character, demonstrating that the appeal of a screen lover boy is not necessarily diminished by time.

His latest outing in Mother’s Bargain, a Nollywood drama released on Uchenna Mbunabo TV, has once again drawn attention to that enduring appeal. Playing Chief Coker, a wealthy politician whose affection and emotional maturity gradually transform an initially transactional marriage into a genuine love story, Ike revisits a character type that helped define his career, this time with the composure and tenderness of a more seasoned performer.

What happened in Part 1

Mother’s Bargain, directed by Ben Cassie and written by Chioma Akpan, centred on Adaora (Chinenye Nnebe), a young woman caught between her mother’s ambitions and her desire to determine her own future. Her mother, Felicia (Charity Onah), whose life had been shaped by poverty, hardship, and abandonment, saw marriage to wealthy politician Chief Coker (Emeka Ike) as the family’s best chance to escape financial difficulties.

Adaora, however, was already in a relationship with Chike, whose marriage proposal was thrown into uncertainty following his arrest for wire fraud. Under sustained pressure from Felicia, she eventually agreed to marry Chief Coker, although the union began more as an arrangement of convenience than a genuine expression of love.

But the marriage took an unexpected turn when Chief Coker demonstrated a tenderness that contradicted the conventional portrayal of wealthy older men in Nollywood romance dramas.

Following a hypertension crisis linked to tampered medication and Felicia’s subsequent death from a stroke, Adaora was left to confront the consequences of the arrangement. She eventually confessed her mother’s original intentions to her husband.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Rather than retaliate, Chief Coker granted her a divorce, provided financial support, and helped secure her a job. Only after experiencing life away from him did Adaora recognise the depth of her feelings and return to rebuild their relationship.

The film ended with the couple reconciled and looking towards a future together, leaving viewers with the impression that their complicated journey had finally found its happy ending.

Its appeal was reflected in its impressive performance on YouTube, where it eventually garnered over 12 million views. Much of the audience’s affection for the film rested on Emeka Ike’s portrayal of Chief Coker, whose quiet confidence, generosity, and emotional maturity earned him admiration as Nollywood’s latest “OG lover boy”.

For many viewers, there was little reason to expect another chapter. But Mother’s Bargain 2, released on November 2, 2026, returns to the couple’s lives, demonstrating that reconciliation does not necessarily guarantee a trouble-free marriage.

Mother’s Bargain 2

Directed again by Ben Cassie, the sequel retains the central characters but introduces new complications that threaten the domestic peace established in the first instalment.

This time, Adaora and Chief Coker must confront infertility, unsuccessful in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) attempts and the unexpected arrival of a son from the politician’s past.

The young man, Ade (Kelvin Utulu), is 26 years old and previously unknown to Chief Coker. His mother, Alicia, also returns to the politician’s life, bringing with her tensions that threaten to unsettle his marriage.

A DNA test confirming paternity at 99.9 per cent establishes Ade’s place in the family. However, the revelation does little to guarantee harmony. Instead, it raises questions about inheritance, family loyalty, acceptance, and Adaora’s place in a household that suddenly has a new heir.

The situation becomes even more complicated as Alicia’s presence and influence begin to affect the newly reunited couple. With Adaora already struggling with the emotional burden of infertility, the arrival of Chief Coker’s adult son creates another test for a marriage that viewers had assumed was finally secure. Would love prevail again?

Emeka Ike remains the film’s strongest attraction

If there is one reason Mother’s Bargain 2 sustains the appeal of its predecessor, it is Emeka Ike’s return as Chief Coker.

Mr Ike doesn’t try to reinvent the character. Instead, he builds on the qualities that made the character memorable in the first film. His portrayal blends authority with gentleness, giving the character a reassuring presence without making him seem overly sentimental.

The description of Chief Coker as an “OG lover boy” is particularly fitting. He represents a kind of romantic masculinity that is increasingly appealing within the film’s narrative: a man who can exercise authority without intimidation and demonstrate affection without making a spectacle of it.

In the sequel, Chief Coker faces the difficult task of processing the discovery of a son he never knew existed, managing Alicia’s return and protecting his marriage from the tensions surrounding his expanded family.

He handles these developments with the composure expected of a veteran actor. Rather than relying on exaggerated expressions or explosive confrontations, the veteran allows disappointment, suspicion, and emotional pain to emerge through measured dialogue and restrained performances.

His strongest moments come when Chief Coker discovers further betrayals, including attempts to undermine Adaora. The actor gives these scenes the necessary emotional weight without allowing the character to lose the dignity that defines him.

This consistency makes his performance particularly effective. Chief Coker is not an entirely new character in Part 2; he is the same man whose kindness helped transform an initially transactional marriage into a genuine relationship.

Review

Despite its engaging performances, Mother’s Bargain 2 does not quite possess the thematic freshness of the original.

The first film drew much of its strength from the unusual circumstances surrounding Adaora’s marriage. It explored poverty, maternal desperation, financial insecurity, and the difficult choices women sometimes face when their futures are determined by family expectations.

Its most compelling achievement was the gradual transformation of a marriage founded on deception into a relationship built on genuine affection. Chief Coker’s unexpected decency also challenged the familiar Nollywood stereotype of the wealthy older man who uses money to manipulate younger women.

The sequel, however, relies more heavily on familiar family-drama devices: a long-lost child, a returning former partner, inheritance concerns, maternal interference, and marital insecurity.

These developments are not inherently uninteresting. Indeed, they provide sufficient conflict to sustain the narrative and give the returning characters new challenges. However, they make the film feel more conventional than its predecessor.

The infertility storyline, in particular, could have been explored more deeply. It offers an opportunity to explore the emotional and social pressures of childlessness, especially in marriages where family expectations and questions of inheritance become intertwined.

Instead, much of the attention shifts towards the intrigues surrounding Ade’s arrival and Alicia’s influence.

However, Mother’s Bargain 2 may not reinvent the original, but it offers a reasonable continuation of a story that resonated with a large YouTube audience.

Where the first film explored whether genuine affection could emerge from a marriage founded on financial desperation, the sequel examines whether that affection can survive the complications of a partner’s past, infertility, and the arrival of a previously unknown child.

The film works best when it lets Mr Ike and Ms Nnebe carry the story’s emotional weight. Their chemistry remains its strongest asset, while Mr Ike’s restrained portrayal of Chief Coker provides the consistency needed to hold the narrative together.

Some of the new conflicts feel predictable, and the sequel occasionally sacrifices thematic depth for familiar family intrigues. Still, its emotional continuity and returning performances give viewers plenty of reason to stay invested.

For audiences who thought Adaora and Chief Coker’s story had ended with the first film, the sequel offers a reminder that even the most unlikely love stories have their unfinished chapters.

Verdict: 7/10

Mother’s Bargain 2 is streaming on Uchenna Mbunabo TV on YouTube

World.title: Tinubu promises to rebuild Plateau communities, return displaced persons
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has promised to rebuild communities devastated by years of violence in Plateau State and return thousands of internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral homes.

Mr Tinubu made the promise on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central rally in Jos, where he acknowledged the devastating impact of recurring attacks on communities across the state since 2001.

The president said his administration would work with Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang, APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda and other political leaders to restore affected communities and facilitate the return of displaced residents.

“Since 2001, crisis attacks have inflicted deep wounds on Plateau. Too many lives have been lost, homes destroyed, communities displaced,” Mr Tinubu said.

He offered condolences to families who had lost relatives, survivors of attacks and residents who remained unable to return to their homes.

“I assure those displaced that we will rebuild your communities. We will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your communities,” he said.

Mr Tinubu said he had directed security agencies to take decisive action to sustain peace and stability in Plateau, adding that his administration was strengthening security deployment and rapid-response mechanisms.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He disclosed that 1,000 forest guards were undergoing training and would be deployed to improve security in vulnerable communities.

“You will feel them, you will see them. You will feel secure in your villages and communities,” he told the gathering.

The president also said surveillance cameras promised to the state had been procured to strengthen intelligence gathering and early-warning operations.

He pledged to work with the state government and other stakeholders to ensure that displaced families returned to their communities and resettled in conditions that would allow them to rebuild their lives.

The promise comes amid persistent security challenges in Plateau, where attacks, communal violence and displacement have affected several local government areas over the years.

According to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), Plateau had 45,212 internally displaced persons as of 1 August 2026.

The agency’s displacement figures, compiled from sources including the International Organisation for Migration’s Displacement Tracking Matrix, underscore the scale of the humanitarian challenge the state faces.

In July, UNHCR also reported distributing essential relief items to conflict-affected households in Bassa, Barkin Ladi and Riyom local government areas, following recurrent violence that displaced families and destroyed homes and household belongings.

Mr Tinubu’s latest pledge therefore raises expectations among affected communities for a concrete resettlement programme backed by sustained security operations, reconstruction and humanitarian support.

Security and political commitments

The president acknowledged that his previous visit to Plateau had been limited to the airport, saying he had nevertheless seen the devastation and received reports from Governor Mutfwang about the situation in affected communities.

He commended the governor for what he described as efforts to promote peace and stability, urging residents to overcome their differences and work together.

According to him, ethnic, religious and linguistic differences should not make residents enemies, stressing that communities must be able to farm, live and develop together.

“Our government is not elected to inflict wounds on one another or to bury people. We have to lift people from penury to prosperity,” he said.

Mr Tinubu also promised to work with the Plateau government to develop the state’s agricultural and mining sectors.

He said his administration would collaborate with Mr Mutfwang to develop Jos Airport into a cargo airport, enabling farmers to export vegetables and potatoes directly to international markets.

He added that tin mining and other economic activities could contribute to the state’s development.

APC mobilises for 2027

The rally also served as a platform for the APC leadership to mobilise support for Mr Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima urged Plateau residents to support the president, describing his economic policies as necessary decisions taken to rescue Nigeria from economic collapse.

Mr Shettima said the country faced difficult circumstances when Mr Tinubu assumed office in May 202,3 but argued that the president had shown the courage to make difficult decisions.

He also appealed to residents to support the APC and its candidates in the forthcoming elections.

Mr Yilwatda, who is from Plateau State, described the president as a promise keeper, listing security-related interventions he said the federal government had delivered to the state.

These included establishing security command centres in vulnerable areas, procuring surveillance cameras,s and training forest guards.

He expressed confidence that Plateau residents would demonstrate their support for Mr Tinubu at the ballot box.

Governor Mutfwang, in his remarks, praised the president’s leadership and said the federal government’s interventions had helped strengthen the state’s development efforts.

He also defended the administration’s handling of insecurity, arguing that the government had made security a priority.

Mr Mutfwang said the APC government would remain committed to implementing its manifesto and improving Nigerians’ lives.

The rally was attended by APC governors, members of the National Assembly, former governors, and other party leaders, including former Plateau governors Joshua Dariye and Simon Lalong.

World.title: Ogun ADC rejects caretaker committee
World.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

Ogun State chapter of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, has rejected the purported establishment of caretaker committees and the appointment of parallel state chairman. They insisted that the executive committee led by Otunba Oluwafemi Soluade remains the legitimate leadership structure of the party in the state.

The party, in a press statement issued on Saturday, by its Publicity Secretary, Adesina Olanrewaju, described the alleged move to introduce alternative leadership arrangements as an affront to internal democracy, constitutional order and the rule of law.

The statement was titled ‘Enough of the Political Arrogance! Ogun ADC Is Not a Personal Estate: We Reject Illegal Caretaker Arrangements and Reaffirm the Otunba Oluwafemi Soluade-Led Executive Committee’.

They maintained that no individual, regardless of political influence or position, had the authority to unilaterally dismantle the party’s established structures in Ogun State.

The party specifically cautioned against attempts to impose a caretaker committee without the requisite constitutional authority, proper national authorisation and compliance with the ADC’s established procedures.

It particularly mentioned Chief Rauf Aregbesola, insisting that neither he nor any other individual could assume the power to impose a caretaker arrangement on the state chapter, outside the party’s constitutional framework.

“Ogun State is not a political playground, neither is the ADC in Ogun State anybody’s personal estate where decisions can be imposed through arrogance, intimidation or unilateral administrative pronouncements,” the statement declared.

The party further argued that political influence should not be used to override established democratic procedures, warning that it would resist any attempt to create parallel leadership structures capable of weakening its existing institutions

Reaffirming its position, the Ogun ADC described the executive committee led by Soluade as the legitimate structure whose authority and tenure it was determined to defend.

According to the statement, an elected party structure cannot be discarded merely because some individuals desire a different leadership arrangement to advance their political interests.

“You cannot build a political party on the foundation of democracy and subsequently destroy that same foundation because the existing leadership does not serve the political interests of certain individuals,” it said.

The party maintained that it would not recognise parallel leadership arrangements allegedly designed to create confusion, undermine established institutions or impose new officers through the back door.

To support its position, the Ogun ADC referred to judicial pronouncements arising from disputes over the constitutionality of caretaker arrangements and the tenure of elected party executives.

Cites court rulings

It cited Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/581/2026, in which the Federal High Court, Abuja, presided over by Justice Joyce Abdulmalik, reportedly delivered judgment on April 29, 2026, affirming the subsisting tenure of ADC State Working and Executive Committees.

According to the statement, the court restrained the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, from recognising or participating in state congresses organised by the caretaker leadership.

It also held, according to the party, that the caretaker/interim National Working Committee lacked the constitutional authority to appoint committees to conduct such congresses.

The statement disclosed that the judgment was subsequently challenged at the Court of Appeal in Appeal No. CA/ABJ/CV/608/2026, but the appellate court dismissed the appeal and upheld the restrictions against congresses organised outside the party’s constitutional framework.

The Ogun chapter also relied on the November 3, 2026 judgment of the Federal High Court sitting in Ibadan in Suit No. FHC/IB/CS/50/2026, presided over by Justice U.N. Agomoh, pointing out that the court declared the purported interim executive committee led by Afeez Adelowo Jimoh as illegal and affirmed the four-year tenure of the Yinka Olona-led Oyo State Executive Committee.

The party explained that the Ibadan judgment relied on Section 223 of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and relevant provisions of the ADC Constitution.

Describing the judicial decisions as binding pronouncements that must be respected, the Ogun ADC warned against treating court judgments as optional directives that could be obeyed or disregarded according to political convenience.

Vanguard News

World.title: Obasanjo urges Nigerian youths to shun divisive, discriminatory campaigns
World.content:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo

Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has called on Nigerian youths to shun campaign of division, segregation, discrimination and marginalisation.

Obasanjo made the call on Saturday after receiving an honorary doctorate degree conferred on him by the Skyline University of Nigeria in Kano.

He was conferred with the honour alongside former Executive Secretary, National Universities Commission (NUC), Prof. Abubakar Adamu-Rasheed and Mrs. Vadana Luthra.

The former president, who addressed the gathering through a recorded video, said the youths, irrespective of their tribe, religion and age, must be the architects of their own future and fortune, noting they have to struggle for what they want, as salvation will not come from heaven.

He said himself, and the late Head of State Murtala Muhammad spearheaded the change in the country.

Obasanjo said the youths have to be positively disruptive to bring about the desired change.

“Most of the leaders of the immediate, pre and post-independent era were young and active.

“They went for change, and they made it happen. Nigeria, as a whole, benefited from their activism.

“Let me name two – Aminu Kano and Enahoro. The military era was not much different.”

Earlier, the Vice Chancellor, Prof. Ajith Kumar, announced approval of new programmes by the National Universities Commission (NUC), adding that the university was the first in North-West Nigeria to receive approval for the B.Sc. Artificial Intelligence programme.

He said the development further demonstrates its commitment to advancing technology-driven education in the region.

Kumar said the institution has awarded a 50% scholarship to all toppers to pursue their postgraduate programmes at the university.

A total of 237 students graduated with various degrees at the institution’s 5th convocation ceremony. (NAN)

World.title: FRSC confirms one dead, eight injured in Anambra multiple crash
World.content:
The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Anambra State Sector Command, has confirmed one death and eight injuries in a multiple-vehicle crash at Agu-Awka, Immigration Junction, along the Awka-Enugu Expressway.

The sector commander, Corps Commander Bridget Asekhauno, personally led the rescue efforts following the crash.

Asekhauno told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday that the crash occurred at about 8.45 a.m. and involved a Sinotruck trailer, a Toyota Camry and a TVS commercial tricycle.

She said that the vehicles had registration numbers AAA920YN, ENU622DR and NSH684VC, respectively.

“Preliminary investigations indicated excessive speeding and inadequate construction warning signs as suspected factors responsible for the crash.

“An eyewitness account indicated that the trailer, while descending a slope, noticed a diversion sign and attempted to manoeuvre into another lane.

“The trailer reportedly collided sideways with the Toyota Camry, which subsequently hit the tricycle from behind, while the trailer somersaulted,” she said.

The sector commander said that nine persons were involved in the crash, with one confirmed dead and eight sustained varying degrees of injuries.

She added that five of the injured victims were taken to hospital for medical attention.

According to her, the FRSC rescue team promptly mobilised to the scene to manage traffic and clear the obstruction.

“The prompt intervention ensured the clearance and reopening of the blocked diversion route to motorists,” she said.

Asekhauno expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery.

She urged construction companies to provide adequate and visible warning signs, particularly around construction zones and diversion points, to guide motorists and prevent avoidable crashes.

She also advised motorists to observe speed limits, exercise caution around diversions and construction areas as well as pay attention to road signs and traffic instructions.

The sector commander reiterated FRSC’s commitment to prompt emergency response, effective traffic management and the protection of lives and property on Nigerian roads. (NAN)

World.title: Lookman ruled out of Tanzania return leg with knee ligament sprain
World.content:
Super Eagles forward Ademola Lookman has been ruled out of Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying return-leg fixture against Tanzania following a knee ligament sprain.

Promise Efoghe, Super Eagles Media Officer, confirmed the development to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday.

“Scan has revealed Ademola Lookman suffered a sprain in his knee ligament during yesterday’s match.

“This rules him out of Nigeria’s next AFCON qualifier against Tanzania in Zanzibar on Tuesday,” Efoghe said.

The injury was sustained during Nigeria’s 3-1 victory over Tanzania in their Matchday Three encounter at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on Friday.

Lookman’s absence will be a setback for the Super Eagles as they prepare for the return fixture against the Taifa Stars.

The Athletico Madrid forward has been an important attacking option for Nigeria, providing creativity, pace and goal-scoring threat in the final third.

NAN reports that Friday’s victory strengthened Nigeria’s position in the qualifying campaign, taking their points tally to six.

The Super Eagles will now travel to Zanzibar for Tuesday’s Matchday Four encounter, hoping to consolidate their position in the group.

Nigeria will be seeking another positive result against Tanzania as the race for qualification for the 2027 AFCON finals gathers momentum.

Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda are already guaranteed places at the tournament as co-hosts, leaving the remaining qualification spots to be contested by other countries.

The 2027 AFCON finals will be jointly hosted by the three East African countries. (NAN)

World.title: Soludo demands reopening of Anambra court of appeal
World.content:
Gov. Soludo

By Vincent Ujumadu

Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for the immediate reopening of the Court of Appeal in the state, arguing that the volume of litigation generated by Anambra, which he said is second only to Lagos, justifies its continued operation.

Soludo made the demand during a church service marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year of the Anambra State Judiciary.

He also urged the Nigerian legal profession to abandon imported wigs and gowns in favour of locally produced alternatives, saying the continued importation of legal attire amounts to exporting employment opportunities that could be created in Nigeria.

The special service was presided over by the Bishop of Aguata, Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka and Coordinating Bishop of the Province on the Niger, Rt. Rev. Samuel Ezeofor. It was attended by judicial officers, legal practitioners and government functionaries.

Addressing the gathering, Soludo reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving justice delivery but expressed concern over the continued closure of the Court of Appeal in Anambra.

“Anambra, after Lagos, generates more cases. We are more deserving to have the Court of Appeal.

“The Court of Appeal in Anambra should not be closed for one day if merit and need happen to be the criteria. Come and open your court,” he said.

The governor also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the welfare of judicial officers and the provision of necessary infrastructure for the judiciary.

He noted that the state’s plea-bargaining initiative was helping to decongest correctional facilities.

On the need to promote local industries, Soludo challenged lawyers and judicial officers to embrace Nigerian-made legal attire rather than continue importing wigs and gowns.

“Can we change the law regalia into what is made in Nigeria? We are creating jobs abroad by importing all the regalia you wear.

“Let us eat what we produce and wear what we make. That is the way to help the economy. I wear Akwete to promote Made-in-Nigeria,” he said.

The governor, who is known for wearing Akwete fabric, said adopting locally produced materials would support domestic industries and create employment opportunities.

On security, Soludo highlighted the cooperation among the executive, legislature and judiciary, crediting the state’s Homeland Security Law with strengthening the security architecture and restoring calm in different parts of Anambra.

“We may have different branches of government, but we have one objective: the security and welfare of Ndi Anambra,” he said.

Addressing the crisis within the Awka Diocese of the Anglican Communion, the governor said his administration had maintained neutrality, describing the dispute as a private affair of the Anglican Church in Anambra and Nigeria.

He, however, called for an amicable resolution, stressing that the government’s responsibility was to maintain law and order.

In his remarks, the Chief Judge of Anambra State, Justice Onochie Anyachebelu, described the Legal Year ceremony as an opportunity for the judiciary to assess its performance and reposition itself for improved service delivery.

While commending Soludo for maintaining a cordial working relationship with the judiciary, Anyachebelu appealed for urgent government intervention in areas requiring attention.

“The Anambra State Judiciary needs help. Your presence has given us renewed hope,” the Chief Judge said.

World.title: Don’t disappoint Nigeria’s founding fathers, Jonathan warns political leaders
World.content:
File: Dr. Goodluck Jonathan

Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria’s political leaders to rebuild the country, warning against disappointing the founding fathers.

This ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‍​‌‌​is contained in a statement issued by the former president’s Media Adviser, Mr Ikechukwu Eze, in Abuja on Saturday.

Eze quoted Jonathan as making the call while delivering his address at a colloquium organised in honour of the 162nd birth anniversary of a nationalist, Pa Herbert Macaulay, at Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos on Saturday.

Jonathan, who was the chairman of the occasion, challenged Nigeria’s political leaders and citizens to reflect on whether the country had lived up to the dreams and aspirations of its founding nationalists.

He asked whether Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and other heroes of the independence struggle would be proud of today’s Nigeria or regret the outcome of their sacrifices.

Speaking on the theme “Nationalism and Nation Building”, the former president said the vision of Nigeria’s founding nationalists went beyond the transfer of political power from colonial authorities to Nigerians.

“They envisaged a sovereign, united and prosperous country where citizens would enjoy equal rights, economic opportunities, quality education, accessible healthcare and the benefits of accountable governance,” he said.

Jonathan appealed that Nigeria must not allow its founding nationalists to regret the struggle they waged for independence.

According to him, the greatest tribute to the nation’s heroes is not merely to celebrate their birthdays or preserve their monuments but to build a country that reflects the ideals for which they sacrificed.

“We must not make Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and the other founding nationalists regret, even in their graves, the struggle they waged for our independence,” he said.

Jonathan urged the present generation to ensure that today’s national challenges were not allowed to become the inheritance of their children and grandchildren.

He expressed concern that 66 years after independence, Nigeria had yet to substantially realise many of these aspirations.

According to him, while Nigeria has recorded progress in several areas, patriotism demands the courage to confront its shortcomings, including leadership failures, institutional weaknesses, corruption, policy inconsistency, inadequate infrastructure, insecurity and over-dependence on raw material exports.

Jonathan challenged Nigeria to learn from countries such as South Korea, India and Singapore, which had made remarkable advancement in industrialisation, technology, education, healthcare and human development.

He noted that Nigeria’s enormous human and natural resources should have translated into comparable levels of development, questioning the obstacles that had continued to constrain the country’s potential.

Distinguishing between independence and nation-building, Jonathan said that while winning independence was a historic achievement, building a prosperous, united and developed country remained an unfinished national responsibility.

Looking ahead to Nigeria’s centenary of independence in 2060, he urged the present generation to begin asking what kind of country it intended to bequeath to future generations.

He said the next 34 years must be used to establish measurable national development targets, strengthen institutions and build a productive economy capable of creating opportunities for young Nigerians.

The former president also called for renewed commitment to Pan-Africanism, stressing that political independence must be complemented by economic emancipation, technological advancement, educational development and stronger continental integration.

He particularly urged young Nigerians to see themselves as inheritors of the nationalist struggle, noting that the responsibility of advancing the ideals of freedom now rested on their shoulders through innovation, enterprise, civic participation and responsible citizenship.

Outlining four critical areas requiring urgent attention, Jonathan called for comprehensive democratic reforms to strengthen popular participation, the rule of law, judicial independence, human rights and accountability.

He also advocated reforms in political recruitment, insisting that competence, capacity and merit must take precedence over ethnic, religious and regional considerations in the selection of political leaders.

On education, he called for a functional system that would prioritise technological advancement, innovation and knowledge production, adding that Nigerian universities must aspire to compete among the world’s leading institutions rather than remaining largely centres of knowledge consumption.

He further emphasised the need to build strong, credible and independent institutions, stressing that sustainable national development would depend on strong institutions rather than the influence of individual leaders.

Recalling the controversy surrounding Nigeria’s 2014 centenary celebrations, Jonathan said he had supported the commemoration in spite of criticisms from those who believed the country had not achieved sufficient progress to justify celebrating its 100 years of amalgamation.

He explained that the importance of remembering history lies in understanding the nation’s journey, assessing its present condition and drawing lessons for a better future.

The former president urged the organisers of the colloquium to move beyond historical reflections and generate concrete recommendations for repositioning Nigeria ahead of its 100th independence anniversary. (NAN)

World.title: Nigerian Mission hits back at Magwenya, insists Ramaphosa intervened
World.content:
Fani-Kayode

The Nigerian High Commission in South Africa has renewed its defence of newly accredited High Commissioner, Chief Femi Fani-Kayode, insisting that President Cyril Ramaphosa personally intervened in the controversy surrounding the presentation of his diplomatic credentials.

The mission was responding to South African Presidency spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, who accused Fani-Kayode of lying about Ramaphosa’s intervention following a disagreement over the omission of his address during Friday’s credentials presentation ceremony in Tshwane.

In a strongly worded statement posted on X, the Nigerian High Commission accused Magwenya of making provocative and undiplomatic remarks, warning that his comments could undermine diplomatic relations between both countries.

The commission said Magwenya had accused Fani-Kayode of lying and disgracing Nigeria barely hours after the envoy presented his letters of credence to the South African President.

“You are the disgrace and no-one else. Outside of that your insolence and ignorance knows no bounds. You are bringing your nation into disrepute and wilfully and purposely burning the bridge of peace and reconciliation. That is a matter of concern to us,” the mission said.

The controversy followed the apparent disruption of the South African Presidency’s YouTube livestream around the time Fani-Kayode was due to present his letters of credence to Ramaphosa.

The broadcast subsequently resumed when the South African President was addressing the ambassadors.

Fani-Kayode, who was the last diplomat to present his credentials, had expressed displeasure over the omission of his address from the ceremony.

He said he subsequently spoke with Ramaphosa, who apologised and assured him that everything was fine.

However, Magwenya disputed the Nigerian envoy’s account, prompting the Nigerian mission to insist that the South African President intervened to resolve the disagreement.

The commission also recalled an earlier controversy in which Magwenya reportedly described concerns expressed by President Bola Tinubu and Ghanaian President John Mahama over xenophobia and Afrophobia in South Africa as fake news.

It said Nigeria had ignored the earlier remarks but questioned why Magwenya would publicly describe its newly accredited envoy as a liar.

“Did you really expect him to simply stomach your ill manners and keep quiet? If so you have misunderstood the character and nature of the Nigerian. We cannot be easily cowed,” the statement added.

The mission further disclosed that several people, including newly accredited ambassadors from other countries, witnessed the proceedings and expressed displeasure over what transpired.

It also claimed to possess a full video recording of the proceedings after the official photographs were taken, adding that it could release the footage if authorised to do so.

Defending Ramaphosa’s handling of the disagreement, the commission said the South African President personally stepped in to resolve the matter and directed the relevant officials and state broadcaster to address the situation.

“Thankfully your President had the decency and presence of mind to put out the fire and direct you and your state broadcaster to do the right thing. He literally saved the day,” it said.

The Nigerian High Commission urged Magwenya to exercise restraint and allow diplomatic channels to resolve the disagreement, stressing that Nigeria remained interested in preserving cordial relations between both countries.

It, however, warned against further escalation of the controversy.

“To us this matter is closed but if you wish to escalate it you are welcome to do so and we are up to the task. A word is enough for the wise,” the commission declared.

World.title: Netanyahu says only unity government can guarantee Israel’s security
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (Photo: AFP)

Israel’s caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, as well as his vow to eliminate the threat from Iran.

A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government” to guarantee Israel’s security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”.

He said this government would be made up of parties that recognise Israel “as a state for the Jewish people”.

It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”.

With backing from 67 lawmakers following last month’s election, Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.

Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election.

Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the centre to the right, while excluding the Arab parties.

Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere”.

But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday.

World.title: Deputy Speaker Kalu Charges Abia APC Presidential Campaign Council To Deliver Votes For Tinubu, Shettima
World.content:
Ahead of the presidential campaign flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Abia State on Monday, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Kalu, has charged the members of the campaign council to work hard to ensure victory for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and all APC candidates in Abia State in the coming election.

Addressing the campaign council members made up of the party’s governorship candidate, Chief Eric Opah, party Chairman, Hon. Chijioke Chukwu, all the candidates of the APC in the elections, Directors and Secretaries of the campaign council directorates, stakeholders and indeed, members of the party in Abia State who converged on his country home, Bende on Friday, Kalu said that the party must ensure that President Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima win in the State.

He said: “We are working hard for ourselves. APC is a moving train. We are progressing. The party belongs to you and I. We are not doing one man show. We will work to make everyone proud and happy. We are working hard against all odds”.

The Deputy Speaker who is also the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign (South) 11 emphasized that a vote for the President is a vote for the reconstruction of Igbo land and for a seat in his government.

“A vote for Mr. President is a vote for the reconstruction of Ala Igbo. When we vote for him, we are voting for our seat in his government. So, we must ensure our votes count in this coming election. We must ensure Mr. President Tinubu and all our candidates in Abia win,” he said.

Kalu further announced that after the flag-off on Monday, the campaign will move into the nooks and crannies of the 17 local government areas with the Renewed Hope message, with rallies planned in all the local government areas.

“After the flag off on Monday, we will begin to enter the nooks and crannies of the local government areas with the renewed hope message. We will do rallies in all the local government areas. We are working hard for our vote. Everyone should get ready,” he said.

The Deputy Speaker stressed that every member of the council has work to do, assuring them of support.

“I want you to know we have work to do, each of us. We are here to support and stand by you. Why we need to flag-off is that without it, we cannot go to the trenches,” he said.

Kalu also directed members to secure buildings in their various local government areas and wards to serve as campaign headquarters for the Presidential campaign.

“I also encourage you to look for buildings in your various local government areas as campaign headquarters of the Presidential campaign for Mr. President. The same in your various Wards. We will do local government tours to campaign for Mr. President,” Kalu said.

The highpoints of the meeting included the distribution of APC branded T-shirts and other campaign materials to the stakeholders and members across the 17 local government areas of Abia State.

World.title: At APC Presidential Campaign Rally In Jos, Tinubu Orders Decisive Security Action Against Plateau Attackers
World.content:
.Pledges to rebuild all displaced communities

.Warns against political violence, assuring Nigerians of peaceful 2027 polls

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu at the weekend revisited the age-long communal attacks in Plateau State with a declaration that his government is taking stern security measures against those carrying out the dastardly acts in the state.

Speaking at the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Rally in Jos, the Plateau State capital on Saturday, the President outlined fresh measures to address the prolonged insecurity in Plateau State, where recurring attacks have resulted in killings, destruction of homes and displacement of several communities.

Tinubu disclosed that he had directed security agencies to intensify operations against those responsible for violent attacks and ensure restoration of lasting peace across the state.

His words: “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau.

“What we should be getting is prosperity, not havoc, not crisis. Our government is not elected to inflict wounds on one another or to bury people. We have to lift people up from adversity to prosperity”.

He stressed that the security arrangements would particularly target threats confronting rural communities, where farmers and other residents have been forced to abandon their homes and livelihoods.

According to him, 1,000 forest guards were undergoing training for deployment, while surveillance cameras earlier promised by his government had already been procured to enhance intelligence gathering, early warning systems and rapid response to security threats.

“We are reinforcing security deployment and strengthening coordination and rapid response.

“One thousand forest guards are undergoing training right now. You will feel them. You will see them. You will feel secure in your villages and communities.

“The surveillance cameras are already procured, as I promised. They will further strengthen early detection and early warning security operations”.

The President also pledged to rebuild communities destroyed by attacks and facilitate the return of internally displaced persons to their ancestral homes.

He said the Federal Government would work closely with Governor Caleb Mutfwang and other relevant stakeholders to rehabilitate affected settlements and restore normal economic and social activities.

Said he: “I assure those displaced that we will rebuild your communities. We will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your communities.

“To our displaced families, I say once again, government is working to see you return, to bring you back, to rebuild your communities.

“We will work with Caleb Mutfwang and other leaders to rebuild those communities and take you back to settle in the comfort of where you belong”.

Tinubu offered condolences to families who lost loved ones in the attacks and residents whose homes and livelihoods had been destroyed.

“Crises and attacks have inflicted deep wounds on Plateau. Too many lives have been lost, homes destroyed, communities displaced.

“To every bereaved family, every survivor and everyone unable to return home, I offer my heartfelt condolences for your loss and pray that only God will console you”, he said.

The President urged Plateau residents to live peaceful together and resist attempts to exploit their ethnic, religious or political differences.

According to him, the state’s recovery from years of conflict would depend on the willingness of its diverse communities to live together in mutual respect and work towards common development objectives.

“We are one single family created by the same God Almighty. We are just living in different rooms, speaking different languages and behaving in different ways, but living in different rooms and speaking different languages does not make us enemies of one another.

“We have to live together. We have to farm together. We have to build this Plateau and this country together. It is our responsibility to behave as brothers and sisters”, Tinubu further said.

The President also while assuring Nigerians that the 2027 polls will be peaceful, warned individuals and groups plotting to unleash violence or intimidate voters that his government will not tolerate any attempt to undermine the democratic process.

Government, he explained, will ensure adequate security for citizens to exercise their constitutional rights without fear, urging voters to disregard those seeking to provoke violence and turn out peacefully to cast their ballots.

He had, in an earlier statement on Friday, condemned violence accompanying political activities, directing security agencies to act firmly against individuals attempting to disrupt public order.

At the rally, Tinubu reiterated his determination to ensure a peaceful electoral atmosphere, urging the electorate not to allow threats of violence to discourage their participation in the democratic process.

He also canvassed for votes for APC candidates at all levels, encouraging voters to support the party in the presidential, governorship, National Assembly and state House of Assembly elections.

“APC, from top to bottom. APC, progress”, he stated.

Also speaking, Vice-President Kashim Shettima credited the progress in Plateau and nationwide to Tinubu’s “transformational and courageous leadership,” calling the president a unique leader.

Shettima praised Plateau residents for their contributions to Nigeria in education, agriculture, the military, trade, culture and sport. He described the people of the state as “a gift to the nation” and said the APC has returned to seek a renewed mandate.

He urged voters to support Tinubu, Plateau Governor Caleb Mutfwang and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

On his part, Senate President, Senator Godswill Akpabio said the creation of state police is in the pipeline as part of efforts to improve security across the country.

APC National Chairman, Nentawe Yilwatda, also cited the provision of surveillance cameras and forest guards among the federal government’s commitments to Plateau.

According to him, the state has benefited from the Federal Government in terms of roads, two army battalions, a brigade and four security command centres.

Yilwatda described Tinubu as a “promise keeper” and urged Plateau residents to support the president at the ballot box. He said federal projects and security measures showed that the administration had acted on commitments made to the state.

Governor Mutfwang welcomed Tinubu to Jos, describing Plateau as a home of peace and tourism and a state with a significant place in Nigeria’s political history.

He said Jos had hosted major political events and welcomed the president’s presence at the rally.

He thanked President Tinubu for federal support, particularly in road infrastructure, education and healthcare. He said his administration has been explaining the impact of federal initiatives to residents and expressed confidence that continued cooperation would benefit Plateau State.

Mutfwang also outlined state programmes designed to address employment, transport and security needs. He added that an initiative would create opportunities for about 2,000 young people to work remotely for organisations in the United States and Europe. He also referred to a tech-driven command centre to support crime detection and other security operations.

The governor said new CNG buses were being added to reduce transport difficulties for residents.

He acknowledged that security challenges remain and expressed hope that displaced people would be able to return to their ancestral homes with continued government intervention.

𝐃𝐢𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐫 𝐆𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐥 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 Pre𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐚𝐥 Cam𝐩𝐚𝐢𝐠𝐧 Cou𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐥, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, urged Plateau residents to vote for Tinubu, saying the president deserved another term.

He praised the administration’s economic management and said increased federal revenues would give governments more resources to deliver public goods.

Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Tajudeen Abbas also urged voters to re-elect Tinubu and Mutfwang. He said residents should compare and contrast the projects done by previous governments with what the current administration is doing today.

Former Plateau State governors Joshua Dariye and Simon Lalong, former Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives Ahmed Wase, and former deputy governor, Pauline Tallen separately pledged support for Tinubu.

They cited federal projects in the state and the appointment of Plateau indigenes to national positions, including Yilwatda’s election as APC national chairman.

World.title: Makinde: We Won’t Allow Religion to Divide Us Over 2027 Polls
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), ‘Seyi Makinde, on Saturday, said his administration will not allow religious differences to divide the people of the state, insisting that the people share a common ancestry and must remain united irrespective of their faith.

This is just as the League of Imams and Alfas in Yorubaland said it will not declare support for any politician or political party ahead of the 2027 general election.

Makinde, who made the declaration in Ibadan at the opening of a three-day conference for Imams, Alfas/Ulama, political office holders and traditional rulers, tagged, ‘Rabitah 2026,’ organised by the League of Imams and Alfas in Yorubaland (Rabitah tul Aimma wal Hulammai fii Biladi Yoruba), also appealed to Muslim leaders across the state to use their influence to promote unity, peace and political stability ahead of the elections.

The conference, with the theme, ‘The Responsibilities of Politicians and Electorate During and After Electoral Process,’ had in attendance prominent Islamic clerics, scholars, traditional rulers and political stakeholders from across the South-west.

Makinde noted that discussions surrounding the choice of the next governor of the state had intensified ahead of the elections, urging political and religious stakeholders not to allow such developments to create divisions along religious lines.

He said: “We won’t allow religion to divide us. Let us pray for our state and country because this is the period leading to the next election, when a new set of leaders will emerge.There is a lot of discussion going on right now about the choice of who will become the next governor.

“What matters most is that we must stay united. The progress of Oyo State is what is important to us, and I believe God will answer our prayers. For us in Oyo State, religion is not an issue.We have all religions in our various families, and we have always coexisted peacefully.”

Makinde further illustrated the historical and familial connections between Muslims and Christians in Oyo State, disclosing that his own family background reflected the religious diversity he was advocating.

“I, standing before you, am Oluseyi Makinde.

Makinde was my grandfather on my father’s side. My father’s name is Olatunbosun, and my grandfather, Makinde, lived and died as a Muslim. Those who are familiar with Oyo know this history.

“If I were to convene an extended family meeting this evening, about 65 per cent of those who would attend would be Muslims. I want to appeal to us that we must not allow ourselves to be divided along religious lines because we share the same ancestry and the same blood flows through our veins,” he said.

In support of the conference, the governor announced a donation of N50 million to the organisers, describing the gathering as an important platform for religious engagement and collective prayers for the state and the country.

He also called on Muslim clerics and traditional religious leaders to play a constructive role in the 2027 electoral process, noting that they would have a significant opportunity to engage voters before they make their choices at the polls.

The Chairman of the League’s Board of Trustees, Sheikh Muhammad Habibullah Adam Abdullahi El-Ilory, in his remarks at the event, said the organisation could not announce any preferred candidate or political platform ahead of the forthcoming elections, stressing that Islamic clerics were not politicians and that their responsibility was not to campaign for political office-seekers or parties but to pray for the emergence of credible leaders.

“We are religious leaders; we are not politicians, but we are the fathers of politicians. We will not declare support for any political party or politicians.We, the League of Imams and Alfas in Yorubaland, cannot declare support or announce our support for any politician or political party. We can only pray to God for Him to give us credible leaders,” he said.

The conference was attended by the APM governorship candidate in Oyo State, Hon. Bimbo Adekanmbi; his running mate, Mufutau Open Salawu; and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Alhaji Hazeem Gbolarumi.

Also present were the League’s President, Sheikh Jamiu Kewulere; Chief Imam of Ibadanland, Sheikh Abdulganiy Abubakar Agbotomokekere; Alfa Agba of Ibadanland, Sheikh Abdulbari Adetunji; Grand Mufti of Yoruba Land, Sheikh AbdulRasaq AbdulAzeez Ishola; Secretary-General of the League, Sheikh Mustapha Oseni Adewale Hamzat; Chairman, Oyo State Pilgrim Welfare Board (Muslim Wing), Sheikh Hashim Atere; and Prof. Kamil Olosho.

Others included the Aare Musulumi of Yorubaland, Alhaji Daud Akinola; the Soun of Ogbomosoland, Oba Afolabi Olaoye; the Onigbeti of Igbeti, Oba Bashir Abioye; and the Iyalode Adini of Yorubaland, Alhaja Sedeekat Aderibigbe, alongside other prominent Islamic clerics, scholars and Muslim faithful from Oyo, Osun, Ogun, Ekiti, Lagos and Ondo States.

World.title: Ondo APC Dismisses Division Claims, Rules Out Political Violence
World.content:
Fidelis David in Akure

The Ondo State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) yesterday dismissed claims of internal divisions within its ranks, declaring that its reconciliation efforts are yielding results as it mobilises support to secure at least one million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

The party also expressed confidence that its growing unity would translate into electoral victories for Tinubu and other APC candidates, insisting that no member or interest group had been excluded from its ongoing reconciliation and mobilisation efforts.

Speaking at a press conference at the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) Press Centre in Akure, the state chairman, Mr. Babatunde Kolawole, dismissed reports of rivalry among party leaders, maintaining that members remained part of the same political family.

He argued that there was no reason for political rivalry, particularly as Ondo State would not conduct a governorship election in 2027 and Tinubu had already emerged as the party’s sole presidential candidate.

“Therefore, there is no rivalry. There is no cause for alarm. I can assure you we are on top of it and everything will be okay,” Kolawole said.

The chairman appreciated Tinubu, the APC National Chairman, Senate Leader, Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, and other party leaders for their support and contributions to strengthening the party.

Also speaking, the Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign in Ondo State, Victor Olabimtan, said the reconciliation committee constituted after the party congress had reached out to party organs, interest groups and individuals within and outside the state.

He disclosed that the committee had visited Abuja to engage some party leaders and extended its consultations to Lagos and other parts of the country, adding that the participation of previously estranged leaders, including Wale Akinterinwa and Princess Oladunni Odu, at the recent presidential campaign rally in Ondo State demonstrated the progress made.

Olabimtan said he had personally reached out to some aggrieved members, while Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa had made the unification of all tendencies within the party a major priority.

“Nobody is left out. All we need to do is to ensure that we put more effort into strengthening the existing unity that we are all enjoying in the party today,” he said.

He expressed confidence that the reconciliation drive would consolidate the party’s electoral strength and deliver victories for Tinubu, senators, members of the House of Representatives and candidates for the state and national assemblies.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner for Women Affairs, Dr. Seun Osamaye, pledged the mobilisation of women across Ondo State to secure at least one million votes for Tinubu, attributing the anticipated support to the Federal Government’s interventions in women’s economic empowerment, education and social protection.

Osamaye said the state had benefited from more than 20 interventions under the Renewed Hope initiatives of the President and First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu.

She listed the distribution of 10,000 professional kits to nurses and professional healthcare assistants, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), youth agribusiness initiatives and the Every Home Garden programme among the interventions, adding that thousands of women had also benefited from economic empowerment programmes.

“For the first time, government is not for the privileged few. Many women now benefit without having to beg or lobby,” she said.

The commissioner expressed optimism that the interventions would translate into unprecedented electoral support for Tinubu on January 16, 2027, insisting that women across the state were prepared to work collectively towards the target.

She also dismissed suggestions of strained relations among party leaders, describing Princess Oladunni Odu, the state’s first female Secretary to the State Government, as a respected leader with whom she maintained a cordial relationship.

Osamaye further described Governor Aiyedatiwa as the undisputed leader of the APC in the state, enjoying the support of party members.

On concerns about political violence ahead of the 2027 elections, APC chieftain, Chief Olusola Oke, maintained that Ondo State remained peaceful, insisting that no opposition member or political party had been attacked by political thugs.

Oke, who commended the media for its vigilance and professionalism, said reports of rising political thuggery in other parts of the country did not reflect the situation in Ondo State.

World.title: Chemical Engineers Urge FG to Revive Ajaokuta Steel to Save $4bn Annually
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The Nigerian Society of Chemical Engineers (NSChE) has called for the urgent revival of the moribund Ajaokuta Steel Company, warning that Nigeria loses about $4 billion annually to steel imports while missing out on millions of jobs and enormous industrial development opportunities.

The Society said reviving the steel complex through a transparent, private sector-led investment arrangement would significantly reduce the country’s dependence on imported steel, conserve foreign exchange, stimulate mining and manufacturing, and accelerate infrastructure development.

National President of NSChE, Bayo Olarewaju-Alo, made the call at the Society’s 56th Annual Conference, Annual General Meeting and Exhibition in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, yesterday.

Olarewaju-Alo disclosed that Nigeria’s annual steel demand stood at approximately 10 million tonnes, while domestic production was only about 1.2 million tonnes, largely from scrap-based operations.

He described the situation as a major economic setback, arguing that the country’s continued dependence on imported steel was draining its foreign reserves and undermining the development of indigenous industrial capacity.

“In my briefing, I stated that currently Nigeria imports about 10 million tons per annum of steel. That’s our need. If we have our own steel-making industry, we wouldn’t be importing that amount of steel. Rather, we’d be saving about $4 billion in foreign exchange,” he said.

He stressed that the benefits of reviving Ajaokuta would extend beyond foreign exchange savings to employment generation, improved infrastructure, technological advancement and stronger industrial capacity.

“The multiplier effect is that we will create a lot of jobs, not just for engineers, but all categories of people. People will be supplying materials that are required. People will be engaged in mining coal and iron ore,” he added.

According to him, a functional Ajaokuta would stimulate activities across the mining, transportation, power, engineering and manufacturing sectors, while strengthening the country’s capacity to execute major infrastructure projects.

“There is no country in the world that has very good infrastructure development that does not need steel input. Any major project to be executed in Nigeria will require steel input,” he said.

To achieve this, the NSChE president advocated majority private ownership by a Nigerian consortium or conglomerate, supported by strategic technical partners and a minority Federal Government stake.

He, however, warned that changing ownership alone would not guarantee success, insisting that investors must have access to reliable iron ore, natural gas, electricity, transportation infrastructure, financing and sustainable markets.

The Society recommended transparent privatisation through competitive international bidding, resolution of Ajaokuta’s legacy liabilities and contractual disputes, and enforceable agreements for critical production inputs.

It also proposed a phased rehabilitation programme, beginning with the restoration of existing rolling mills using imported billets within the first three years to generate revenue, rebuild technical capacity and restore investor confidence.

The Society further urged investors to evaluate conventional blast-furnace technology alongside gas-based direct-reduced iron and electric arc furnace technology, noting that Nigeria’s natural gas resources could provide a competitive advantage.

Olarewaju-Alo said gas was equally critical to the country’s industrial transformation, not only as an energy source for steel production but also as feedstock for fertilisers, methanol, hydrogen and petrochemicals.

He maintained that increased domestic gas utilisation could support manufacturing, improve electricity supply and strengthen Nigeria’s energy security.

The conference themed, ‘Advancing Nigeria’s Industrial Revolution Through Gas Valorisation and AI-Driven Engineering Imperatives’, also examined artificial intelligence, smart manufacturing, energy efficiency and indigenous technological development.

The Society called on the federal government to prioritise gas infrastructure, local equipment fabrication, research commercialisation and responsible adoption of artificial intelligence to accelerate industrialisation.

It urged policymakers and investors to move beyond repeated promises and translate the Ajaokuta revival agenda into a commercially viable industrial project.

“Ajaokuta must become a productive industrial asset whose output serves Nigeria’s development. The time for a private sector-led revival is now,” the Society declared.
