World.title: NAWOJ Tasks Members On Maternal, Child Health Reporting
World.content:
Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi

The Nigeria Association of Women Journalists (NAWOJ) has called on female journalists to intensify reporting on maternal and child health issues to promote public awareness, strengthen advocacy and hold relevant authorities accountable for healthcare delivery.

The Chairperson of NAWOJ Bauchi State chapter, Rashida Yusuf, made the call during a training on maternal and child health reporting organised for members of the association in the state on Thursday.

Yusuf said female journalists had a critical responsibility to give visibility to issues affecting women and children, particularly at the grassroots level.

“As female journalists, we have a very important role to play in promoting maternal and child health by giving visibility to issues affecting women and children,” she said.

She stressed the need for journalists to amplify the voices of women and children while ensuring that government and relevant authorities were held accountable for their policies, programmes and interventions.

“We must also amplify the voices of women and children to ensure that their concerns are heard and that they have access to the information and awareness they need, especially at the grassroots level,” Yusuf added.

She urged members to move beyond event coverage to sustained, solution-driven reporting that puts pressure on policymakers to improve healthcare services for women and children.

World.title: Lalong, Dariye, Badaru Lead Plateau Leaders to Back Tinubu’s Second Term
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

Former governors Simon Lalong and Joshua Dariye, alongside other political heavyweights in Plateau State, have thrown their weight behind President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

The leaders, under the banner of Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), endorsed Tinubu at a high-level stakeholders’ meeting in Jos on Thursday, pledging to deliver massive votes for the All Progressives Congress (APC) across the state.

The meeting held yesterday in Jos brought together former ministers, former senators, former members of the House of Representatives, former commissioners and former local government chairmen.

By voice vote, participants unanimously adopted Tinubu, the Plateau State Governor and all other APC candidates for the forthcoming elections.

The meeting, chaired by Lalong, who is Deputy Chairman of the A4A Board of Trustees, also resolved to ensure the APC wins all elective positions in the state.

Lalong told the gathering that stakeholders were convinced Tinubu is committed to Nigeria’s development.

He said the President’s continued leadership would guarantee accelerated socio-economic growth and national transformation.

Dariye, in his remarks, commended the Tinubu administration for what he described as its contributions to Plateau State and the country.

According to him, President Tinubu deserved another term to consolidate on the achievements of his administration.

Also, the Director General of A4A and former Governor of Jigawa State, Badaru Abubakar, said the North should repay Tinubu’s spirit of equity, fairness and political inclusion with overwhelming support in 2027.

Badaru said he was satisfied with the commitment shown by the Plateau stakeholders, describing the endorsement as a major boost for the APC’s chances in Plateau and across Northern Nigeria.

He expressed optimism that the political commitment on display would translate into millions of votes for Tinubu and other APC candidates.

The meeting closed with a renewed pledge by A4A and its Plateau stakeholders to sustain political mobilisation, grassroots engagement and coordinated efforts to secure victory for the APC in 2027.

World.title: Seychelles Ambassador, St.Ange, Travels to Madagascar to Woo Investors
World.content:
Charles Ajunwa

Following an official initiative by the Chairman of the Board of the Madagascar’s Diego Suarez Regional Tourism Office, Dr Herilaza Hugues Randrianjohany, who addressed the President of the Republic of Seychelles, His Excellency Dr Patrick Herminie, on 16 August 2026, through the island’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Diaspora, and after receiving approval from the Seychellois government via Mrs. Sherin Francis of the Ministry of Tourism and Culture of Seychelles, the Diego Suarez Regional Tourism Office, in collaboration with the Madagascar National Tourism Office,

will host a high-level delegation from November 15 to 20, 2026.

Alain St.Ange, Seychelles’ Tourism Ambassador-at-Large, will lead the delegation. It will also include Mr Pascal Viroleau, Chief Executive Officer of the Vanilla Islands organisation. Ambassador St.Ange is remembered in the Indian Ocean Islands Group as one of the founding tourism personalities responsible for creating the Indian Ocean Vanilla Islands Organisation and served as its First President.

St.Ange, regarded as a tourism expert, has been invited to help guide Madagascar’s Diego Suarez Regional Tourism to become a stronger player in the Indian Ocean tourism region.

The mission will begin in Antananarivo with meetings with the Malagasy government to present the initiative to the highest authorities, reaffirm Madagascar’s role in the regional Vanilla Islands strategy, and secure the institutional support required for its implementation. The delegation will then travel to northern Madagascar, where an extensive programme will showcase the region’s tourism assets. The visit will begin at the Red Tsingy, a remarkable laterite formation sculpted by erosion from the Irodo River, followed by a tour of Diego Suarez, which will highlight its historical identity, cultural atmosphere, and high-quality hospitality infrastructure. On the second day, the guests will visit the Montagne des Français and the famous Three Bays, then enjoy lunch in Ramena, focusing on local cuisine and gastronomic tourism.

A key highlight of the mission will be a meeting at the Grand Hotel, bringing together local authorities, tourism operators, institutional partners, private-sector stakeholders, and the Tourism Office. Discussions will focus on practically integrating regional tourism products into combined Vanilla Islands travel itineraries.

Beyond the programme itself, the visit is expected to pave the way for several important developments for the destination: the creation of integrated tourism products that fully showcase Madagascar, the establishment of B2B partnerships with targeted tour operators and travel agencies, and the strengthening of northern Madagascar’s credibility in an increasingly competitive international tourism market.

Madagascar tourism is banking on Alain St.Ange’s extensive network to provide privileged access to key source markets and cruise companies. At the same time, the mission also aims to mobilise institutions and investors for hotel and infrastructure projects. Supported by the reputation of its two prominent guests, the initiative further seeks to generate lasting international media exposure commensurate with the destination’s potential.

World.title: Miss South Africa 2026 – meet your new queen!
World.content:
Miss South Africa 2026 has been crowned, and she is Tiyani Makamu.

The 27-year-old communications professional and entrepreneur succeeds 2025 title-winner Qhawekazi Mazaleni.

MEET THE MISS SOUTH AFRICA WINNER

Tiyani Makamu was crowned Miss South Africa at a glittering finale at the Sandton Convention Centre, hosted by former pageant queen Jo-Ann Strauss and Lawrence Maleka.



Her first and second princesses are Cwenga Koyana Kotu-Rammopo and Lesego Khumo Nyathela, respectively.

Tiyani is a 27-year-old Group Digital Lead and Client Success Executive who has a degree in PR and Corporate Communications.

Her advocacy is centred on entrepreneurship and skills development, youth unemployment, and expanding access to education and knowledge.

The Top 5 also included rugby WAG Simone Tshituka and singer and model Makhosazana Azana Masango.

PRIZES

The 2026 Miss South Africa winner not only receives a crown and title, but also a R1 million cash prize and R500 000 in dedicated funding for her social-impact projects.

The First Princess receives a R250 000 cash award and a dedicated R150 000 Impact Fund, whilst the Second Princess gets a R150 000 cash award and a dedicated R100 000 Impact Fund.

The top three contestants will also receive executive development opportunities, mentorship, wellness support, access to regional and international leadership networks, and the opportunity to lead initiatives focused on education, entrepreneurship, health, and youth development.

World.title: Curro commits R500k to get SA swimmers to Beijing World Aquatics Championships
World.content:
Curro commits R500k for 21 swimmers to travel to Beijing to attend the World Aquatics Championships. Image via Facebook

Curro, South Africa’s largest network of independent, private schools, has pledged half a million to help 21 swimmers – including Olympian Chad le Clos – travel to the World Aquatics Championships in Beijing.

This comes after the sporting federation, Swimming South Africa (SSA), issued a notice calling for each swimmer to contribute R55,000 each towards their trip – or risk losing their places on the team. It also comes in the wake of gold medallist Tatjana Smith announcing her decision to switch sporting nationalities to the Netherlands, citing her grievances with SSA.

The sporting tournament takes place between 1 and 6 November.



CURRO PLEDGES R500K TO GET SWIMMERS TO BEIJING WORLD AQUATICS CHAMPIONSHIPS

In a statement, Curro announced it would commit R500 000 to send the 21 South African national swimmers to the World Aquatics Championships in Beijing next month.

Additionally, the independent schools network would host a national training camp in 2027 for the South African team and Swimming South Africa (SSA) to work with their top swimmers at Curro clinics, assisting school coaches and learners.

Curro CEO Cobus Loubser said: “We are patriotic South Africans, and we feel compelled to assist the team.



“This sponsorship helps dreams come true for swimmers who have worked their whole lives for this opportunity. It speaks to what Curro does: we create opportunities and help prepare learners for a hopeful future. Next year should be an exciting year for Curro’s thousands of young swimmers when they meet and train with their heroes.”

CONTROVERSIAL TRAVEL ARRANGEMENT COSTS

This week, news broke that SSA had issued 21 South African swimmers with a notice to pay up to R55 000 for travel and accommodation to attend the World Aquatics Championships in Beijing next month.



Swimmers were required to fork out a R40,000 deposit by 10 November and pay the remaining R15,000 by 25 November.

Those who chose to arrange their own international flights are required to pay R37,000 towards accommodation and management costs.

Additionally, swimmers are required to pay for their Chinese visas, International travel and domestic flights to Johannesburg.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs new signing reportedly goes AWOL
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs winger Faiz Abrahams has reportedly gone AWOL after failing to report for duty ahead of the club’s Carling Knockout Cup clash against Mamelodi Sundowns.

Amakhosi players regrouped on Thursday before travelling to Polokwane for a mini-camp as they prepare for the upcoming encounter. The squad is expected to return to Johannesburg on Sunday.

The 21-year-old winger, who joined Chiefs this season, was reportedly absent from the travelling squad.



Kaizer Chiefs star refuses to return to training?

According to FARPost, Abrahams has yet to report for duty following the team’s short break.

“FARPost also understands from reliable sources that the 21-year-old is yet to report for duty following the squad’s short break. Amakhosi regrouped on Thursday before travelling to Polokwane for a mini-camp, with the team expected to return to Johannesburg on Sunday. However, Abrahams was notably absent from the travelling squad,” the publication reported.

His absence comes amid reports that he has refused to return to the Chiefs camp. Sources reportedly told FARPost that the youngster has made it clear that he no longer wants to play football.

Abrahams joined Kaizer Chiefs on loan from Stellenbosch FC in August. However, he has struggled to secure regular playing time, making only a handful of appearances and scoring just once this season.

His reported absence is another concern for Amakhosi as they prepare for their cup assignment against Sundowns.

Kaizer Chiefs are yet to release an official statement or comment on the reports surrounding the winger’s alleged absence.



Should Abrahams get released?

World.title: From stress to illness: Factors driving men in Eswatini to suicide
World.content:
Speaking in parliament during discussions on the second-quarter performance reports, Mbabane East MP Welcome Dlamini outlined the key factors driving men in Eswatini to commit suicide.

With gender-based violence (GBV) at an all-time high in the country, Dlamini urged the government to also give equal attention and support to men who feel overwhelmed by their challenges, since most existing programmes do not fully cater to men.

MEN LEAD SUICIDE STATS IN ESWATINI

According to Swazi Daily News, the MP revealed that 42 men committed suicide over the last three months. He said the concerning pattern calls for practical solutions and meaningful engagement with men.



Dlamini said men grapple with a range of challenges, including unemployment, illness, domestic and social isolation.

He added that stress remains a dominant factor, as many men may feel emasculated when they are unable to provide for their loved ones due to debt, unemployment or the cost of living.

PROPOSED SOLUTIONS

The MP not only raised concerns around GBV and men’s mental health but also proposed practical solutions.



He suggested an “on-the-ground” approach that engages directly with men, including in communities, churches, social spaces and workplaces.

His proposals also included counselling, creating support groups, as well as a partnership between the health sector and the police.

He said this collaboration would ensure that men in distress receive the professional care they need and that their cases are treated with dignity and compassion.

World.title: Is Jägermeister leaving South African shelves?
World.content:
Is Jägermeister being discontinued in South Africa? Image via Facebook

A circular claiming that Jägermeister, a German liqueur, is being withdrawn from South African shelves has gone viral on social media.

But is it true?

JÄGERMEISTER NOTICE GOES VIRAL ON SOCIAL MEDIA

On the X app, an image of a notice about Jägermeister being discontinued, or at least withdrawn from South Africa, has gone viral.



The notice reads: “Jägermeister wishes to inform our valued consumers, retail partners and distributors that, following an internal review of our South African market operations, a decision has been made to discontinue the distribution of Jägermeister products in South Africa.

“Effective 31 January 2027, Jägermeister will no longer be supplied to liquor retailers, wholesalers or distributors across the country.

The notice added that “existing stock will remain available while supplies last”. It added that “once depleted, no further stock will be distributed”



In the fine print under the notice read the following: “This is a prank and is not an official statement from Jägermeister.

“No product discontinuation has been confirmed”.

Jagermeister is leaving SOUTH AFRICA@casspernyovest Don Billiato is about to double it’s profit



Get ready for the Ferarri bro bro pic.twitter.com/iPsHEgsV34  November 14, 2026

‘NOT GOING ANYWHERE’

According to Jägermeister South Africa’s Facebook and Instagram page, the circular is fake news.

A post referenced the notice, stating: “Still here, not going anywhere. Discontinued? Never that. Always read the fine print”.

The liqueur is manufactured by Mast-Jägermeister in Germany, with a South African office in Sandton that is responsible for local marketing and sales.



It is imported by Nu-World Industries.

World.title: South Africa recall Hamza for Bangladesh Test
World.content:
Zubayr Hamza will play in his first Test match in more than two years when he lines up for South Africa against Bangladesh in the first Test starting at the Wanderers on Sunday. Image: AFP

Zubayr Hamza will play in his first Test match in more than two years when he lines up for South Africa against Bangladesh in the first Test starting at the Wanderers on Sunday.

Captain Temba Bavuma said Hamza would bat at number three in place of David Bedingham, who was dropped after the series against Australia last month.

READ | Temba Bavuma set to extend remarkable Test captaincy record



Also dropped

In the only other change from the team that clinched the series against Australia with a 176-run win in the third Test in Cape Town, seam bowler Dane Paterson replaces Gerald Coetzee, who is also dropped.

Fast bowler Anrich Nortje, who played in the first two Tests against Australia, is in the squad but has still not fully recovered from a groin injury, Bavuma said.

Off-spinner Simon Harmer, who was man of the match in Cape Town, remains as the sole specialist spinner ahead of long-time incumbent Keshav Maharaj.



Hamza, 31, played for a below-strength South African team in a series in New Zealand in 2023/24 but has not played in a home Test since appearing against England in January 2020.

Hamza served a nine-month ban after testing positive for a banned substance in 2022, which he said was the result of accidentally taking medication prescribed for his father.

“He has gone back and done what he can in domestic cricket,” said Bavuma.



“He’s scored runs in all formats.”

Home ground

Hamza plays his domestic cricket for the Gauteng Lions, whose home ground is the Wanderers.

Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto said his team would be finalised on the morning of the match but said it was likely they would pick three seam bowlers and one specialist spinner.



“I think I can say that there will be three pacers,” said Shanto.

“There must also be a spinner.”

Although South Africa will be strong favourites, Shanto said Bangladesh took confidence from recent performances as well as a one-day series win in South Africa in 2021/22.



Bavuma said that it was important for South Africa to maintain the standards of world Test champions as they aim to reach the next final in 2027.

“We are halfway on our journey and we are still looking at ways we can improve,” he said.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Discontinuation claims about popular drink turn out to be a prank
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africans were briefly left wondering whether a popular party favourite was about to disappear from shelves.

This comes after a statement claiming that Jägermeister would be discontinued began circulating online.

The statement, dated 9 November, claimed that the decision followed an internal review of South African market operations, with 31 January 2027 set as the final date.

But there was a catch.

World.title: From heatwave to thunderstorm: Heavy downpours expected in these areas
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Weather Service has issued a warning for severe thunderstorms and heavy downpours across parts of the country this weekend.

The warning, valid from this afternoon, is expected over Free State, North West, Gauteng, Mpumalanga, KwaZulu-Natal, and Limpopo.

For the Western Cape, a Yellow Level 1 warning of damaging winds for Saturday has been issued.

It comes after a week of heatwaves in various areas.

READ | Joburg residents urged to take precautions as heatwave continues

The City’s Emergency Management Services has urged residents, particularly those in low-lying areas, to avoid crossing flooded roads, rivers and streams.

Emergency Services spokesperson Robert Mulaudzi extended the same caution to motorists.

“We are pleading with our residents, especially those in our low-lying areas, to avoid crossing rivers and streams while conducting their daily activities. “We encourage our motorists to exercise caution while driving, extend a safe following distance and try to avoid crossing flooded roads and low-lying bridges.”

Mulaudzi said emergency service authorities will remain on high alert, monitoring all seven regions of the city for any emergencies which might occur.

World.title: No major incidents reported as matric exams near end
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Department of Basic Education is gearing up for the marking phase as the 2026 National Senior Certificate examinations near their end.

To date, the department's spokesperson, Terence Khala, said they have noted a few minor incidents reported, but none are serious enough to affect the integrity of the examinations.

READ | Senior teachers opt for early retirement as government trims wage bill

This is as he points to taxi violence in the Western Cape and scholar transport challenges in Gauteng as some of the issues experienced during the examination period.

But upon being notified of this, the department acted.

“The sector kicked in and was able to make sure that the requisite protocols were put in place. Learners in Gauteng were able to write adequately and equally in the Western Cape. “And I think it's only for us to commend the system and commend every individual that forms part of the system that assists us to make sure that we can really take this massive undertaking and make it a seamless one,” Khala said.

Markers, according to the department, will get to work on 1 December.

World.title: Six people killed in head-on collision on Eastern Cape N2
World.content:
At least six people have died in a horror crash on the N2 in the Eastern Cape.

The victims were travelling in a minibus taxi when it collided head-on with a truck on Saturday morning.

Provincial transport spokesperson Unathi Binqose said the minibus taxi was travelling from Alice towards Bizana while the truck was travelling from Kokstad towards Mzamba when the accident happened.

"Preliminary information suggests that the Toyota Quantum crossed into the path of the oncoming truck, resulting in a head-on collision. "There is also a suspicion that driver fatigue may have contributed to the crash. However, the exact circumstances surrounding the collision remain subject to police investigation," he said.

Three others were seriously injured, while three others sustained slight injuries.

"The injured were attended to by emergency services and transported for medical treatment".

The victims are believed to be university students travelling home to Bizana.

This comes just a day after seven people died in another crash on the N2 near Ndabakazi.

World.title: Madlanga Commission hears ex-JMPD top cop allegedly forced officers to take bribe
World.content:
PRETORIA - A major drug bust operation in Johannesburg has led to explosive testimony at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.

The commission heard on Friday how former JMPD superintendent Phineas Manyama allegedly instructed officers to release suspects and accept whatever money was offered in return.

READ | LIVE | JMPD corruption under the spotlight at Madlanga

Testifying at the commission Tactical Response Unit officer Michael Potsane said refusing the instruction came with threats of dismissal, arrest or even death.

He testified that he regarded the instruction as unlawful and did not comply with it.

World.title: Hot weather, dry taps, fuming Joburg residents
World.content:
SOWETO - Water shortages are worsening across various parts of Johannesburg, with residents reporting days without water supply amid the heatwave.

In Soweto, one resident detailed how the community has been without water since Tuesday, with supply returning briefly during the early hours of the morning.

“We've been having challenges with water in this community whereby each and every weekend we don't have water at all. It is becoming a new normal now,” the resident said.

The resident adds that the situation becomes more concerning during the current heatwave when residents need water the most.

“We are encouraged to drink more water because people are going to suffer because of dehydration, but at this particular moment, Joburg Water is not doing justice to us."

He said adding to the frustration is the lack of communication between Joburg Water and residents.

READ | Joburg residents urged to take precautions as heatwave continues

In a statement on Saturday, Joburg Water said bulk supply meters in the Roodepoort and Soweto regions, which were closed on Thursday to rescue and boost bulk supply levels, commenced reopening on Friday afternoon.

The water utility said it is worth noting that systems were not fully opened but taken back to their original curtailment before being fully closed on Thursday.

“While some bulk supplier systems have stabilised and recovered, there are still several systems which will take time to recover over the next few days. The recovery is also impacted by the demand for the system as they are integrated. “The affected Johannesburg Water reservoirs will first need to fill to acceptable levels before the system stabilises. Customers may experience low pressure or intermittent supply and, in some cases, no water until the system recovers,” the statement read.

In the meantime, Joburg Water said alternative water arrangements are being made and deployed through the central and regional coordination groups.

World.title: A grave clash: One family's search, many families' pain
World.content:
LICHTENBURG - A quest for closure for one family has thrown Boikhutso’s cemetery in Lichtenburg, North West and countless other families into chaos and heartache.

The families claim graves were disturbed and their dignity upended during an exhumation process conducted by the North West Department of Health after it got a court order in June 2023 to dig up graves, searching for a man missing from the old Thusong Hospital.

It was suspected that he had died and received a pauper’s burial at this cemetery.

However, families say the process has left the cemetery in disarray, with some unable to identify the graves of their relatives.

Mmakhumo Moja’s family is among those affected.

READ | Fort Jackson SAPS building turns into haven for criminals

She says both her parents’ graves have since vanished, lost in the shuffle. They found the graves disturbed, soil scattered and headstones missing.

"We want our graves, and we want to know exactly where they are located. After the exhumation, we were supposed to come and clean up, but we didn't know whose graves we were cleaning. When we're supposed to do some of our cultural rites at the grave, it's a problem. “When you carry out traditional rituals, you have to come to the ancestors and engage them. But the place is a mess; it's dug up, and there are holes everywhere,” Moja said.

The North West Health Department spokesperson Tebogo Lekgethwane insists it consulted some families ahead of the dig, and flat-out denies leaving the cemetery in shambles.

But three years on, the cemetery is still in a mess, and the family’s still waiting.

They’re holding out for answers, longing for restoration, and just a little respect for their dear departed.

eNCA Bafedile Moerane filed this report.

World.title: Fort Jackson SAPS building turns into haven for criminals
World.content:
MDANTSANE - Once a well-resourced police station where officers carried out their duties but today the Fort Jackson SAPS building in Mdantsane in the Eastern Cape has become a haven for criminal activity.

Criminals have taken over the building, vandalising offices that were meant to benefit the people of Mdantsane and surrounding areas.

This has left Mdantsane residents questioning how a government-owned building intended to strengthen policing could be allowed to deteriorate while crime escalates.

READ | Vandals savage Eastern Cape school

According to the community crime organisation, the Buffalo City Special Team Task Force, criminals have had easy access to the building since a taxi crashed into the perimeter fence earlier this year.

The full extend of the damage remains unclear, however police suspect opportunists trashed the premises after hours.

Eastern Cape police spokesperson Siphokazi Mawisa said following the incidents, cases were opened, and arrests were made.

"The cases are currently before court, and the suspects are out on bail,”she said.

Measures are being put in place to deploy police units that will utilise the building on a 24-hour basis to safeguard it.

eNCA's Ronald Masinda filed this report.
