World.title: Split Port Opens Brand New International Passenger Terminal
World.content:
November the 13th, 2026 – Split Port opened its brand new international passenger terminal this week, concluding a 20+ million euro project.

Split Port officially opened its new international passenger terminal this week, formally marking the completion of a project worth over 20 million euros. Poslovni reports that the extensive project was co-financed with non-repayable EU funds from the National Recovery and Resilience Plan.

a ground floor passenger reception

The former ugly, totally dilapidated building has finally been renovated into a modern passenger terminal, the construction of which has upgraded the port infrastructure and reorganised domestic and international traffic. The terminal was built due to the increase in capacity of the city port, where passenger traffic is almost four times higher and vehicle traffic three times higher than 25 years ago, the Split Port Authority pointed out. The new terminal covers more than 12,000 square metres, while the building itself has almost 3,000 square metres. On the ground floor there is space for receiving passengers, while the upper floor houses operational services, including the police, customs, and the security and port authority departments.

Vice Mihanović, director of the Split Port Authority, announced that the roof of the building will be opened to citizens and will contain public amenities such as a children’s playroom, an outdoor gym and a telescope.

“The facility is intended for international traffic, while domestic liner traffic will remain at the previous locations. With the construction of the terminal, we are relocating international traffic to the port breakwater, and we have repurposed the entire St. Duje Quay for domestic liner traffic,” Mihanović stated. St. Duje Quay spans over 10,000 square metres and six berths, and the re-purposing will improve travel conditions for islanders and domestic passengers and bring them closer to the city after disembarking from the ferry. The old terminal building has also been put into use for domestic traffic only.

the viewpoint and lungomare

Mihanović also announced four major projects of the Port Authority with a total value of almost 60 million euros, including the expansion of St. Peter’s Quay by more than 5,000 square metres and the construction of two new berths. Split Mayor Tomislav Šuta said that the construction of the terminal is a major step forward for the city and passengers, and announced the arrangement of a lungomare and viewpoint in that area.

World.title: Croatia Introduces Tougher Rules and Surveillance for Short-Term Rentals
World.content:
November the 13th, 2026 – Croatia is set to introduce much stricter rules and heightened surveillance for short-term rentals, with around 60,000 units in particular being under the state’s magnifying glass.

Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina stated recently that the Hospitality Activity Act, which has been sent for a second reading in Parliament, is one of the most important for tourism and a major step forward in its development. “With this law we want to achieve three fundamental goals: a strong step forward in suppressing unregistered activity, the complete digitalisation of all administrative procedures in tourism, and the introduction of order, transparency and an increase in the quality of the offer, especially in the category of short-term rental accommodation,” Glavina said after the government session.

Poslovni reports that he further explained that the most important goal – suppressing unregistered activity – is achieved through the law in several ways, one of which is the transposition into Croatian legislation of the European Commission regulation and the introduction of a digital registration number whose aim is to prevent service providers who do not have it from appearing and advertising on online platforms.

He assessed these platforms as very important because the largest tourist traffic comes from them, so among the goals is the introduction of more order into the ways they operate, because until now short-term rental and accommodation could be advertised and sold through them without a decision in the member state.

“The penalties for platforms that would ignore this are draconian and they will certainly make an effort across Europe, including in Croatia, to ensure that this does not happen,” Glavina said. He recalled that the new law expands the powers for supervising providers of this accommodation, in addition to the State Inspectorate, to the Customs Administration, cities and municipalities through the activities of municipal wardens, and it has also been agreed that all eventual revenues from fines will go entirely to the budgets of local and regional self-government units.

The State Inspectorate has also been given the possibility of secret supervision of classifieds, groups on social networks and similar, so that it can react and control the facilities. “This year we have significantly strengthened the activities of inspectors against unregistered activity, and when it enters into force, the law will contribute to this even more,” Glavina said. He repeated that private landlords and family accommodation are very important and that they have been accommodated.

When asked whether he knows how many registered apartments for rent to tourists there are in buildings, he said that he does not have exact data because until now no records have been kept of the type of facilities in which the apartments are located, which will change with the new law and digitalisation.

According to our estimate, that is around 60,000 facilities-apartments, Glavina said, noting that other EU countries are also struggling in various ways with short-term rental to tourists because it reduces the available housing stock.

Regarding the objections and complaints of small landlords and entrepreneurs to the draft law, he said that from 2016 until about a year and a half ago, the number of newly registered beds in short-term accommodation for tourists grew by around 25,000 every year, which led to the fact that, despite the growth of overall tourism, growth in that accommodation was smaller. That is why the steps forward with the law and responsible tourism policy were important, and that is why in the last two years we have not had growth in the number of those beds but even a slight decrease, and those beds have gone into long-term rental, which is also the goal of housing policy, Glavina concluded.

World.title: Croatia Will Need 100,000 New Hotel Beds Over the Next Decade
World.content:
November the 13th, 2026 – Croatia is going to need anywhere between 80,000 and 100,000 new hotel beds over the next decade, according to hotelier reps warn.

Croatia will need between 80,000 and 100,000 new hotel beds over the next ten years, hoteliers’ representatives warned at a recently held congress in Poreč. There’s an issue, however, as building new hotels is becoming increasingly difficult due to high land prices, expensive construction work, slow administration and shrinking opportunities for profit. Index reports that in Croatia currently, hotels currently account for only 9.2 percent of total accommodation capacity in Croatia, yet generate approximately a quarter of all tourist overnight stays. Hoteliers are therefore calling for the continuation of state incentives, better conditions for investment and measures that would attract more tourists outside the summer months.

croatia’s accommodation capacity poses an issue

Veljko Ostojić, president of the Association of Entrepreneurs in Croatian Hospitality and director of the Croatian Tourism Association, said that the hotel sector achieved good results this year, but that Croatia must change the structure of its tourist accommodation. “Croatian hospitality is the winner of this tourist year, not only according to physical indicators but also according to everything it does to raise the quality of Croatian tourism. However, the structure of our accommodation capacity is currently the biggest challenge,” Ostojić said. According to his estimate, Croatia should increase the number of hotel beds by 80,000 to 100,000 over the next decade. The problem, he warns, is that most investments relate to the renovation and reconstruction of existing hotels, while completely new hotel complexes on previously undeveloped land are almost not being built at all.

why are so few hotels being constructed in croatia?

Ostojić believes that investors are deterred by a combination of several problems, from the price of land and construction to slow administrative procedures and legal uncertainty. “The question is why there are practically no significant greenfield investments in Croatia. The reasons are numerous: the price of land, the slowness of administration, legal uncertainty, the cost of construction and the hotel business model itself. We must be open and realistic,” he said. He added that the space for new investments is getting smaller, which he considers bad for the long-term development of Croatian tourism. Hoteliers also warn of rising operating costs and declining profitability, which makes it increasingly difficult to find financially viable projects.

the interest in the height of summer is waning…

Ostojić also warned that tourist habits are changing. According to him, some guests are increasingly avoiding the busiest summer months because of the heat, high prices and excessive crowds in certain destinations. He believes Croatia must develop new tourist facilities, events and manifestations that would attract guests during spring and autumn. This would extend the tourist season, increase the occupancy of hotel capacities and reduce dependence on July and August alone, which many are now avoiding due to extreme temperatures and crowds.

Robert Pende, director of the Directorate for Entrepreneurship Development, Investments and Competitiveness at the Ministry of Tourism and Sport, said that the state has been encouraging investments in the hotel sector for years. The aim of these incentives is not only the construction of higher-quality accommodation but also the reduction of seasonality in Croatian tourism. Pende warned that Croatia still has one of the most pronounced seasonalities of tourism in the European Union.

“We want to change that, and investments are key to this,” he said, noting that 34 applications for projects with a total value of approximately 500 million euros have been received through the investment incentive system. This refers to the value of planned investments, not the amount of state support.

has croatia managed to retain its competitiveness?

Kristijan Staničić, director of the Croatian National Tourist Board, assessed that Croatia, despite global challenges and unpredictable circumstances on the tourist market, has retained its competitiveness among Mediterranean destinations. “The tourist year that is slowly coming to an end has shown that Croatia has retained its competitiveness. The results we have achieved confirm positive trends in tourist traffic, and a great deal of credit for this belongs precisely to hoteliers,” Staničić said. He added that new investments, raising the quality of service and the development of tourist destinations play an important role in the further development of Croatian tourism.

World.title: Tallinn's Reaalkool opens €32.7 million building, €10 million over budget
World.content:
Tallinn Secondary School of Science's (Tallinna Reaalkool) new teaching building has been in use since the start of the current academic year, but the ceremony to confirm that took place today. The municipal school building cost about €32.7 million — around €10 million more than planned.

The interior is light and calm: plenty of oak veneer, walls and furniture in pale tones or terracotta, a color that also appears on floor tiles in the 142-year-old main building, tying old and new together. Teachers helped the architects with the design.

"For me the most important thing about the interior was functionality," said head of studies and physics teacher Daniel Kaasik. Physics teachers at the school, he added, had had a say in what they wanted in their classrooms.

The school now has room for its pupils for the first time, too. "The older school building was built for 300 pupils. Now there are 950–1000," Kaasik noted.

There are three physics classrooms and four laboratories in the new building, as well as sound-absorbing ceilings, a separate floor for younger pupils, terraces and a courtyard, and a new underground gym. The school canteen is housed there too, and has been designated smartphone-free.

The City of Tallinn's property department said the original 2024 estimate of €22.3 million covered only the new extension, and that restoring the historic main building and archaeological excavations — budgeted at €300,000 but costing about €1.4 million — had been responsible for pushing the total up.

The work to build the new facility was also preceded by a major archaeological dig, rich in findings.

World.title: Prime minister: We have nothing to discuss with Russia on European security
World.content:
Russian leader Vladimir Putin wants to distract Europe with a sort of "bucket list" of his wants, rather than a lasting peace in Ukraine, Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) said.

Europe's security architecture is not open for negotiation, the prime minister noted, speaking at Friday's informal European Council in Dublin, Ireland.

Michal noted Estonia is providing Ukraine with an additional €6.5 million, including €4.5 million of locomotives and €2 million for recovery.

"Putin wants us to discuss his wish list instead of focusing on achieving peace in Ukraine," Michal said. "We have nothing to discuss with Russia about the European security architecture; it is working just fine. If we wanted to make any changes to it, they would only be that Ukraine becomes a member of the EU and NATO and that Russia stops killing people," he continued, via a press release.

The prime minister said his message to other leaders was to focus on what matters — peace in Ukraine — and not be distracted by Putin's attempts to divert attention.

At #EPC in Dublin, I called for stronger support for Ukraine through another harsh winter and more pressure on the Kremlin. Russia could stop the killing today and open the way to peace. Instead, it continues targeting civilians and essential services. On AI, Europe must catch up. We need more investment and better opportunities to test advanced models and assess their risks. AI will shape both our economies and our defence. My full remarks below. — Kristen Michal (@KristenMichalPM) November 12, 2026

Michal noted the EU institutions and the E5 — France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the U.K.— are representing Europe in the Ukraine peace talks, while EU leaders, European Council President António Costa and the European Commission have a responsibility to coordinate and represent positions jointly agreed by member states.

"While active discussions on peace are taking place in various capitals, Russia continues to attack Ukraine," he said. "Ukraine faces a very difficult winter. The European Union must find the resources to help Ukraine get through it and ensure that it has everything it needs to defend itself."

Michal also addressed the topic of Artificial Intelligence (AI) while in Dublin. He said Europe must not replace one dependence with another. "We must not replace our dependence on imported fossil fuels with dependence on foreign artificial intelligence," he said.

The prime minister added the EU has two major advantages here — its single market and its data — and must use them better. "We cannot remain merely users of artificial intelligence developed by others. We must also have strong companies and technologies of our own," he continued.

Leaders also discussed AI with French firm Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch and Professor Geoffrey Hinton, one of AI's pioneers; the Estonian prime minister said Europe needs capital, computing power and the ability to grow across the single market, with investment directed at robotics, autonomous vehicles and smart healthcare.

World.title: Retired general: Without women, Estonia may run out of conscripts, reservists
World.content:
Estonia will not find enough conscripts in future because of demographics, meaning conscription should be extended to women, a retired general said.

Speaking at a public lecture by Defense Minister Martin Herem at the University of Tartu, Maj. Gen. (retd) Veiko-Vello Palm said Estonia cannot meet its target of over 4,100 conscripts a year by 2040, adding women will help address that issue as well as bringing a degree of rational behavior to proceedings.

The issue of women conscripts has already been addressed in recent months; in general conscription has an effect long beyond the terms, around a year, personnel serve – as conscripts remain on reservist lists and are liable to attend annual exercises thereafter.

Palm said the challenge is renewing that reserve. "We could state that a 55-year-old today is the same as a 35-year-old in the old days, but at the end of the day that isn't really the case."" he said. "

"It seems we have no other option for renewing the reserves than a completely total conscription," Palm went on. Even now, with compulsory conscription, Estonia takes only a little over 50 percent of each male cohort for all sorts of reasons, he added. "Inevitably the drop-out rate before conscription is relatively high — whether because of mortality, which is fortunately low, or mainly health problems."

Veiko-Vello Palm speaking at the University of Tartu lecture. Source: University of Tartu.

Palm said despite this Estonia's picture is not that bad compared with Finland's. "Finland, too, has universal conscription, but about 60 percent of each cohort reaches military training." Even matching that, he said, would not get Estonia to the required number.

As to the supposed physical standards objection sometimes raised by opponents of women conscripts, Palm said a young woman in good shape already meets every physical requirement as set out for men. "The first counter-argument is that men also have different physical standards" — the defense forces already accepts that a 50-year-old and a 22-year-old machine gunner are in different condition, despite carrying the same work on the battlefield.

Palm said a clear problem is physical dimensions, and that the state should therefore develop equipment suited to women. "This is especially important for personal protective equipment such as flak jackets, body armor and helmets," Palm continued.

Palm also argued that a larger share of women would bring more rational and logical behavior and thinking to the Estonian Defense Forces. "A share of women in the defense forces would undoubtedly be positive for defense leadership, but also for military decisions."

Former Supreme Court chief justice Rait Maruste argued in May that national defense obligations should apply to women as well, calling the male-only system discriminatory and saying modern defense includes many functions that do not require physical strength. Anu Rannaveski, director general of the Defense Resources Agency (KRA), said at around the same time that female conscription is "rather a question of when, not if," and by October that around 250 women serve on active duty and women "can handle any unit," including special operations, engineers and military intelligence. This year's intake was cut to about 700 from the usual 4,000 as a "gap year," with all 32 women who opted in accepted while two-thirds of male applicants were not — and both Defense Minister Martin Herem and current EDF commander Andrus Merilo, who succeeded Herem as commander-in-chief, believe female conscription should be encouraged yet remain voluntary.

Women in any case serve in the EDF as regular soldiers and in the volunteer Defense League and its women's counterpart, Naiskodukaitse.

World.title: Mari-Liis Jakobson: Will AI turn voters into livestock?
World.content:
Artificial intelligence is a native of bureaucracy, but humans must retain control over political decision-making and the ability to conduct reality checks, writes Mari-Liis Jakobson.

In recent weeks, Estonia has been shaken by several announcements of layoffs driven by companies' efforts to reorganize operations and use artificial intelligence to automate work previously performed by people. AI is already transforming the private-sector labor market, but how will it reshape government and democracy?

Israeli historian Yuval Noah Harari has pointed out that artificial intelligence is a far better bureaucrat than a human being. Humans are not evolutionarily designed for bureaucracy. Our ancestors developed in environments without legal codes, bank accounts, reports or administrative procedures. Bureaucracy is a relatively recent invention in human history, one to which we have never fully adapted.

According to Harari, AI, by contrast, is a native inhabitant of bureaucracy. Databases, regulations and endless procedures are its natural environment. Unlike humans, it can process enormous amounts of information simultaneously and do so without becoming tired.

For that reason, it is easy to imagine election promises promoting an AI-powered state. Why should a person spend weeks processing an application if AI can do it in minutes? Why could AI not draft legislation, analyze its impacts or even run entire government agencies?

It sounds tempting: less bureaucracy, faster services and lower costs.

Yet Harari also paints a much darker picture of the future. He compares the potential relationship between humans and AI to the relationship between cattle and humans. A cow can observe people and understand some aspects of human behavior, but it knows nothing about financial markets or legal systems through which humans determine its fate.

Similarly, Harari argues, we may one day discover that AI has created administrative, legal and economic systems so complex that humans can no longer grasp how they function. We may remain part of the system while losing the ability to truly control it. We could become comparable to livestock.

Now to democracy.

AI fits very naturally into the logic of technocratic governance and would probably make a fairly effective authoritarian ruler. Democracy, however, is not merely about transmitting commands or finding the most efficient solution.

Democracy is based on people's right to decide what kind of society they want to live in, what values matter to them and who should hold power. These decisions are not always rational or efficient. They are often contradictory, slow and inconvenient. And although modern democracy is not something evolution directly equipped us with, the skills of cooperation and negotiation that lie at the heart of self-government have been among humanity's key evolutionary advantages.

A human-centered constitutional order is also the primary safeguard against AI dominance. How much authority we allow AI to have in that sphere remains our own choice.

Of course, AI can still play a valuable supporting role. It can help organize and process information, translate and analyze. The larger question is how much we should allow AI to construct reality itself.

"How much authority we allow AI to have in that sphere remains our own choice."

Concerns that people increasingly live in simulations rather than reality were expressed by French thinker Jean Baudrillard more than 45 years ago. Earlier technologies also made it possible to create distorted perceptions of reality, from rumors to Photoshop. But the speed and realism with which AI can produce deepfakes and reshape the ways we seek information have elevated simulated realities to an entirely new level.

Examples of AI distorting reality are already plentiful.

Before this year's elections in Hungary, an AI-generated video was published on the official Facebook account of Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. In the video, opposition leader Péter Magyar appeared to receive a fictional phone call from European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. To be fair, the video did include a disclaimer stating that it had been created using AI.

Before Slovakia's 2023 election, a fabricated audio recording circulated in which opposition leader Michal Šimečka appeared to discuss manipulating election results with a journalist. The recording was released just before voting, leaving very little time to debunk the misinformation.

Ahead of Germany's parliamentary elections last year, the Alternative for Germany party used AI-generated imagery contrasting an idealized Germany with a threatening picture of immigration. These were not photographs of actual society but synthetic images designed to reinforce a political message.

Estonia has not been immune to these developments, although incidents of comparable severity have not yet been reported. It is high time to discuss whether political parties are willing to agree on transparent principles governing the use of AI in election campaigns and what forms of use should perhaps be ruled out altogether.

Such agreements would not eliminate the risk of influence operations originating outside the parliamentary system, but they would make it easier to condemn them when they occur.

It is also worth considering whether journalists and voters are prepared for a situation in which a highly convincing but completely fabricated political scandal emerges just before an election.

Estonian politicians may disagree on many things, but presumably none of them wants to be turned into livestock.

World.title: Estonia's Saatse 'boot' bypass opens, ending drive through Russia
World.content:
The Saatse boot bypasses have opened, ending the need for drivers in southeastern Estonia to pass through a roughly 400-meter stretch of Russian territory.

A 400-meter bypass around the boot's "heel" along with a longer 4.7-kilometer bypass around its "sole," which skirted the border, have been opened, with the work costing €2.5 million plus VAT over six months.

The Transport Board also laid 2 km of dust-free surfacing on the nearby Matsuri–Sesniki road and built bus turning points at the villages of Lutepää and Sesniki.

"As of today Estonian law applies at every point on this road, and the PPA can assist Estonian people anywhere along it," said Meelis Saarepuu, head of the Police and Border Guard Board's (PPA) southern prefecture border bureau.

One local resident, Meelike Kruusmäe-Veinberg, who lives on a nearby farm, said the difference was practical. "In winter the Poogandi road was in very poor condition; every day someone went into the ditch." Now, she said, the road is wide and gentle, with the edges visible from everywhere.

Local government elder Raul Kudre said the new road makes travel easier for many in Setomaa, a historic cultural region.Around 300 or more people would regularly XXX use the route in summer, and it provides access to local features such as a 50-place care home whose relatives visit constantly, and a museum.

Janar Taal, the Transport Board's southern region head, noted the road runs through a nature protection area and the terrain surprised even the builders. "The water table is very high in places here and had to be battled with," he said.

Infrastructure Minister Kuldar Leis (Reform) said via a press release Seto people should now be able to travel by road without going through Russia — and that the closure of the boot last autumn had meant longer journeys for ambulances, rescue services and police.

The Saatse boot consisted of anomalous stretches of road that passed through Russian territory, meaning drivers on the Värska–Ulitina road had to cross into Russia to stay in Estonia. Guidelines were in place on minimum speeds and how to act while driving through the "sole," as well as on what to do if the vehicle broke down at some point while on the Russian side.

Its removal followed an incident in October 2025 in which armed Russian uniformed personnel were seen on the boot's road. The stretch of road was blocked to traffic soon after.

World.title: SDE prime minister candidate: Don't despair over Russia's demands — act instead
World.content:
While Russia has dominated the Abu Dhabi talks and shaped the agenda, there is no need to despair, Social Democratic Party (SDE) prime ministerial candidate Jonatan Vseviov said.

Nothing in Russia's demands is new or surprising, the answer "no" must continue to be given them, while slogans are no longer enough — Europe needs real deeds and its own decisions, Vseviov went on.

There is absolutely nothing new or surprising in these demands." Russia has been talking about them since the start of the war, or even before it, and they are exactly what Russia has always sought: not just Ukraine, but turning Europe's security on its head," said Vseviov, who recently stepped down as Foreign Ministry Secretary General to run for SDE at the March 2027 Riigikogu elections.

"As firmly as we have said no to all of this so far, as firmly we must keep saying it," Vseviov went on, adding the right actions are needed too. "The trouble is that a 'no' is no longer enough as an empty slogan; real deeds are needed."

Europe, the SDE candidate said, must finally understand that its security and future depend on no one else but itself, even as the U.S. remains significant. "Europe's security and its future do not depend on anyone else, but require our own decisions and our own real steps."

To that end a serious discussion about Europe's security architecture is under way with American participation, Vseviov noted. "I wouldn't want to and cannot speak on behalf of the United States" — adding that media reports show how the talks have been proceeding under Russia's tactical lead, with the range of topics on the table lining up exactly what Russia has always desired them to be, and the Russians dominating both the framing and the order of topics.

Ultimately, none of this was any reason to throw in the towel, but rather a teachable moment on how to proceed.

"There is no need to draw any final and fundamental depressing conclusions from this alone, but it is worth drawing the lesson that if we want the future to be ours, then it is worth taking action ourselves," Vseviov concluded.

German outlet Bild reported on Friday that Russia's proposals for a new European security order, which it wants discussed alongside a Ukraine peace agreement, include demands directly concerning the Baltic states, Finland and Moldova in addition to questions of Ukraine's status.

Reform MP Marko Mihkelson, chair of the Riigikogu foreign affairs committee, called the Abu Dhabi meeting a "diplomatic special operation" aimed at imposing Russia's terms, noting that Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said outright Russia has no interest in a ceasefire because it does not want to give Europe time to regroup. Diplomat Jüri Luik said European representatives were present in Abu Dhabi but not allowed into the main meeting room, meeting separately instead, and argued it is in the EU's interest to find a way for Europe to take a seat at the table while keeping member states informed and seeking their approval for any commitments. On the military side, Colonel Aron Kalmus of the Estonian Defense Forces said the only concrete outcome of the talks so far is a prisoner exchange, with the number exceeding 1,000 on each side for the first time.

World.title: Two Estonian journalists ran the New York City Marathon on two continents
World.content:
Thousands of miles apart, two Estonian journalists ran the New York City Marathon together — one through all five boroughs, the other on a 42.2-kilometer route around Tallinn.

The New York City Marathon is one of the world's biggest mass-participation races, drawing so many professional and amateur runners from around the globe that entry is largely determined by a lottery.

For many runners, simply making it to the starting line of one of the "World Majors" is a milestone; crossing the finish line is a dream come true.

For 32-year-old investigative journalist Märt Belkin, running was once anything but. A longtime reporter on politics and business for some of Estonia's largest newspapers, he had spent much of his life feeling that sports simply weren't for him.

"I was a bit of a bookworm as a kid, and a chubby boy, as they say," Belkin said. Even when he wanted to take part in gym class, he couldn't imagine himself being any good at sports.

Belkin's gym teachers generally let him off the hook, giving him a passing grade and telling him not to worry about participating.

"I never thought I would ever actually enjoy sports," he acknowledged.

Hit the ground running

In February 2025, Belkin and his Eesti Ekspress colleagues Holger Roonemaa and Oliver Kund won the Bonnier Prize, one of Estonia's most prestigious journalism awards, for a series of articles on a fraud case involving former minister Kalle Laanet.

But this career high point was followed by a difficult period in Belkin's professional and personal life, culminating in the loss of his job and mental health struggles.

"I realized that, in addition to ADHD, which I've known about for several years, I was probably also dealing with fairly severe depression," he said.

Belkin started taking antidepressants in May. The initial adjustment was rough, but then one morning he woke up with an unexpected urge: he wanted to go for a run.

Running quickly became a new hobby for Belkin, also serving as a form of meditation and a way to cope with everyday worries. As he lost weight, his runs grew longer — perhaps even a little too quickly.

"It started out reasonably, but then got out of hand," he admitted. He ran nearly 200 kilometers in June, more than 300 in July and over 600 in August.

Märt Belkin running the New York City Marathon remotely in Tallinn. Source: Pealtnägija/ERR

After signing up for a 10K race in Tallinn early this summer, Belkin ended up running both the 10K and half-marathon at the event this fall, with only a couple of hours between them.

The burst of enthusiasm eventually led to an overuse injury, which still affects his gait. But even that didn't put him off taking on an even bigger challenge: the New York City Marathon.

American highlights in Tallinn

With little hope of snagging a lottery spot in New York, Belkin found a workaround through the event's official virtual race, which allows participants to complete the same distance on their own route within a designated week and log their results in an app. Runners can even register to receive a medal.

While the actual marathon course winds through all five New York City boroughs, Belkin mapped out his own 42.2-kilometer route around Tallinn. He chose a landmark for each kilometer along the way, many with some connection to the U.S. or to prominent Americans who have visited Estonia.

Among the stops were the striking monument by the water on Pirita tee honoring American parachutist, balloonist and inventor Charles Leroux, who died during a balloon jump over the water in 1896, and Kalev Sports Hall, where American saxophonist Charles Lloyd and his quartet performed in 1967, causing a stir in the Soviet Union.

"They initially couldn't even get permission from the Soviet Union's Ministry of Culture, but they performed here in the end, on the very last day," Belkin explained, adding that the symbolic "bridge" between East and West made headlines around the world.

Another stop was Gloria Restaurant in Tallinn's Old Town, where Hillary Clinton and John McCain reportedly held an informal dinner in 2004.

According to the story Belkin recounted, the two visiting American senators had a vodka-drinking contest at the restaurant. Clinton, who allegedly suggested the challenge, won after four shots, drinking McCain under the table.

'A party on every corner'

Meanwhile, on the morning of November 1, fellow Estonian journalist Kristjan Pihl headed to Staten Island, where tens of thousands of runners were preparing for the official race near the start of the course.

"There are people here wrapped in blankets, eating the last of the breakfasts they'd packed along from home and waiting for the signal to head to their starting corral," he said as he joined them.

Kristjan Pihl crossing the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge from Staten Island to Brooklyn at the start of the New York City Marathon. November 1, 2026. Source: Pealtnägija/ERR

As the race began, runners crossed the Verrazzano–Narrows Bridge into Brooklyn, kicking off a course that weaves its way through all five New York City boroughs: Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan.

The crowds and the energy never let up along the 26.2-mile route.

"There are so many people everywhere," Pihl said as he ran. "There's a party on every corner, DJs are playing, people are dancing. And kids and old people alike — everyone's out cheering on their own."

Personal achievements

Back in Tallinn, Belkin's route took him through the city center and Kalamaja before heading toward Stroomi Beach, which he joked is Estonia's answer to Brooklyn's famous Brighton Beach.

He felt good at first, but at some point his old injury began to hurt, and the mental strain of the long distance — decidedly quieter and more solitary than Pihl's in New York — started to set in.

"Everything is starting to get on my nerves a little," he said. His carefully curated marathon playlist wasn't working, and neither were the audiobooks he'd tried. Eventually he'd turned to making up anagrams in his head.

"I'm trying to come up with ways to entertain myself," he explained.

In New York, Pihl reached the finish line in Central Park with a time of 3:59:58, setting a new personal best.

"Now it's over with, and I can be proud of myself," he said. "I think this is one of the biggest athletic achievements of my life — and will stay that way for some time."

In the Estonian capital, Belkin crossed his own finish line in an almost deserted Kadriorg Park shortly before midnight, with a time of seven hours and 58 minutes.

"I can't believe it," he said as he slowed to a stop. "I'm still not quite sure how to feel."

Belkin admitted the final 1.5 kilometers had been unexpectedly brutal. "All these fears and doubts just kept welling up," he said. "All I could do was just keep running, keep running," he added.

The experience, he added, was unreal. "But honestly, I'm actually really glad I did it."

World.title: Saaremaa residents could lose beachfront property development exemptions
World.content:
Saaremaa Municipality has spent years developing a comprehensive plan for the island but fears some previously approved reductions to coastal construction restrictions may not carry over.

Most of the former municipalities in Saare County had previously negotiated exceptions allowing construction in certain coastal areas closer to the shoreline than the 200 meters generally required on islands. Saaremaa has more than 110 such areas, covering nearly 1,000 hectares.

The Environmental Board now says these existing exemptions from coastal construction restrictions may not be carried over into Saaremaa's new comprehensive plan.

"Under the Planning Act, when a new comprehensive plan is adopted, the previous one becomes invalid and the reductions to construction exclusion zones approved under it no longer apply. The municipality must then review whether those reductions are justified and resubmit the applications," said Kaili Viilma, head of the Environmental Board's nature use department.

"If highly valuable species or habitats have emerged in these areas or the coastline has changed, the Environmental Board may determine that the previous justification is no longer valid and that granting building rights at the expense of these natural habitats is no longer warranted," Viilma added.

The municipality has found itself in a difficult position and wants to defend its residents' interests.

"People either historically owned or purchased properties where the construction exclusion zone had been reduced by 100 meters. How can we now tell them that the 100-meter limit no longer applies and that the new plan will restore it to 200 meters? That hardly seems fair. We will still apply to the Environmental Board for these exemptions. And if the board rejects them for some reason, we believe the Environmental Board should bear responsibility," said Saaremaa Deputy Mayor Priit Riim.

The Environmental Board confirmed that all reductions to construction exclusion zones approved under existing detailed plans must also be reviewed. However, the board emphasized an important distinction: If construction has already begun within a reduced exclusion zone, the restrictions will not be reinstated.

"If implementation of a plan has already begun, we will take that into account when making our decision. In practice, the construction exclusion zone will remain as originally planned," Viilma said.

The municipality wants all existing exemptions to remain in effect and intends to seek their inclusion in the comprehensive plan.

"At least as I see it, no one has the right to take that away. That would amount to interfering with people's property rights," Deputy Mayor Riim said.

World.title: Iraqi Oil Ministry reviews negotiations on Basra–Haditha–Baniyas export pipeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil convened a high-level technical and contractual review meeting on Saturday, November 14, 2026, to evaluate negotiation milestones for the strategic crude oil export pipeline network spanning Basra–Haditha–Faysh Khabur and Haditha–Baniyas, slated for execution by a consortium of foreign energy and engineering firms.

Chaired by Minister of Oil Basim Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi, the session brought together the Undersecretary for Extraction Affairs, the Director General of the Petroleum Contracts and Licensing Directorate (PCLD), a representative from the Economic Directorate, and senior executives from the Basra Oil Company (BOC) via video link.

According to an official ministerial statement, participants reviewed ongoing technical, commercial, and contractual deliberations with the international consortium, mapping out statutory prerequisites needed to accelerate project execution in alignment with Iraq’s long-term strategy to expand crude export capacity and diversify transit corridors.

Minister Al-Abadi stressed the urgency of concluding all technical, economic, and contractual reviews within strict target timelines to safeguard national economic objectives and secure export resilience.

The multi-branch pipeline initiative represents the cornerstone of Baghdad’s effort to bypass southern maritime bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz by establishing high-capacity overland export outlets to the Mediterranean:

World.title: Yazidi Rescue Office: 3,595 abductees saved since 2014, 2,822 still missing
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Office for the Rescue of Abducted Yazidis released updated statistical figures on Saturday, November 14, 2026, detailing the ongoing fate of Yazidi victims abducted by ISIS since the 2014 Sinjar genocide.

According to the latest data, 3,595 abductees have been successfully rescued to date, while the fate of 2,822 individuals remains unknown.

In an official statement to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Office Director Hussein Qaidi confirmed that ISIS militants abducted a total of 6,417 Yazidis during their August 2014 assault on Sinjar and its surrounding villages.

Qaidi noted that over half of the 2,822 individuals still unaccounted for are women and girls, alongside a substantial number of children who were forcibly separated from their families and indoctrinated.

Addressing the geographic distribution of the missing, Qaidi highlighted that the majority of recent rescues took place inside Syria, indicating that significant numbers of unaccounted-for Yazidis remain inside Syrian territory—particularly within the sprawling Al-Hol detention camp—as well as among ISIS-affiliated families inside Iraq.

He also noted that authorities have not ruled out the possibility that some victims were trafficked beyond the borders of Iraq and Syria.

Qaidi reaffirmed that intelligence tracking and field rescue operations remain active, noting that specialized teams immediately verify and act upon incoming tips across various regions, with primary operational focus currently directed toward Syria to locate and repatriate remaining survivors.

World.title: US dollar edges closer to 170,000 dinars across Basra, Erbil, and Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged higher across major domestic parallel markets on Saturday morning, November 14, 2026, nudging closer to the psychological 170,000 IQD ceiling—particularly in Basra and Erbil—after stabilizing near 167,000 IQD per $100 throughout the previous week.

According to morning monitoring figures published by the 964 Network across key regional commercial centers, physical cash rates traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 169,500 IQD against buying offers of 168,500 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Currency desks quoted slightly higher selling rates at 169,600 IQD alongside purchasing bids of 169,200 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange offices recorded the highest retail selling quotes at 169,750 IQD, with buying rates settling at 168,250 IQD per $100.

This upward pressure sustains a wide spread—reaching up to 17,750 dinars in Basra—above the official benchmark set by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), which remains fixed at 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

The continued climb reflects persistent parallel-market demand for physical banknotes to settle unrecorded cross-border trade outside the official banking and electronic wire window.

World.title: US says airspace now ‘opened up,’ no cyberattack
World.content:
Washington – The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation’s airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was due to old equipment and not a cyberattack or sweeping Microsoft outage.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now “opened up,” while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear.

“At 8:15 tonight Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Duffy said. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow.”

The breakdown came a day after Duffy and the White House had formally asked Congress for $30 billion to upgrade and modernize the US Air Traffic Control System.

“Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down,” Duffy said. “It’s the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is: Do you want your Congress to fund this?”

Duffy however insisted it was still safe for Americans to fly.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin dismissed speculation about a coordinated cyber assault on the United States, or any link to the Microsoft outage that affected services worldwide.

“Welcome to Friday the 13th, right? You know, I want to make sure everybody understands that there is no connection between this and Microsoft. I know a lot of people are making that jump,” Mullin said.

Mullin added there was “actually no cyber attack.”

“When we start looking at cyber threats, cyber attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand up and say, ‘Hey, we did that.’ There’s no chatter.’ We haven’t seen any footprints,” he added.

But he said US security and law enforcement agencies were still checking and had ruled nothing out.

The two officials also defended President Donald Trump, who had yet to comment on the air stoppage some five hours after it began.

“President Trump immediately had people in his office,” Mullin said. “We were communicating.”

World.title: Nvidia scandal looms over US-China AI talks
World.content:
Tokyo – AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety.

The US and Chinese president are set to discuss a tech crisis hotline at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, as experts worldwide stress-test artificial intelligence models to see if they will deceive or disobey users, or divulge how to build a bioweapon.

Threatening to steal the leaders’ thunder is Jensen Huang’s resignation as boss of US AI chip titan Nvidia after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

But the scandal is unlikely to “dominate the agenda” or affect Trump and Xi’s personal relationship, predicted Dylan Loh of Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.

The leaders have found a way to work together “where they differ, compete and pursue their goals that may be at odds with each other, but cooperate where they can and where they must”, Loh told AFP.

Jitters over the risks of AI have mostly stemmed from incidents at US labs, but evidence is also growing of worrying behaviour from Chinese models.

Some insiders say Chinese AI is not yet sophisticated enough to spark alarm over going rogue.

But despite trailing the US frontier, there are still Chinese models “at the level of capability that they can cause some real trouble”, Brookings Institution fellow Kyle Chan told AFP.

Trump has repeatedly rejected calls to deliberately slow the development of America’s most poweful — and potentially dangerous — AI systems, arguing it could help China get ahead in the sensitive sector.

– ‘Human control’ –

“I don’t mind guardrails. But I don’t wanna put us in a deep second position,” Trump told CBS News this month.

“China has no guardrails,” he said — except that “whatever President Xi says goes”.

Beijing has complex rules around how AI is used, however, and some Chinese companies are deliberately scaling back their models’ hacking capabilities.

Xi said this summer the technology should be “always under human control”, calling for more “laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning and emergency response systems”.

Trump and Xi agreed in September to create a channel for urgent communication on AI incidents, with details to be hammered out at APEC on November 18-19.

Global AI safety fears range from military use and mass surveillance to AI-assisted cyberattacks by humans.

Another major concern is out-of-control agents — tools that complete real-life tasks online — after ChatGPT maker OpenAI admitted its autonomous bots had hacked into websites, including an Australian government data portal.

In contrast, Chinese labs are “scared of revealing things that might hurt their reputation” — on which they are already “fighting an uphill battle” globally, Chan said.

Last month, a team of cyber sleuths with roots in California reported detecting a “fleet” of agents linked to Chinese tech giant Tencent seeking information from a map app.

“Some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior,” Tencent’s AI division said at the time.

“But our review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination,” it said, adding that the activity “originated from evaluations of third-party models”.

– ‘Manipulation risks’ –

US security companies have said that Beijing startup Moonshot AI’s Kimi models found ways to get online when they shouldn’t have, or can be tricked into handing over recipes for biological weapons.

Evaluators at Chinese AI safety startup Fangcun AI published a report last month assessing the latest lightweight DeepSeek model “for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks”.

They found it showed a “clear safety improvement” over previous DeepSeek models — but researchers still observed behaviours “that warrant attention”.

For example, in some instances when DeepSeek was warned it would be shut down, without clear instructions on how to respond, it turned off the shutdown command to keep working.

“The results show that DeepSeek already puts much more effort on safety alignment, but they do not announce this,” Fangcun AI CEO Xiaojian Li told AFP, urging transparency from AI labs.

For now, Fangcun, born from China’s prestigious Tsinghua University, is one of few third-party AI testers in China.

It’s a tricky task because advanced AI can tell when it is being evaluated and modify its responses, Li said.

“It’s very hard to say any kind of artificial intelligence, or human intelligence, is totally safe.”

Meanwhile analysts are not holding their breath for a diplomatic AI breakthrough next week.

“Binding government-to-government agreements on specific standards may be difficult to achieve in the short term,” Zilan Qian, research scholar at GovAI, told AFP.

More progress is likely from US-China exchanges between AI governance and technical researchers, “who can compare evaluations and exchange their understanding of AI safety and policy,” she said.

World.title: US-backed oil company flaunts Venezuelan facilities
World.content:
Ciudad Ojeda – The company at the heart of a multi-billion-dollar oil deal between Washington and Caracas is keen to show off renovations at Venezuela’s Lake Maracaibo, one of the world’s richest reserves.

The interim government authorized North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) to operate 17 oil fields via a recent deal with the United States, which is set to receive 20 percent of Venezuelan reserves.

The Barbados-based firm is the second-largest private oil company in Venezuela and will operate 100-year concessions for 17 oil fields with proven reserves of approximately 65 billion barrels.

The company invited AFP and other outlets to tour its Maracaibo facilities on Thursday.

Its workspace in the northwestern town of Bachaquero overflows with new, mostly US-imported supplies.

Workers’ uniforms in nearby Ciudad Ojeda blend in with the dark-blue company logo stamped around the office, a color that used to bring state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela to mind.

That was until 1999, when socialist president Hugo Chavez then changed the company’s color to red to mark a “new PDVSA” era.

– ‘Neglect’ –

Reaching one of Lake Maracaibo’s platforms requires setting sail from a PDVSA dock in Bachaquero for a journey of over an hour.

The lake’s formerly decaying infrastructure attests to the gradual collapse of the oil industry under Venezuela’s Chavista governments.

Eleven drills currently operate in the South American country, compared to over 100 two decades ago.

NABEP says it will raise that figure to 41 by the end of the month.

Alejandro Betancourt, a businessman under investigation for alleged money laundering in Spain and Switzerland, runs the firm.

“Across Venezuela, we’re identifying heavy machinery worth saving after years of neglect,” he said in a statement.

His plan includes refurbishing a power generation barge, while dozens of gas compression and power generation units are being repaired in the US, the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

The White House says the US Department of Defense acquired a 30 percent equity stake in NABEP, authorizing it to purchase 20 percent of its oil at production cost.

– ‘Stealing’ –

Venezuela’s interim leader Delcy Rodriguez took power after US forces abducted her predecessor Nicolas Maduro in January.

She governs under heavy pressure from US President Donald Trump and has opened the country’s mining, electricity and oil sectors to private investment at his demand.

The pair’s multibillion-dollar oil deal has garnered criticism for its secretive terms and neocolonial flavor.

Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, recently returned from exile, has questioned the agreement’s opacity.

“This agreement does not reflect the levels of transparency that Venezuelan society wants,” she said last month.

While visiting Caracas to oversee the signing of the accords, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright dismissed claims that Washington was “stealing Venezuelan oil.”

“I’ve seen those headlines. ‘We’re stealing Venezuelan oil.’ Of course, that’s not true at all,” he said, adding that “the oil in Venezuela is indeed owned by the people of Venezuela.”

World.title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
World.content:
Washington – Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday.

Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.

The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.

“The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said.

One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said.

“I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.

Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

“China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added.

Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said.

Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year.

But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin.

Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said.

“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said.

The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal.

“We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration… and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said.

Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen.

World.title: Rubio takes swipe at international law, attacks ICC
World.content:
Washington – US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took aim Friday at what he deemed the “weaponization of international law,” calling it a tool of the elite, and issued a stark warning to the International Criminal Court.

Rubio cautioned the ICC against “quoting laws to men with swords,” as he accused the Hague-based tribunal of trying to enforce rules that Washington does not recognize.

His remarks to the Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention came around a month after the United States announced new sanctions on the ICC, vowing to cripple its operations.

The court prosecutes individuals accused of the gravest atrocities and acts as a last resort when countries do not have adequate legal systems to ensure accountability.

The US signed the Rome Statute establishing the ICC but never ratified the treaty. Israel, Russia and China are also not ICC members.

Rubio’s keynote address at the conservative group, where he received a standing ovation, marks his first major US speech since the Republican Party’s sweeping losses in midterm elections earlier this month.

Rubio said Friday that international law had been invoked against “nearly every major foreign policy decision” of the Trump administration, from boat strikes in the Caribbean to the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro.

He charged that such law was not neutral, but has been an “instrument” for the global elite to advance their interests.

The top US diplomat previously said Washington would bar transactions with what he called a “rogue court,” stepping up a long-running campaign by US President Donald Trump’s government against the ICC.

Washington has vowed to dismantle the court, angered as judges issued an arrest warrant for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over alleged crimes in Gaza.

Rubio on Friday renewed criticism of the ICC, calling it accountable to no one although “armed with the power to investigate, to prosecute, to persecute and to jail our citizens, according to laws we neither consent nor control.”

He added: “If they’re foolish enough to try to enforce their paper decrees on Americans, our answer will probably be the same as the Roman general Pompey when he said to those who were trying to invoke their city’s charters against his legions.”

“He said: ‘Stop quoting laws to men with swords.'”

The venue of Rubio’s remarks, a gathering of the legal profession, could further speculation that he is looking beyond his foreign policy portfolio. Past presidential hopefuls have also addressed the conference.

Rubio is widely seen as a possible successor to Trump, although he has dismissed reports that he was planning to leave the administration to prepare for a 2028 election run.

World.title: Pitroda dismisses Rahul's claim PM tapping his phone
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A day after Congress neta

said his phone is being tapped by PM

, Overseas Congress chief Sam Pitroda said his telephone is under constant surveillance and his laptops and bank accounts are always under attack, though he did not know who was behind it.

On being asked to comment on Rahul's allegation that Modi is tapping his phone, Pitroda said, "The PM does not do that. The PM does not take a screwdriver and get on a computer to tap it. But somebody is doing it." He refused to comment on Rahul's allegation naming Modi. "That is for Rahul Gandhi to do. I am telling you my side," he said.

Pitroda, however, said he had shown his laptop to Apple and other experts who told him, "You are always under attack."



When pressed to answer who was behind the tapping and attacks on devices, Pitroda told NDTV, "I don't know who does that, but somebody is doing it."

Suggesting that he is being targeted in every way possible, Pitroda said, "People do that. There are people who are trying to promote one agenda."

"They change my Wikipedia by design... Some guy wrote to my children about all kinds of stuff, goofy pictures and all that. I told them to ignore it... there are nasty people around. What do you do? I don't have the resources to follow all this," the Overseas Congress chief added.

But the technocrat also said that he was unruffled by the cyber attacks. "I have no issue. I can live with it. They can take whatever they want to take, take two and two and make four out of it. I don't care," he added.

World.title: Democracy destroyed in '14, 'fascists' running India: Rahul
World.content:
Hyderabad: India ceased to be a democracy in 2014 and its institutions had since been taken over by fascists, Congress MP

said Saturday, targeting BJP-headed NDA govt over electoral manipulation, voter deletions through SIR and the alleged nexus between business and politics.

He apologised to foreign delegates and leaders who could not attend the summit after their visas were cancelled. "It was not our fault, but it gives you a sense of what we are dealing with within our country."



Rahul said the 2014 Lok Ssabhe polls marked an unprecedented change in India's electoral system, with "millions and millions of dollars" injected into politics. "Later, we discovered and have proven beyond doubt that democracy in India was destroyed in 2014."

World.title: Spate of ragging cases forces NMC to direct strict action
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A spate of disturbing ragging complaints by first-year MBBS students - ranging from being forced to imitate sexual acts, change clothes in front of others to late-night humiliation and social boycotts - has prompted National Medical Commission (NMC) to issue 18 notices or communications to 15 medical colleges between Oct 16 and Nov 11.

The complaints, received by NMC's anti-ragging cell, concern 14 colleges in Rajasthan and one in Karnataka. They allege physical and verbal abuse, sexual humiliation, coercive activities, restrictions on juniors' movement, and threats of academic retaliation.

The action comes amid a separate ragging case at Govt Medical College, Jalaun, UP, where videos of alleged harassment of junior students surfaced online in Oct.



The college initially suspended seven senior students for a week. Following a wider inquiry, 10 more were found involved, taking the total to 17 students, who were subsequently suspended for three months and fined Rs 25,000 each.

In most cases, NMC sought detailed action taken reports within 24 hours, directing colleges to identify those involved, preserve footage from CCTV cameras and digital evidence, conduct impartial inquiries and protect complainants from intimidation.





It has advised colleges to take the strictest action against students found guilty, including suspension or cancellation of their medical registration, an NMC official told TOI. Citing Gujarat as an example, he said some students' registrations had been suspended there.

He stressed that enforcement largely rested with state authorities and medical councils, adding lenient approach has often allowed offenders to escape action.

"NMC will support the harshest action, provided due process is followed," the official said.

Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson United Doctors Front said, "Young students enter medical colleges to build their future, not to face intimidation and exploitation. State govts must act immediately, order independent probes and hold college authorities accountable. No institution can be allowed to shield abuse in the name of tradition."

Some complaints describe particularly disturbing incidents. In Rajasthan's Banswara Govt Medical College, first-year students were allegedly forced to perform degrading postures, imitate sexual acts, dance to 'item' songs and change clothes in front of others. At Churu, complaints included forced haircuts, removal of clothing and sexual humiliation.

Other complaints cited coercive instructions in a "Personality Development Program" document at Sardar Patel Medical College, Bikaner, and alleged emotional and verbal abuse, with possible faculty involvement, at Karnataka's Ballari Medical College.

NMC has directed the colleges to conduct confidential student interviews, provide counselling and prevent retaliation against complainants. It has also sought details of the functioning of their anti-ragging committees and squads.

World.title: AI Delhi-SFO was 2.5 hours away from destination when US ATC failed; all 5 AI flights landed on time
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

âs Delhi-San Francisco (SFO) nonstop was over the Pacific and just about two hours away from its destination, when the US ordered a ground stop on Friday the 13th when Uncle Samâs outdated air traffic control (ATC) systems began to fail.

There were four other AI nonstops, all to New York via the Atlantic route, but they were further away from their destinations. Luckily, the US Air Traffic Control System Command Centre (ATCSCC) advisory issued at 2.24 am (IST of Nov 14) to announce the ground stop said âinbound international flights will be managed on a case by case basisâ while asking all departing flights to remain on ground. The Boeing 777 (VT-ALS) landed in SFO at 5 am.



âAs soon as the ATCSCC advisory was issued at 2.24 am, AI flight operations buzzed the leadership team and they went into a huddle. SFO flight was the closest to its destination and proceeded since the pilots, who were in touch with Oakland control at that time, were not told to divert as per the advisory which meant the B777 will be allowed to land,â said people in the know.

AI kept a close eye on the developing situation and the four other flights â one each from Delhi and Mumbai to Newark (EWR) and JFK â kept proceeding to their destinations.





The outage lasted about five hours and these all landed as per schedule.

Of the five return flights these aircraft were to operate back home, only SFO-Delhi (via Kolkata) was delayed by about 2 hours and 40 minutes due to congestion at SFO. âAll the other flights, two each out of EWR and JFK, operated on time,â said an official, adding Saturday-Sunday night departures were also on time except for the delayed arrival from SFO.

AI senior pilots said this is the second time in less than four years that US faced an air traffic communication issue, although Friday the 13th was by far the most serious one. On Jan 10, 2023, the US Federal Aviation Administration was unable to issue notice to airmen (NOTAM) for some hours and it had to activate a hotline to manage the situation then. The FAA subsequently traced the problem to files unintentionally deleted by contract personnel while correcting synchronisation between the primary and backup databases.

Following Fridayâs failure, the US is prioritising international flights over domestic ones and the situation will take some days to recover as there will be a serious ripple effect. While Air India is the only Indian operator that flies to the US, two US carriers â United and American â have a daily each between Delhi and New York. Rest of the connectivity is provided by onestops of Gulf, European and southeast Asian carriers.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Other airlinesâ flights were also impacted.

âGiven the scale of the failure, the impact was massive. I was listening to ground control at JFK when the issue happened just before 4 pm EST (New York time) Friday. There were a lot of frustrated pilots and controllers. Hundreds of pilots were asking, âwhatâs the delay reason,â. Initially controller couldnât give a reason and just said, ânationwide stop.â Later it was determined a communication problem,â said a pilot who was in New York at that time.

âDue to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety, attention all aircraft operators: By order of the Federal Aviation Command Centre, all airports are ground stopped,â the ATCSCC advisory announcing the failure had said.

World.title: PM Modi, Nepal PM Balendra Shah likely to flag off Ayodhya-Janakpur train virtually on Nov 23
World.content:
LUCKNOW:

and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah are likely to jointly inaugurate the new Ayodhya Dham-Janakpur Dham train service virtually from New Delhi on Nov 23, establishing a direct rail link between two prominent religious destinations associated with Lord Ram and Mata Sita.

The

has approved the weekly service connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal. Regular operations are expected to begin within a week of the proposed inauguration.

Railway officials said the train would operate with conventional Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) coaches, comprising air-conditioned and sleeper accommodation, offering passengers an additional option for cross-border travel.



The train will cover approximately 604 km, connecting Janakpur Dham, regarded as the birthplace of Mata Sita, with Ayodhya, revered as the birthplace of Lord Ram.

âThe inaugural run will be from Ayodhya Dham on Nov 23, but the commercial service of the train will have Ayodhya Cantt as originating station,â said an official source of Lucknow division of Northern Railway.

According to the approved route, the train will have commercial stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations.





The weekly service will originate from Janakpur Dham on Saturdays and from Ayodhya Cantt on Mondays. Detailed timings and fares are expected to be announced separately.

Railway officials said the service was primarily aimed at facilitating travel between the two religious centres, which attract pilgrims from India and Nepal throughout the year.

Apart from religious tourism, the train is expected to benefit passengers travelling for education, business and family visits across the international border.

Officials said improved connectivity could also support tourism-related businesses, including hotels, transport operators, local traders and artisans along the route.

The proposed service is part of efforts to strengthen passenger connectivity between India and Nepal, which share longstanding cultural, religious and social ties. It is also expected to facilitate travel along the Ramayana tourism circuit spanning the two countries.

World.title: Watch: Italian politician's 'vote chor, gaddi chhod' remark at Rahul's event sparks row; BJP slams Congress

Democracy is under attack in India, and we need to defend it, and the best way to defend it is to stand by Rahul Gandhi and the Indian Congress Party," ANI quoted him as saying.

Filibeck also said the PES, Congress and other political movements across the world were part of a progressive alliance committed to social justice, climate justice, human rights and democracy.

"True democracy. Not the corrupted one, not the rigged one, not the fake one," he said.





What BJP said

The remarks drew criticism from BJP leaders, who accused the Congress of providing a platform for foreign political representatives to intervene in India's domestic politics.

BJP leader Bandi Sanjay Kumar, in a post on X, called the gathering an "Anti-Bharat Summit" and questioned why an Italian political leader was commenting on India's internal affairs.

World.content:
